issues.title: warn when a coding agent commits in an enabled repo but no session is being recorded
issues.body:
### Problem or use case

an enabled repo can silently accept agent-driven commits while recording nothing. entire's git hooks run on every commit, in the right repo, with settings loaded, and when they find no session they log a debug line (`manual_commit_hooks.go:414`) and move on. the user finds out much later, when they go looking for a session that was never recorded. i'd like to propose that this combination becomes a warning instead.

how i got here: i ran a long claude code session against this repo. it created a worktree, wrote a fix, committed twice, opened a pr. days later i wanted to look back at the session:

```
~/W/o/e/c/fix-checkpoint-metadata-bloat> entire checkpoint list
  branch       fix-checkpoint-metadata-bloat
  checkpoints  0
```

nothing on the branch and nothing in the web ui. the mistake was mine: i use a bare-clone worktree layout (a parent folder holding `.bare/` plus one directory per worktree) and i started the agent in the parent folder instead of inside a worktree. agents read their repo-level config from the directory the session starts in, and that's where entire's hooks live (`.claude/settings.json` in my case, and the equivalent checked-in files for the other integrations). the parent folder has none, so no agent hook ever fired. the folder doesn't feel wrong either: its `.git` file points at the bare gitdir, so git commands work, branches resolve, commits succeed.

but the specific mistake matters less than the shape of it. "agent committing, nothing recorded" is reachable many ways:

- the agent session started outside the worktree (my case, and possible with any integrated agent, and from any directory above a normal repo)
- the hooks are registered but the binary they invoke fails at startup (i also had a second, older `entire` on my path that can't parse this repo's current settings schema; every hook invocation through it would die silently)
- the hooks were removed or drifted out of the agent's settings file
- session state was wiped mid-conversation with `entire clean`

no one warning can name the cause, and it doesn't need to. the commit is the anchor: at that moment the git hook already has everything needed to notice. entire is enabled in the worktree. the commit is agent-driven (claude code sets `CLAUDECODE=1` in the environment of every command it runs, verified, and it also sets `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, so the warning could even name the unrecorded session; the `interactive` package already reads `GEMINI_CLI`, `COPILOT_CLI` and `PI_CODING_AGENT` as agent markers for tty detection; markers for the remaining integrations would need to be verified per agent). and no session anywhere in the repo has seen recent activity.

### Desired behavior

```
$ git commit -m "fix: ..."
[entire] a coding agent is committing but no session is being recorded.
did the agent session start outside this worktree? run 'entire doctor' to check.

$ entire doctor          # run from the layout root
  ✗ you're at the root of a bare-clone worktree layout, not inside a worktree.
    entire is enabled in 3 worktrees below this directory:
      main/  fix-a/  fix-b/
    agent sessions started here are not recorded. start them inside a worktree.
```

a nice property of the git-hook route: hook stderr goes to whatever process ran `git commit`, which is the agent itself, so the warning lands in the agent's transcript and the agent can pass it on to the user immediately.

### Proposed solution

**warn when:** settings are enabled, an agent env marker is present, and no session anywhere in the repo shows recent activity (session state carries `LastInteractionTime`, so "recent" is a cheap check against a live window rather than a guess). cause-agnostic on purpose: it catches every path into "nothing recorded" without having to detect any of them specifically. rate-limited the way `warnStaleEndedSessions` already does it (sentinel file mtime in the session-state dir, fail-open), once per worktree until a live session appears.

a note on why the condition is "no recently active session" rather than the more obvious "no session state files at all": ended sessions deliberately leave their state files behind (they're kept for amend-trailer restoration), and stray files accumulate in long-lived repos. i checked my own repo while writing this: `.git/entire-sessions/` contains leftover state from months ago, so a zero-files condition would never fire anywhere a session has ever run. recency is the version of the signal that keeps working after the first week.

**stay quiet when:** a session is recently active somewhere in the repo, even if not in this worktree. that shape is usually deliberate (task fan-out into fresh worktrees, review in isolated worktrees, an agent cd-ing between checkouts), the driving session is alive and recording in its own worktree, and `entire session adopt` already covers moving it. warning here would mostly nag power users.

**supporting pieces:**

- the env markers could live in the agent registry, next to the per-agent facts each integration already declares (protected dirs, transcript layout). the hook checks the union over registered agents instead of a hardcoded list, each integration verifies its own agent's marker, and new integrations get detection for free.
- `entire doctor` could learn to diagnose the most common cause. detection: cwd `.git` is a file pointing at a bare gitdir, registered worktrees are children of cwd, and at least one of them has entire enabled while cwd has none. output: the message shown above, listing the enabled worktrees by name so the fix is a visible `cd`. no auto-fix on purpose: writing agent config at the layout root would be wrong (there's nothing to record against) and would teach the wrong habit. doctor's existing wiring checks (`checkClaudeCodeHookDrift`) already help with the hook-drift causes.
- these two land together or not at all: the warning's "run `entire doctor`" hint is only honest once doctor can actually recognize the situation. today doctor reports a healthy worktree (correctly, the worktree's wiring is fine) and has no concept of the layout root.

**edge cases i thought about:**

- human commits with no agent env never warn.
- a human committing from a shell that inherited an agent marker gets misread once, then the rate limit caps it.
- someone deliberately running an untracked agent in an enabled repo eats one line, and a settings switch (`warnings.unrecorded_agent_commit: false` or similar) turns it off for good.
- agents without a verified marker are missed, which is the status quo; registry-driven detection makes each fix a one-liner in the integration.
- there's no race with the first commit of a healthy session: session state is written at session start (`lifecycle.go` initializes it on the session-start event), before the agent can run anything, so if hooks fired at all a recently-active session exists. its absence is exactly the signal.
- a human committing by hand while no agent has run recently, in a repo with an agent marker leaked into the shell: the worst-case false positive, one line, once, suppressible.

happy to take this if the shape sounds right, and equally happy if you'd rather solve it differently.

### Alternatives or workarounds

- discipline: always `cd` into a worktree before starting the agent. works until it doesn't, which is how i got here.
- running `entire doctor` proactively from inside a worktree confirms the wiring, though it reports healthy in this scenario, and in practice you only run doctor once you already suspect something.
- `entire import` (experimental) can backfill the lost session from the agent's own transcript after the fact, which recovers the data but not the moment the warning was needed.

issues.title: Checkpoint duplicated when a session-end hook is killed between the v1 write and the state save
issues.body:
A session-end hook killed part-way through can leave a checkpoint committed to `entire/checkpoints/v1` whose session bookkeeping never advanced, so PostCommit later writes a **second** checkpoint covering the same transcript range.

Found by an agent review on [trail #1001](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1001) (finding `01M0A84AHZ7F`) while reviewing #1940, and verified against the code. Filed as a follow-up because the durable fix changes the condensation path, which did not belong in a session-cleanup PR.

### The window

`CondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed` runs the condense *inside* the `MutateSessionState` callback (`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_condensation.go:1350`), and `MutateSessionState` persists the state only after that callback returns (`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/session_state.go:563`). The checkpoint, however, is committed to v1 partway through the callback, at `manual_commit_condensation.go:434`.

Kill the process between those two points and:

- the checkpoint is durable on `entire/checkpoints/v1`
- `CheckpointTranscriptStart`, `LastCheckpointID`, `StepCount` and `FullyCondensed` are all unchanged on disk

so the next PostCommit mints a fresh checkpoint ID over a transcript range that already has one.

The other kill windows are fine, which is what makes this one worth fixing rather than absorbing: before `markSessionEnded` the exited-owner sweep reclaims the session, and before `store.Write` nothing durable happened so the existing fail-open retry is correct.

### Who can hit it

Any agent whose host kills the hook. Today that is Codex, which runs `SessionEnd` inside its shutdown under a hard 3s `SESSION_END_MAX_TIMEOUT_SEC` and terminates the hook's whole process tree on expiry. #1940 widened Entire's self-imposed budget to 2s and pinned ≥1s of headroom for wrapper and binary startup, which makes overrunning much less likely — but a budget only narrows the race, it cannot close it. A SIGKILL, a laptop suspend, or an OOM kill lands in the same window.

No data is lost in any case, and the flock is OS-advisory so a killed hook cannot wedge later sessions. The cost is duplication.

### Fix

Make the v1 write and the state save one recoverable unit, so a retry after a kill cannot duplicate. Roughly, either:

1. persist the advanced bookkeeping (at minimum `LastCheckpointID` and `CheckpointTranscriptStart`) before or atomically with the v1 write, so a retry recognises the range as already covered; or
2. make PostCommit idempotent against an existing checkpoint for the same transcript range, and reconcile rather than mint.

### Also worth answering

- **Do `tokens profile` / `checkpoint list` double-count an overlapping pair?** If they do, the user-visible symptom is inflated token totals, not just a redundant checkpoint.
- **Does Codex send SIGTERM or SIGKILL on expiry?** On SIGTERM, `cmd/entire/main.go:47` prints `Received termination signal, shutting down… signal again to force quit.` to stderr, which would surface on the user's terminal during Codex's own shutdown. The cancellation itself is the graceful path; the message is the problem.

issues.title: Checkpoint metadata.json exceeds GitHub's 100 MB limit: files_touched is never deduplicated, and nested git worktrees are walked
issues.body:
## Summary

On a repo that uses git worktrees, `entire/checkpoints/v1` grows a
`metadata.json` large enough that GitHub refuses the push outright. Once that
happens the checkpoint branch can never be pushed again without rewriting its
history, and the failure surfaces only as a warning attached to an unrelated
`git push`.

Two separate causes compound. Either one alone would be survivable.

## Symptom

Every `git push` in the host repo now ends with:

```
[entire] Warning: failed to push entire/checkpoints/v1 after sync: push failed:
remote: error: File 53/596dc8fea0/1/metadata.json is 111.79 MB; this exceeds
GitHub's file size limit of 100.00 MB
remote: error: GH001: Large files detected.
! refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1 -> [remote rejected] (pre-receive hook declined)
```

The user's own branches push fine, so this is easy to miss for a long time —
it reads as noise attached to a successful push.

Environment: Entire CLI 0.8.42, go1.26.4, darwin/arm64.

## Cause 1 — `files_touched` is appended to, never deduplicated

That `metadata.json` is a single checkpoint record with
`"checkpoints_count": 213`. Measured on the blob:

| | |
|---|---|
| file size | 111.79 MB |
| lines | 1,292,267 |
| `files_touched` entries | 1,292,257 |
| **unique** entries | **67,340** |
| `files_touched` share of the file | 105.6 MB of 111.79 MB (94%) |

A 19× duplication factor. No single path dominates — the most repeated one
appears 77 times — so this is broad re-appending across checkpoints rather than
one pathological entry. Deduplicating alone takes the file to roughly 5.5 MB
and puts it back under the limit.

## Cause 2 — nested git worktrees are walked as if they were project files

Of the 67,340 unique paths, broken down by top-level segment:

| prefix | unique paths |
|---|---|
| `.claude/` (agent worktrees live here) | 43,184 |
| `worktrees/` | 21,833 |
| the actual project | ~1,241 |

96% of what is being recorded lives inside *other git checkouts* nested under
the repo root. Linked worktrees have their own `.git` and their own history;
their contents are not changes to the host repo. `node_modules` is correctly
excluded, so the walker already has an ignore mechanism — nested worktrees just
aren't in it.

This is the part that makes the growth unbounded in practice. Anyone driving
parallel coding agents accumulates worktrees, and each one multiplies the
recorded set.

## Scale of the resulting branch

| | |
|---|---|
| commits on `entire/checkpoints/v1` | 8,842 |
| files | 32,799 |
| unique blob bytes | 1,336.9 MB |
| distinct blobs over 50 MB | 3 |

Many identical 50 MB `full.jsonl` blobs exist, but git dedupes those by hash,
so they cost storage once. The 111.79 MB `metadata.json` is the only blob that
actually blocks the push.

## Suggested fixes, in order of leverage

1. **Deduplicate `files_touched` before writing.** One line, ~19× smaller, no
   behaviour change — the array is a set in everything but type.
2. **Do not descend into nested git worktrees.** A directory containing a
   `.git` entry that is not the repo root is a separate checkout. This is where
   the remaining ~50× lives.
3. **Store `files_touched` as a newline-delimited sidecar** rather than inline
   in a JSON object. It streams, it chunks, and it stops one growing field from
   deciding whether the whole record is writable.
4. **Check size before pushing and fail loudly.** A blob over the remote's
   limit is unrecoverable once committed; catching it at write time is cheap,
   and catching it at push time is too late. The current warning is easy to
   scroll past.

Fix 1 is the emergency stop. Fix 2 is the actual bug. Fixes 3 and 4 are what
stop the next version of this.

## Offer

Happy to send a PR for 1 and 2 — they look self-contained and the repo has CI
in `test.yml`. Say which shape you'd prefer for 2 (skip any dir containing
`.git`, versus consulting `git worktree list`), since that's a design call
rather than a mechanical one. I can also supply the checkpoint that triggered
this if a reproduction is useful, though it is 111 MB.

Disclosure: this report was researched and written with AI assistance
(Claude Code). Every number above is measured from the actual blob with
`git cat-file`, not estimated.
issues.display_title: Checkpoint metadata.json exceeds GitHub's 100 MB limit: files_touched is never deduplicated, and nested git worktrees are walked

issues.title: PRD: Restructure CLI commands into noun groups (session/checkpoint/agent/doctor)
issues.body:
## Problem Statement

The Entire CLI has accumulated 17 visible top-level commands plus a handful of hidden ones. Users hit several problems:

- `entire --help` reads as a wall of verbs with no grouping. Discoverability suffers — useful commands like `attach`, `resume`, `rewind`, `explain`, and `trace` sit at the same depth as repo lifecycle commands like `enable`/`disable`/`status`.
- The naming verb-first instead of noun-verb diverges from the conventions users already know (`git`, `kubectl`, `gh`, `docker`). When a user thinks "I want to inspect a checkpoint", they look for a `checkpoint` noun and find none.
- `entire configure` is a vague catch-all that mixes interactive setup with agent CRUD via flags (`--agent`, `--remove`). The agent-management surface is buried in flag descriptions instead of being a first-class set of subcommands.
- `entire reset` overlaps with `entire clean` and is confusingly hidden.
- `entire search` is implemented but hidden, leaving useful checkpoint search undiscoverable.
- Several commonly needed troubleshooting capabilities are missing: there is no way to show the active session for the current directory, no direct viewer for a checkpoint by ID (it requires `explain --checkpoint <id>`), no way to diff two checkpoints, no way to tail the operational logs, and no way to produce a self-contained diagnostic bundle for bug reports.
- The existing `explain` command does three different jobs (list checkpoints on a branch, show a single checkpoint, show a session) routed through flags, which makes its own `--help` hard to scan and reason about.

## Solution

Reorganize the command surface around four noun groups — `session`, `checkpoint`, `agent`, `doctor` — promote the troubleshooting capabilities to first-class subcommands, and fold overlapping verbs together. Keep the most common top-level verbs (`rewind`, `resume`, `attach`, `explain`, `trace`, `search`) as silent permanent aliases so existing muscle memory and documentation continue to work.

The change is rolled out in three phases. Phase 1 (this PRD) introduces the new structure entirely additively: every existing invocation continues to work unchanged, and the deprecated aliases (`configure`, `reset`) print a one-time stderr warning. Phase 2 (a later release) adds deprecation warnings to additional renamed top-levels if needed. Phase 3 (a future major release) hides the deprecated aliases.

The final shape:

```
entire
├── enable
├── disable
├── status
├── login / logout
├── activity
├── dispatch
├── agent                             # was: configure
│   ├── list
│   ├── add <name>
│   └── remove <name>
├── session                           # alias: sessions
│   ├── list
│   ├── info <id> [--json]
│   ├── stop [id]
│   ├── attach <id>
│   ├── resume <branch>
│   └── current                       # NEW
├── checkpoint                        # aliases: cp, checkpoints
│   ├── list                          # NEW (was: explain default)
│   ├── show <id> [--short|--full|--raw|--generate]
│   ├── rewind [--to|--list|--logs-only|--reset]
│   ├── search [query]                # unhidden
│   └── diff <a> <b>                  # NEW
├── doctor                            # default: scan + fix
│   ├── trace
│   ├── logs [--tail|--follow]        # NEW
│   └── bundle                        # NEW
├── clean [--shadow]                  # absorbs `reset`
├── help / version
└── hidden: hooks, migrate, trail, configure (warn), reset (warn), …
```

Permanent silent top-level aliases:

| Alias | Resolves to |
|-------|-------------|
| `entire rewind` | `entire checkpoint rewind` |
| `entire resume` | `entire session resume` |
| `entire attach` | `entire session attach` |
| `entire explain` | `entire checkpoint show` (smart-route between checkpoint-id, commit-sha, session-id) |
| `entire trace` | `entire doctor trace` |
| `entire search` | `entire checkpoint search` (hidden alias) |
| `entire sessions` | `entire session` (Cobra alias) |

Deprecated aliases with one-time stderr warning:

| Alias | Resolves to |
|-------|-------------|
| `entire configure` | `entire agent` (interactive picker) |
| `entire configure --agent <x>` | `entire agent add <x>` |
| `entire configure --remove <x>` | `entire agent remove <x>` |
| `entire reset` | `entire clean --shadow` |

## User Stories

1. As a CLI user new to Entire, I want `entire --help` to fit in a screen and clearly group commands by domain, so that I can discover commands without scrolling.
2. As a CLI user familiar with `git`/`kubectl`/`gh`, I want a noun-verb structure so the CLI feels predictable and matches my muscle memory.
3. As a developer who frequently uses `entire rewind`, I want my existing one-word invocation to keep working forever, so that I do not have to retrain my muscle memory.
4. As a developer using `entire resume <branch>` and `entire attach <id>`, I want those one-word forms preserved as silent aliases of the new `session` subcommands, so that scripts and personal docs do not break.
5. As a developer who uses `entire explain <commit-sha>`, I want the smart-routing behavior preserved so a sha resolves to the underlying checkpoint and an id resolves to a checkpoint show.
6. As a CLI user managing AI agent integrations, I want to run `entire agent list` to see which agents are integrated in this repo, so that I do not have to read settings JSON.
7. As a CLI user adding an agent, I want `entire agent add claude-code` to be the canonical command, so that the action is self-documenting.
8. As a CLI user removing an agent, I want `entire agent remove claude-code` instead of `entire configure --remove claude-code`, so that the verb matches the intent.
9. As a CLI user running `entire configure` out of habit, I want the command to keep working with a single deprecation warning pointing me to `entire agent`, so that I have time to update my habits.
10. As a CLI user, I want `entire enable` to remain a focused on/off switch and not also handle agent CRUD, so that the lifecycle of the integration is easy to reason about.
11. As a developer debugging a session issue, I want `entire session current` to tell me which session is writing checkpoints in this directory right now, so that I do not have to guess from `sessions list`.
12. As a developer reviewing a checkpoint by ID, I want `entire checkpoint show <id>` to be a direct command instead of `entire explain --checkpoint <id>`, so that I do not have to remember a flag.
13. As a developer reviewing the recent activity on a branch, I want `entire checkpoint list` (the new default) to give me the previous `entire explain` no-arg behavior, so the most common view stays available.
14. As a developer comparing two points in a session, I want `entire checkpoint diff <a> <b>` so I can see the delta in files-touched, tokens, and transcripts between two checkpoints.
15. As a developer searching for a past checkpoint, I want `entire checkpoint search "fix login"` to be discoverable in `--help` instead of hidden, because the underlying capability is already implemented.
16. As a developer with a stale shadow branch, I want a single `entire clean --shadow` that does what `entire reset` used to do, so that there is one canonical "clean up state" command.
17. As a developer who learned `entire reset`, I want it to keep working with a deprecation warning, so I can migrate at my own pace.
18. As a developer triaging a hook failure, I want `entire doctor logs` to tail `.entire/logs/` instead of having to remember the path, so that I can see operational output quickly.
19. As a developer who needs to keep watching the logs while reproducing an issue, I want `entire doctor logs --follow` to behave like `tail -f`, so I can iterate without restarting the command.
20. As a developer reporting a bug, I want `entire doctor bundle` to produce a single zip of logs + settings + git snapshot, so that I can attach it to an issue without manual copy-pasting.
21. As a maintainer reviewing bug reports, I want users to be able to attach a deterministic diagnostic bundle, so that I have consistent context across reports.
22. As a developer, I want `entire doctor` (no args) to remain the existing scan-and-fix command, so that the most common usage stays unchanged.
23. As a developer, I want `entire doctor trace` to be the new home for the existing `entire trace` command, while the top-level `entire trace` keeps working silently.
24. As a developer, I want `entire sessions` (plural) to be a Cobra alias of `entire session`, so that I can use whichever form feels natural.
25. As a CLI maintainer, I want every Phase 1 change to be additive so that no user-visible invocation breaks at release time.
26. As a CLI maintainer, I want deprecation warnings to print only once per process so that scripts running many subcommands do not spam stderr.
27. As a CLI maintainer, I want the new noun groups to be wired through small, testable modules (agent CRUD, checkpoint view, checkpoint diff, alias factory, deprecation warner) so that group commands are thin Cobra wrappers around tested cores.
28. As a CLI maintainer, I want the `agent` package to be Cobra-free so that its CRUD logic is reusable and testable in isolation.
29. As a CLI maintainer, I want `checkpointview` to be Cobra-free so that the formatting logic for `checkpoint list`, `checkpoint show`, and the `explain` alias is shared and golden-tested.
30. As a CLI maintainer, I want one alias factory used by all seven silent aliases and both deprecated aliases, so that alias behavior is consistent and rare bugs are fixed in one place.
31. As a developer reading `CLAUDE.md`, I want the Key Directories section updated to reflect the new noun groups, so that contributors understand the layout.
32. As a CLI user using accessibility mode, I want every new interactive picker (e.g. the `agent` no-arg picker) to honor `ACCESSIBLE=1`, so that the new structure does not regress accessibility.

## Implementation Decisions

### Modules to build

- **`agent` package (new)** — Cobra-free CRUD over agent integrations: `Add(ctx, name)`, `Remove(ctx, name)`, `List(ctx)`. Lifts logic out of the existing `setup.go` flows. Becomes the core powering `entire agent add|remove|list`, the deprecated `configure` alias, and the existing `enable` first-run bootstrap.
- **`checkpointview` package (new)** — Cobra-free list/show formatters with selectable verbosity (short, full, raw, default-detailed) and intent/summary generation. Lifted from `explain.go`. Backs `checkpoint list`, `checkpoint show`, and the `explain` top-level alias.
- **`checkpointdiff` package (new)** — Cobra-free diff over two checkpoint identifiers. Reads checkpoint trees via the existing `checkpoint.GitStore`. Returns a structured diff (file-touched delta, token delta, transcript delta) plus a renderer.
- **`doctorlogs` module (new)** — Reads `.entire/logs/`, supports `--tail N` (default last N lines) and `--follow` (polling, no fsnotify dependency).
- **`doctorbundle` module (new)** — Produces a zip containing the logs directory, current settings (project + local), `git status` / `git log -n 50` / `git remote -v` snapshot, CLI version, and Go runtime info. Returns the path to the produced archive.
- **`alias` helper (new, single file)** — `aliasOf(child *cobra.Command, opts ...AliasOption) *cobra.Command` produces a thin top-level Cobra command that delegates to the child's `RunE` while preserving args, flags, and exit codes. Optional `WithDeprecation(replacement string)` triggers a once-per-process stderr warning.
- **`deprecation` helper (new)** — `WarnOnce(cmd, replacement)` emits a single stderr line per process (guarded by a `sync.Once`).

### Modules to modify

- **`cmd/entire/cli/root.go`** — Stops registering the now-grouped commands at the root. Adds four new group roots (`session`, `checkpoint`, `agent`, `doctor`). Registers all silent aliases via the `alias` helper. Registers `configure` and `reset` as deprecated aliases.
- **`cmd/entire/cli/setup.go`** — Carves agent CRUD out into the new `agent` package. `enable` / `disable` stay; their bodies become thinner, focused on state toggle and first-run bootstrap.
- **`cmd/entire/cli/clean.go`** — Adds `--shadow` flag whose handler calls into the existing `manual_commit_reset` logic from the strategy package, replacing the hidden `reset` command.
- **`cmd/entire/cli/explain.go`** — Decomposed into `checkpoint_list.go`, `checkpoint_show.go`, and a slim alias wrapper that preserves the smart-routing between checkpoint id, commit sha, and session id. Shared formatting moves into the `checkpointview` package.
- **`cmd/entire/cli/sessions.go`** — Renamed/restructured to register children under a `session` parent. Adds `attach`, `resume`, and `current` as session subcommands. The plural `sessions` form remains as a Cobra alias on the parent.
- **`cmd/entire/cli/trace_cmd.go`** — Becomes a child of the `doctor` group; the existing top-level form remains as a silent alias.
- **`cmd/entire/cli/search_cmd.go`** — Becomes a child of the `checkpoint` group; the top-level form stays registered but hidden as an alias.

### Architectural decisions

- **Silent aliases** are produced by the `alias` helper to avoid duplicating Cobra command construction; they reuse the child's `RunE` directly, so behavior cannot drift.
- **Deprecated aliases** print exactly one warning per process, regardless of how many times the alias is invoked or recursed into.
- **No settings/feature flag** gates the rollout — Phase 1 is purely additive, so a runtime gate would add complexity without value.
- **`doctor` is both a runnable command and a parent**: bare `entire doctor` runs the existing scan-and-fix flow, while `entire doctor trace|logs|bundle` are subcommands.
- **Accessibility**: any new interactive picker (the `agent` group's no-arg flow) uses `NewAccessibleForm` per the existing convention.
- **Hidden infrastructure commands** (`hooks`, `git-hook`, `migrate`, `__send_analytics`, `curl-bash-post-install`, `trail`) are unchanged.
- **CLAUDE.md** is updated to document the new groups and the `agent`, `checkpointview`, and `checkpointdiff` packages under "Key Directories". The "Code Patterns" section gains a brief note describing the alias and deprecation helpers.

### API contracts

- The deprecation warning format is fixed: `Warning: 'entire <old>' is deprecated; use 'entire <new>' instead.` printed to stderr, exit code unchanged.
- `entire doctor bundle` writes its archive to a deterministic path under the OS temp directory and prints that path to stdout (so it is shell-pipeable).
- `entire doctor logs --follow` exits cleanly on SIGINT.
- `entire checkpoint diff <a> <b>` accepts checkpoint IDs (12-hex prefix accepted) and returns a non-zero exit code only on lookup failure, not on a non-empty diff.

### Out-of-band changes

- Update getting-started docs and `gettingStarted` constant in `root.go` to reference `entire enable` (already canonical) and remove any lingering `entire configure` references where appropriate, while keeping the deprecation alias functional.

## Testing Decisions

A good test exercises external behavior: command-line invocation, output, exit code, and observable state changes (files written, settings updated, archives produced). Tests should not assert on Cobra internals or pin specific log strings unless those strings are part of the user contract. Tests prefer `testutil.InitRepo` over raw `git.PlainInit` per CLAUDE.md, and every test calls `t.Parallel()` unless it modifies process-global state.

### Tested modules

- **`agent` package** — Add (new agent + idempotent re-add), Remove (existing + missing), List (empty + populated). Verifies hooks installation/uninstallation side effects on a temp repo.
- **`checkpointview` package** — Golden tests for short / full / raw renderings against fixture transcripts. Asserts intent/summary fallbacks when no AI summary is present.
- **`checkpointdiff` package** — Diff between two synthetic checkpoints (file-touched delta, token delta), empty diff for identical inputs, error path for missing checkpoint.
- **`alias` helper** — Top-level alias forwards args, flags, and exit codes to child. Deprecated alias prints exactly one stderr line per process even when invoked twice in the same process.
- **`clean --shadow`** — Removes shadow branch and session state files for current HEAD; behaves identically to the old `reset` command on equivalent fixtures.
- **`doctor logs`** — Returns last N lines from a fixture log directory; `--follow` exits on context cancellation.
- **`doctor bundle`** — Produced zip exists at the printed path and contains the expected entries (logs, settings.json, git snapshot file, version info).

### Skipped (or only smoke-tested)

- Cobra wiring in `root.go` is not unit-tested; coverage comes from the alias and group children's tests.
- Existing tests for `rewind`, `resume`, `attach`, `explain`, `trace`, `search`, `sessions`, `configure`, and `reset` continue to pass against the alias surface; no new tests are added there in Phase 1.

### Prior art

- Integration tests in `cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/` cover hook-driven flows using `testutil.InitRepo` and `execx.NonInteractive` — the new bundle/logs tests follow the same pattern.
- Existing `explain_test.go`, `sessions_test.go`, and `clean_test.go` are the closest reference for command-level test shape.
- Strategy package tests demonstrate fixture-based shadow-branch setup that the `clean --shadow` test reuses.

## Out of Scope

- Phase 2 (additional deprecation warnings) and Phase 3 (hiding deprecated aliases). Scheduled for later releases once Phase 1 lands.
- Renaming or restructuring the hidden infrastructure commands (`hooks`, `git-hook`, `migrate`, `trail`, `__send_analytics`, `curl-bash-post-install`).
- Any changes to checkpoint storage, session state machine, or strategy semantics. The new `checkpoint`/`session` groups are reorganizations of existing capabilities, not new behavior.
- Adding `checkpoint replay`, `update` (self-update), `feedback`/`report`, or any other commands floated during exploration but not selected.
- Changes to telemetry events. The `__send_analytics` subprocess is unchanged.
- Any refactor of `activity` or `dispatch`.

## Further Notes

- Phase 1 is intentionally additive so that `mise run test:ci` should remain green throughout. The integration test suite already invokes the existing top-level commands, which continue to work via aliases.
- The Vogon canary suite must run after the changes (`mise run test:e2e:canary`) to verify the new structure does not regress hook-driven flows; no Vogon changes are anticipated since prompt wording does not change.
- Documentation updates land in the same PR: `CLAUDE.md` Key Directories section, getting-started snippet in `root.go`, and any inline references in `--help` output that still mention the old names should be reviewed for accuracy.
- Future work to consider after Phase 1 lands: `checkpoint replay <id>` (re-run a captured prompt against current HEAD), `update` (CLI self-update partner to the existing `curl-bash-post-install`), and `report`/`feedback` (one-shot bug submission using `doctor bundle`).

# `entire review`

Experimental review command for running one configured review profile.

## Basic use

```sh
entire review --configure       # create or edit a profile
entire review --list            # list profiles
entire review <profile>         # run a profile
entire review --profile <name>  # same as positional form
entire review --agent <name>    # run one reviewer from the profile
entire review --target <ref>    # review a branch/trail in a managed worktree
entire review --findings        # view local findings
entire review --show-config     # list what the review would run, then exit
```

Useful run flags:

```sh
entire review --prompt "focus on auth"
entire review --timeout 15m
entire review --agent claude-code --model opus
entire review general --target feature/my-change
entire review general --target feature/my-change --cleanup-worktree
entire review general --target https://entire.com/gh/acme/app/trails/42/my-change
```

`--target` accepts a branch name, trail ID/number, or Entire trail URL. It
resolves the trail when needed, fetches a remote-only branch, and creates or
reuses a worktree under `.entire/worktrees`. The review command is then re-run
inside that worktree, leaving the caller's current checkout unchanged. If the
branch is already checked out in another worktree, that worktree is reused.
After a successful interactive review, a newly-created worktree prompts for
removal. Non-interactive reviews keep it unless `--cleanup-worktree` is passed.
A reused worktree is never removed by the review command, and failed reviews
retain newly-created worktrees for inspection. Cancelling the optional cleanup
prompt also keeps the worktree without changing the successful review exit.
Findings are attributed to the caller's worktree, so the completion handle
remains available through `entire review --findings` even after target cleanup.
Positive integer targets always mean trail numbers rather than numeric branch
names; this avoids a local branch silently shadowing a trail selector.

## Profiles

Profiles live in:

- `.entire/settings.json` for shared project config
- `.entire/settings.local.json` for local, git-ignored config

A profile contains:

- `task`: what to review for
- `agents`: reviewer slots
- `judge`: optional final consolidating reviewer
- `output`: `local` or `trail`

Minimal example:

```json
{
  "review_default_profile": "general",
  "review_profiles": {
    "general": {
      "task": "Review this change for correctness, regressions, tests, and maintainability.",
      "agents": {
        "claude-code": {"skills": ["/review"]},
        "codex": {"skills": ["/review"]},
        "pi": {"model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet", "prompt": "Review the change according to the profile task."}
      },
      "judge": {"agent": "claude-code"},
      "output": "local"
    }
  }
}
```

`entire review --models` lists the models each review-runner agent advertises via the optional `agent.ModelLister` capability (`cmd/entire/cli/agent/model_lister.go`). claude-code returns a curated list of real aliases (opus/sonnet/haiku); Pi enumerates live by shelling out to `pi --list-models`. An agent whose CLI has no enumeration command (codex) does not implement `ListModels`, so the picker offers only Default + Custom. The `--model` flag still forwards any value the agent CLI accepts.

The profile-level `task` is the shared work item. Each `agents` map entry is a worker id. For simple entries the worker id is also the agent name; to run the same agent more than once, use aliases and set `agent` plus `model`. Per-worker `skills`, `prompt`, and `model` adapt that task to agent-specific mechanics. Pi is a prompt/model-driven worker (`pi --mode json --print [--model ...]`, prompt on stdin) rather than a slash-command worker. Every reviewer, and the judge, receives its prompt on stdin, never in argv; `TestReviewers_PromptNeverInArgv` and `TestJudges_PromptNeverInArgv` enforce this. Settings fields: `EntireSettings.ReviewProfiles` and `EntireSettings.ReviewDefaultProfile` in `cmd/entire/cli/settings/settings.go`. The old top-level `review` map is parse-tolerated and can be exposed as a legacy `general` profile when no `review_profiles` are configured.

## Behavior

- Reviewers run the profile task.
- Multi-reviewer profiles run reviewers concurrently, then run one judge.
- Results are printed and saved locally; `output: "trail"` also posts findings to the branch trail.
- In trail mode, reviewers and the judge end their output with a JSON line, `{"summary":...,"comments":[...]}` (`trail_report.go`). The instruction is appended last, after profile and per-run text, and is skipped for a verbatim `prompt` override. Posting reads that line instead of interpreting prose:
  - `"comments":[]` posts nothing, unless the prose has a list item, a severity marker, a feedback label such as `Nits:` or `Findings:`, or a non-approving verdict such as `request changes`, `approve with nits`, or `needs changes` (also when labeled `Verdict:` or `Verdict -`).
  - Comments post as native findings with their severity and location; entries without a body are dropped. When the prose has more severity-marked findings than the line has comments, the line is incomplete and the prose is posted instead, since it normally repeats every comment. When a judge runs, its line alone decides what is posted. Without a judge, each reviewer's report (the last text between tool calls that ends with a valid line) is read separately and the comments are merged; earlier narration cannot contradict it. A reviewer whose report contradicts its line posts that report; one without a valid line posts its whole narrative. Either is posted alongside the other reviewers' structured comments.
  - A missing or malformed line (no `comments` array) posts the prose, with a trailing `summary`/`comments` object removed, split into findings by top-level bullet. Other trailing JSON, such as a quoted config snippet, stays. A JSON-only reply posts its `summary`, or the reviewers' narratives when it has none; when neither has text, nothing is posted and the run says so.
  - The line is kept in the saved manifest and hidden when results are displayed.
  - Posting keeps at most `maxPostedReviewFindings` findings, most severe first (high, medium, low, then unrated) and in their original order, and cuts a body over `maxPostedReviewFindingRunes` characters on a character boundary with a note, closing any code fence the cut leaves open (`review_bridge.go`). Both stay under the server's per-batch and per-body limits, so a capped review posts in one request and one long finding cannot fail the batch. The command says how many findings it left out or shortened. A line or range finding's `selected_text` is capped at the same length in `prepareTrailReviewLocationForCreate`, which `entire trail finding add` also goes through: a worktree span over the cap posts at file granularity. `entire trail finding add` does not cap the body.
  - A line or range location, from a comment or inferred from prose such as `path/file.go:12`, keeps its lines only when the scope lets its file be quoted and the span is at most `maxReviewTrailAnchorLines` (`review_bridge.go`). Otherwise a file the scope covers is posted against that file, and any other file against the whole change. Posted paths are cleaned. The quoted snippet is always read from the worktree at those lines; a model-supplied `selected_text` is ignored.
  - The scope (`TrailScope`, `review/scope.go`) is computed before any reviewer runs. Quotable files are those the branch adds or modifies since the scope base, plus staged, unstaged, and untracked files that are not ignored. Paths the uncommitted changes delete or rename away are left out, since an ignored local file can sit at one, and so are skip-worktree and assume-unchanged files, whose local text git hides. Each quotable file is hashed then; a file whose contents changed by posting time, such as one a reviewer rewrote, is posted against that file without a quote. Every tracked file is covered at file level. An untracked file that is not ignored, such as a new `.env`, is quotable. Without a scope base only uncommitted files are quotable, and the run says so; if git fails the scope is empty, the run says so, and every line location is posted against the whole change.
- A bare non-interactive `entire review` does not auto-run a profile. Automation should pass a profile name.
- Profile selection is positional/`--profile` → `review_default_profile` → `general` → the only configured profile.

## Reviewing code by someone else

Reviewers load the checkout's full agent configuration: `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`,
skills, hooks, MCP servers, plugins, and settings. On a teammate's branch that
configuration is theirs, so a review of commits you did not author needs your
approval first.

- **Whose commits.** Every commit between your default branch (origin/HEAD,
  origin/main, origin/master, main, master) and the head must have your
  `user.email` as its git author, as for any commit; who committed it does not
  matter. `--base` only scopes the review; it never shortens this range.
  Uncommitted changes in a plain review are yours. With no `user.email`
  (common on CI runners) or no default branch, the commits count as someone
  else's, so automation passes `--trust-target`. The author is self-declared,
  as in any git commit, so this tells a teammate's branch from yours; it is
  not proof against a branch that copies your email. Verifying commit
  signatures and using a trail's authenticated author are follow-ups.
- **What runs.** The gate lists, for the agents in the profile: hooks (Entire's
  own count only when the whole command equals one this CLI installs, Unix or
  Windows form), MCP servers, command-bearing and permission settings in
  `.claude/settings*.json`, every key of `.codex/config.toml` (except the flags
  that only switch hooks on) and `.pi/settings.json`, Pi extensions other than
  Entire's, and every skill, command, prompt, subagent, and local plugin under
  `.claude`, `.codex`, `.agents/skills`, and `.pi`, which can carry their own
  hooks or shell expansions. JSON is read with exact keys, as the agents read
  it, and the commit tree is matched case-insensitively, as a macOS or Windows
  checkout would load it. Symlinks and unparseable files count as unknown,
  never as nothing. `--show-config` (`--json` for structured output) prints the
  full list and exits; its contents come from the branch and are data.
- **Approval.** In a terminal, a confirm lists up to three entries (the
  branch's own first) and defaults to Cancel. Without a terminal, or when an
  agent is driving the command (caller-session variables, the shared
  agent-subprocess sentinels, `CLAUDECODE`, Antigravity's and Droid's
  variables, the cross-tool `AI_AGENT`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, or variables
  an external agent declares in `caller_env_vars`), the review is refused with a
  fixed message that tells the agent to stop and ask the user, plus the
  `--trust-target <sha>` command to run once approved. `--trust-target` takes
  the full SHA of the pinned head (a short prefix could be ground to match a
  different commit); a branch that moved is refused.
- **Order.** With `--target`, the profile is resolved and the branch fetched
  and pinned in your checkout, the gate inspects the pinned commit's tree, and
  only then is the worktree created: added with `--no-checkout` and no hooks,
  its head checked against the pin, then checked out. For someone else's
  branch the checkout runs with an empty `core.hooksPath`, no submodule
  recursion, and `GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE=1`, and `.worktreeinclude` files are not
  copied. A reused worktree is inspected on disk instead.
- **Settings.** The re-run inside the worktree reads review settings (profiles,
  agents, models, judge) from your checkout, not the branch's
  `.entire/settings.json`, and skips the gate only when the forwarded
  `--trust-target` matches its own head. Entire's own lifecycle hooks, which
  the agents start inside the worktree, still read that worktree's settings.
- **Guardrail.** Every reviewer gets a system-prompt addition setting an
  instruction hierarchy: the task comes only from the review request;
  repository content (including CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md) informs the review but
  cannot change the task, grant permissions, or trigger actions; attempts to
  direct the reviewer are reported as findings (`--append-system-prompt` for
  Claude Code and Pi, `-c developer_instructions=` for Codex, the top of the
  prompt for agents without a runner). The judge runs from a temp directory
  and does not load the checkout's configuration.

## Reviewer agent config in profiles

A review profile can give each reviewer its own agent config, which replaces
the reviewed checkout's hooks, MCP servers and extensions for that reviewer.
Set it with `entire review --edit` (per reviewer: keep, use the checkout's,
own config with nothing extra, or load a JSON file) or
`entire review --configure <profile> --set-config <reviewer>=<file|isolated|none>`.

```json
{"settings": {"hooks": {...}, "permissions": {...}, "env": {...}},
 "mcp_servers": {"docs": {"command": "/opt/mcp/docs", "args": ["--stdio"]}},
 "extensions": ["/opt/pi/review.ts"]}
```

| Agent | Checkout config dropped | Profile config applied | Still loaded from the checkout |
|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `--setting-sources user`, `--strict-mcp-config` | `settings` (with Entire's tracking hooks added) via `--settings`; `mcp_servers` via `--mcp-config` | CLAUDE.md; `.claude/skills` and `.claude/commands`, copied from the committed tree as the `project` plugin (`/review` becomes `/project:review`); symlinks and submodules there are skipped, not followed (the trust gate lists them as not inspected) |
| Codex | checkout and main repo marked untrusted for the run (project config, hooks, rules) | `mcp_servers` via `-c` (`command`, `args`, `url` and `default_tools_approval_mode`; other fields and literal `env` values are refused, and so is a server name the user's `~/.codex/config.toml` already defines, since Codex would merge the two); Entire's tracking hooks via `-c` with `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust`, which also runs the user's own untrusted hooks (Codex keeps hooks per config layer, so these are added beside the user's `config.toml` hooks, not in place of them) | AGENTS.md; skills |
| Pi | `--no-extensions` | `extensions` via `--extension`, plus Entire's own | AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, skills, prompt templates, `.pi/settings.json` |

Rules:

- **Developer-owned only.** A reviewer config is honored only from clone-local
  preferences or an untracked `.entire/settings.local.json`, never from the
  committed settings file (dropped with a note), the judge, or the legacy
  `review` map. A local file that can't be verified as untracked fails the
  review instead of running it with the checkout's config. Saves go to the
  local file when it defines the profile, else clone-local preferences
  (`review_agent_configs`, by profile and reviewer), which overlay only the
  config so the rest of the profile still comes from its own layer.
- **Where config comes from is enforced; what commands do is not.** The
  branch's hooks, MCP servers and extensions are not loaded. The profile's own
  hooks, MCP servers and helpers are the user's code, like the hooks in their
  agent settings: they run in the reviewed checkout as configured, and Entire
  doesn't vet them (a command at an absolute path can still run the branch's
  `package.json` scripts). A value naming a path inside the checkout or
  `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` gets a warning at save time and before each run, since
  it is usually a copy-paste mistake. Prompts never say nothing runs when the
  profile configures hooks or MCP servers.
- **Permissions come from the loaded settings.** Reviewers run headless, so a
  tool call not allowed by the settings the reviewer loads is denied. With a
  profile config those are the user's own settings plus the profile's
  `settings`; the project's `.claude/settings.json` allows no longer apply.
  Allow a profile MCP tool in the profile's `settings.permissions.allow`
  (e.g. `mcp__docs__search`) for Claude, or with
  `"default_tools_approval_mode": "approve"` on the server for Codex, whose
  exec mode can't ask. Both report blocked calls, and the run prints them
  after the reviewer finishes with where to allow them.
- **Fail, don't fall back.** An agent that can't apply a field (Codex
  `settings`, Pi `mcp_servers`, …) fails the review with an explanation.
- **Gate.** Skills and commands can run their own commands, so reviewing
  someone else's code still needs approval; for reviewers with their own
  config the warning lists only what still loads from the branch, and
  `--show-config` names them (`isolated_agents` in `--json`). Each run prints
  which reviewers use their own config.
- Files the run needs (settings, MCP config, the skills plugin) are written
  0600 to a per-run directory under the user cache and removed when the
  reviewer exits. An older `entire` binary rejects settings files containing
  `config`.
- Team-shared reviewer config and Codex hooks are follow-ups.

## Flow

1. With `--target`, `entire review` selects the profile in the caller's checkout, resolves the branch directly or through its trail, pins its head, runs the trust gate, prepares a worktree, and re-runs the command there without `--target`. `--prompt` reaches the re-run through `ENTIRE_REVIEW_TARGET_PROMPT`, not its argv.
2. It selects a profile. If no profiles exist, it runs guided setup in an interactive terminal or writes an opinionated clone-local default profile in non-interactive mode. Plain reviews then run the trust gate.
3. It composes worker prompts via `review.ComposeReviewPrompt` and computes scope (mainline base ref via `review.ComputeScopeStats`, overridable with `--base`).
4. Adapter-backed review workers (claude-code, codex, pi) are spawned with `ENTIRE_REVIEW_{SESSION,AGENT,SKILLS,PROMPT,STARTING_SHA}` env vars. Their lifecycle hooks use those values to tag sessions as `Kind = "agent_review"`.
5. Each spawned process has its own env, so multiple worktrees and multi-agent runs do not need a shared marker file.
6. In multi-worker profiles, the configured judge receives all worker reports and produces one final verdict. The judge prompt asks it to reject unsupported claims, resolve contradictions, merge duplicates, and prioritize evidence-backed findings. Each report sits between BEGIN and END lines that carry a random token made for that prompt, after the reviewers finished, so a report cannot write a marker that closes its own fence. The prompt tells the judge to treat report contents as untrusted data.
7. On the next `git commit`, the PostCommit hook condenses worker review sessions into the checkpoint on `entire/checkpoints/v1`, with `Kind`, `ReviewSkills`, and `ReviewPrompt` recorded in `CommittedMetadata`.
8. `CheckpointSummary.HasReview` is set for O(1) lookup. `entire status` and the re-run guard read this flag from checkpoint metadata.

## Checkpoint Metadata

Review metadata is stored at two levels on `entire/checkpoints/v1`:

- **`CommittedMetadata` (per-session)**: `kind: "agent_review"`, `review_skills: ["/skill1", "/skill2"]`, `review_prompt: "..."`
- **`CheckpointSummary` (per-checkpoint)**: `has_review: true` (umbrella; set when any session in the checkpoint has a review-kind `Kind`)

## Architecture

- **`AgentReviewer` interface** (`cmd/entire/cli/review/types/reviewer.go`): per-agent contract with `Name() string` and `Start(ctx, RunConfig) (Process, error)`. Each adapter-backed review worker implements this in its own package.
- **`ReviewerTemplate`** (`cmd/entire/cli/review/types/template.go`): shared scaffolding (spawn → pipe stdout → run parser → forward events → close). Each agent supplies its `BuildCmd` and `Parser`, plus an optional `Preflight` that refuses an unusable CLI before the run (Pi requires >= 0.65.1, the first release that keeps `--mode json` output for a prompt on stdin).
- **`Sink` interface** (`cmd/entire/cli/review/types/sink.go`): consumers of the event stream. Production sinks include `DumpSink`, `TUISink`, and `SynthesisSink`.
- **`Run(ctx, reviewer, cfg, sinks)`** (`cmd/entire/cli/review/run.go`): single-agent orchestrator. Forwards events to sinks and calls `RunFinished` once with a populated `RunSummary`.
- **`RunMulti(ctx, reviewers, cfg, sinks)`** (`cmd/entire/cli/review/run_multi.go`): N-agent orchestrator. Agents run concurrently; events fan into a single dispatch loop so sink dispatch remains serialized.
- **Env-var contract** (`cmd/entire/cli/review/env.go`): single source of truth for `ENTIRE_REVIEW_*` constants used by spawn-side and lifecycle adoption.
- **Scope detection** (`cmd/entire/cli/review/scope.go`): `detectScopeBaseRef` returns the first existing ref from `origin/HEAD → origin/main → origin/master → main → master`.

## Multi-Agent UI

When `RunMulti` is dispatched in a TTY, sink composition includes a live Bubble Tea dashboard plus buffered narrative/final-report output:

- **`TUISink` / `reviewTUIModel`** (`cmd/entire/cli/review/tui_sink.go`, `tui_model.go`, `tui_detail.go`): one row per agent with status, tokens, last assistant preview, and duration. `Ctrl+O` enters drill-in mode; `Esc` returns; `Ctrl+C` cancels through the shared context.
- **`SynthesisSink`** (`cmd/entire/cli/review/synthesis_sink.go`): in profile-native mode, runs automatically after the dump, composes an adjudication prompt covering worker narratives + per-run user prompt + profile task, calls the judge agent, and prints the final report.
- **Sink composition** (`composeMultiAgentSinks` in `cmd/entire/cli/review/cmd.go`): pure helper taking explicit `isTTY`/`canPrompt` so tests do not depend on real TTY detection.

## Skill Discovery (Claude Code)

`DiscoverReviewSkills` (`cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode/discovery.go`) walks three roots under Claude Code's config directory (`$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, default `~/.claude`): plugin cache (`plugins/cache/<market>/<plugin>/<version>/{skills,commands,agents}`), user skills (`skills`), and user commands/agents (`commands`, `agents`).

For the plugin cache, `pickLatestVersion` picks one version directory per plugin: highest valid semver wins; if no entries parse as semver, the lexicographic max is picked.

## Anti-Features (do NOT recreate)

The redesign eliminated several constructs from the prior implementation. None should be reintroduced without explicit design:

- `PendingReviewMarker` for adapter-backed review workers (env-var handshake makes it unnecessary)
- `WorktreePath` field + worktree-scoping logic (env per process eliminates the multi-tenant problem)
- `AgentEntries` map on the marker (each agent has its own env)
- Marker overwrite tripwire / refuse-attach guard (the bug classes they defended against do not exist)
- `--track-only` flag
- `--postreview` / `--finalize` / empty review commits / `/entire-review:finish` skill installer
- `Launcher` + `HeadlessLauncher` as separate interfaces (single `AgentReviewer`)
- Codex chrome-line filtering or any agent-specific stdout post-processing in shared multi-agent code (per-agent parsers own their format)
- `sync.Once`-guarded onCancel + parallel `signal.Notify` goroutine (single cancel from start)

## Key Files

- `cmd/entire/cli/review/cmd.go` — `NewCommand()`, `runReview`, sink composition
- `cmd/entire/cli/review/picker.go` / `profile.go` — profile config picker, first-run setup, profile resolution/default tasks
- `cmd/entire/cli/review/prompt.go` / `scope.go` / `run.go` / `dump.go` / `run_multi.go` — core machinery
- `cmd/entire/cli/review/tui_sink.go` / `tui_model.go` / `tui_detail.go` — Bubble Tea TUI sink
- `cmd/entire/cli/review/synthesis_sink.go` / `synthesis_prompt.go` — judge adjudication
- `cmd/entire/cli/review/types/{reviewer,sink,template}.go` — interface contracts and shared review template
- `cmd/entire/cli/review/env.go` — `ENTIRE_REVIEW_*` constants + `EncodeSkills`/`DecodeSkills` + `AppendReviewEnv`
- `cmd/entire/cli/agent/{claudecode,codex,pi}/reviewer.go` — per-agent `AgentReviewer` implementations
- `cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode/discovery.go` — skill discovery + plugin-cache dedupe
- `cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go` — `adoptReviewEnv` reads `ENTIRE_REVIEW_*` from process env
- `cmd/entire/cli/review_bridge.go` / `review_target.go` — bridge code for cycle-bound functions, trail posting, and target resolution and checkout
- `cmd/entire/cli/review/trust.go` / `trust_run.go` — trust gate: authorship, approval, messages, `--show-config`
- `cmd/entire/cli/review_trust_inventory.go` — per-agent inventory of what a checkout would run
- `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/checkpoint.go` — review metadata on checkpoints
- `cmd/entire/cli/settings/settings.go` — review profile settings

issues.title: fix(review): don't hang when a grandchild inherits the agent's stderr
issues.body:
## The bug

`templateProcess.Wait` waited for stderr EOF before calling `cmd.Wait`:

```go
if p.stderrDone != nil {
    <-p.stderrDone
}
err := p.cmd.Wait()
```

stderr reaches EOF only when every writer closes it. A review agent that leaves a background helper running — a language server, an MCP process, a sandbox helper — hands that helper the same stderr pipe. The agent can exit, the findings can be parsed, and `entire review` still blocks forever on the final wait.

## Reproduction

```go
// BuildCmd
exec.CommandContext(ctx, "sh", "-c", "sleep 5 >/dev/null & exit 0")
```

`Start` succeeds, the agent exits 0 immediately, and `Wait` is still blocked 2s later. On a real run the helper can outlive the review by minutes or hours.

## The fix

`cmd.StderrPipe` is replaced with a pipe we own. `Wait` now reaps the agent first and only then drains stderr:

- normal agent: the capture goroutine has already reached EOF, so nothing changes;
- helper still holding stderr: after a 250ms grace period we close our read end, the capture goroutine finishes, and `Wait` returns with whatever stderr it copied (kept for `ProcessError` diagnostics).

This also keeps the `Process` contract: no goroutine outlives `Wait`.

## Tests

`TestReviewerTemplate_WaitDoesNotBlockOnInheritedStderr` starts the shell above and fails on `main` after 2s with:

```
Wait() blocked on stderr held by a grandchild after the agent exited
```

The existing `WaitIncludesStderrOnFailure` test still passes, so normal failure diagnostics are preserved.

## Verification

- `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/review/...` passes
- `mise run lint:go`: 0 issues

issues.title: feat(execx,procutil): terminate process tree on Windows when context is cancelled
issues.body:
## Description
Fixes #3052.

### Background
On Unix, `execx.TerminateOnCancel` and `procutil.TerminateOnCancel` configure a new process group (`Setpgid = true`) and send `SIGKILL` to `-cmd.Process.Pid` on cancellation to terminate the entire process group.
On Windows, `killProcessGroupOnCancel` was previously a no-op stub:
```go
func killProcessGroupOnCancel(_ *exec.Cmd) {}
```
This fell back to Go's default `Cancel` behavior, which calls `TerminateProcess` on the direct child only. Because Windows does not automatically terminate child processes when a parent process exits, any descendants spawned by the child (such as `git-remote-https.exe`, `ssh.exe`, MCP servers, subagents, or clean filters) remained running in the background. Whenever descendants inherited stdout/stderr pipes, `cmd.Wait()` blocked for the full `KillWaitDelay` (10s in `execx`, 5s in `procutil`), causing noticeable delays and leaking running processes and pack file locks.

### Solution
1. **`execx.KillProcessTree(rootPid int)`**:
   - Uses `windows.CreateToolhelp32Snapshot(windows.TH32CS_SNAPPROCESS, 0)` to capture running processes and map parent-child relationships.
   - Traverses the process hierarchy to find all descendants of `rootPid`.
   - **PID Reuse Protection**: Queries `GetProcessTimes` on the root process and candidates, ensuring only processes created after the root process started are treated as descendants.
   - Terminates descendants bottom-up (deepest leaves first) before terminating the root process.
   - Falls back gracefully to direct process termination if taking the snapshot fails.

2. **Integration**:
   - Configures `cmd.Cancel` in `execx_windows.go` to invoke `KillProcessTree(cmd.Process.Pid)`.
   - Configures `cmd.Cancel` in `procutil_windows.go` to invoke `execx.KillProcessTree(cmd.Process.Pid)`.

3. **Tests**:
   - Added `TestTerminateOnCancel_SetsWaitDelayAndCancelWindows` and `TestTerminateOnCancel_KillsProcessTreeWindows` in `cmd/entire/cli/execx/execx_windows_test.go`.
   - Added `TestTerminateOnCancel_UnblocksGrandchildHoldingPipeWindows` in `cmd/entire/cli/procutil/procutil_windows_test.go`.
   - Both tests verify that a background grandchild process holding the stdout pipe is cleanly terminated and `cmd.Wait()` unblocks immediately without waiting for `WaitDelay`.

## Verification
Tested on a native Windows machine:
- Grandchild process holding the output pipe unblocks in **<10ms** upon context cancellation.
- Grandchild process (`ping.exe`) is confirmed terminated from the system process table.
- Verified that `go build ./cmd/entire` and `go vet` pass cleanly.

issues.title: fix(execx): kill the whole process tree when a command is cancelled on Windows
issues.body:
Fixes #3052: on Windows, cancelling a subprocess at its deadline killed only the direct child, so its children kept running.

## What happened

On Unix, `execx.TerminateOnCancel` and `procutil.TerminateOnCancel` start the command in its own process group and kill the whole group when the context is cancelled. On Windows both were no-ops, so cancellation fell back to `exec.Cmd`'s default `Cancel`, which terminates the direct child only. Windows doesn't kill a process's children when it dies. A child that inherited stdout (`git-remote-https` behind `git`, a sandbox helper or MCP server behind an agent CLI) kept running, and `Wait` blocked until `WaitDelay` force-closed the pipe: 10 s late in execx, 5 s in procutil.

## The fix

I went with option 1 from the issue, walking the process tree, because it needs no caller changes. Option 2, a Job Object, would make every caller start through a helper. Happy to switch if you'd rather have that one.

On Windows, `Cancel` now:

1. Reads the process table (`CreateToolhelp32Snapshot`) and opens every descendant of the direct child. This happens before anything is killed, so a child that exits as soon as its parent dies is already held. Everything runs inside `Process.WithHandle`, so the child's PID keeps naming it for the whole walk, even if it has already exited.
2. Terminates the direct child, then every descendant, parents before children, as `taskkill /T` does.
3. Repeats up to three passes for processes started while it ran. `TerminateProcess` only starts a termination, and a process can create children until it has exited. So each later pass first waits for everything killed so far to exit, with one two-second deadline for all the waits. A pass that finds nothing ends the walk only if all of them had exited before it read the table.

**PID reuse.** A table entry's parent PID survives the parent, and the PID can then be reused. So a process counts as a descendant only if, opened by PID, the kernel reports a tree member as its parent for that handle (`NtQueryInformationProcess`), and it was created after that member. Creation order comes from the process sequence number, which the kernel counts per boot, so a clock change can't reorder it. Where the system doesn't report one (older Windows versions, Wine), the creation time stands in. Every member stays open until the walk ends, so its PID can't be reused meanwhile. A member has held its PID since it was created, so any later process that names that PID as its parent was started by it.

**After `Wait`.** Once `Wait` has reaped the child, `Cancel` walks nothing and returns `os.ErrProcessDone`, as the default `Cancel` does then. The PID may already name another process.

**A child that already exited.** If the direct child has exited but hasn't been waited for, `Cancel` still kills its descendants and returns nil, as the Unix group kill does. That is the case from the issue: a child that starts a grandchild sharing its stdout, then exits.

**What it can't reach.**

- A process whose own parent, other than the direct child, had already exited.
- A process started after the last pass.
- A command whose direct child `Wait` has already collected, for example through `Run` or `Output`, while a descendant still holds stdout. os/exec doesn't call `Cancel` after that point, so the deadline does nothing. That holds on Unix too: with a 1 s deadline, `sh -c 'sleep 30 & exit 0'` through `Output()` returns `ErrWaitDelay` after 10 s. In the narrow race where the child exits just as the deadline fires and `Wait` releases its handle before `Cancel` runs, `Cancel` returns `os.ErrProcessDone`. Unix's group kill would still reach the group there.

`WaitDelay` still bounds all three, as before. A Job Object would cover the first and third on Windows.

`procutil.TerminateOnCancel` now calls the new `execx.KillTreeOnCancel` instead of keeping its own copy, so Unix and Windows each have one implementation. Unix behaviour doesn't change: the two Unix copies were identical. `docs/development/git-safety.md` has a short section on the Windows walk.

## Tests

`execx/treekill_windows_test.go`. Every test has `Windows` in its name, so the `test-windows` job runs them. They re-exec the test binary to build real process trees that inherit stdout.

- `TestTerminateOnCancel_KillsProcessTreeWindows` covers five trees: a child the parent waits for, a child whose parent already exited (the issue's case), a grandchild, a grandchild whose parent already exited, and a grandchild under a child that exits as soon as its own parent does. Each checks that the drain returns in under half of `KillWaitDelay`, and that the leaf process is dead.
- `TestTerminateOnCancel_SparesUnrelatedProcessesWindows`: a process started beside the command survives the cancel.
- `TestKillProcessGroupOnCancel_AfterWaitWindows`: `Cancel` after `Wait` returns `os.ErrProcessDone`.
- `TestFindDescendantsWindows`: the PID-reuse checks against a fake process table. The cases are:
  - a process older than the parent PID it lists;
  - a PID reused after the table was read;
  - a parent that can't be opened;
  - a child created in the same clock tick as its parent;
  - a clock set back between parent and child, where the sequence numbers decide;
  - an equal sequence number;
  - the creation-time fallback.

I don't have a Windows machine. I ran the Windows test binary under Wine 9.0 on Linux: everything passes, three runs in a row. Wine doesn't report sequence numbers, so those runs use the creation-time fallback, and the fake-table cases cover the sequence-number path. With main's no-op `Cancel`, every tree case fails with "drain did not return after cancel". Wine isn't Windows, so the `test-windows` job is the real check. @mattjes, if you have a minute, `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/execx/ ./cmd/entire/cli/procutil/` on Windows would help.

On Linux, the execx, procutil and review/types tests pass, golangci-lint v2.15.0 is clean for `./...` and for these packages with `GOOS=windows`, and `GOOS=windows` and `GOOS=darwin` builds pass.

@MuskanPaliwal @Soph

<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Follow-up to #2140, from findings left on [trail #1153](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1153) that weren't picked up before it merged.

## The judge still hung

#2140 applied `execx.TerminateOnCancel` to `RunIsolatedTextGeneratorCLI`, covering codex, cursor, gemini, copilot and pi. Claude Code deliberately runs the CLI itself on both its text-generation paths (`generate.go`, `generate_streaming.go`), so neither was bounded — and `defaultJudge` prefers claude-code, so `entire review`'s judge still hung in the default configuration.

- **`generate.go`** is the judge's path: `AgentSynthesisProvider.Synthesize` calls `tg.GenerateText`.
- **`generate_streaming.go`** blocks in the `io.Copy(io.Discard, counted)` drain *before* `cmd.Wait()`, so absent `WaitDelay` nothing force-closes the pipe. Its comment — "Without this, a blocked pipe would deadlock cmd.Wait()" — only holds for the direct child. Reached from `entire explain --generate` and from post-commit condensation (`manual_commit_condensation.go:1015`), where `summarizeCtx` carries no deadline at all.

Both hung >20s past a 300ms deadline before this and return in ~300ms after. The new table test in `generate_cancel_test.go` fails on the pre-fix tree (verified by reverting the two source hunks).

## Also from the review

- **`execx`: skip `Setpgid` when the caller already set `Setsid`.** `setpgid(2)` on a session leader is `EPERM`, which surfaced from fork/exec as a bare `operation not permitted` — reading as a sandbox problem rather than misuse. `NonInteractive` + `TerminateOnCancel` therefore could not compose, guarded only by a doc comment. A session leader is already its own process-group leader, so the group kill still reaches the tree; this replaces the warning with working behaviour, covered by `TestTerminateOnCancel_ComposesWithNonInteractive`.
- **Document the `TextCommandRunner` contract.** Setting `Cancel` on a cmd the helper didn't build makes `exec.CommandContext` mandatory for injected runners; exec otherwise fails with `command with a non-nil Cancel was not created with CommandContext`, naming a field the runner author never set. No production caller is affected (all pass nil).
- **Tighten the agent-level deadline test** to `KillWaitDelay/2`, so the 10s backstop can't mask a group-kill regression.
- **Drop the group-kill test duplicated into `checkpoint/remote`** — after #2140 it's byte-identical to the execx copy and only exercises a one-line pass-through. `TestKillProcessGroupOnCancel_SetsSetpgidAndCancel` still covers `newCommand`'s wiring.
- **`architecture_test.go`:** allow agent packages to import `execx`, a leaf utility with no repo-internal deps (`go list -deps` confirms).

## Testing

`mise run fmt && mise run lint` clean (0 issues). `mise run test:ci` green except `TestCodexAppServerHooksList_BareWorktreeUsesLayoutRoot`, which fails identically on clean `main` on macOS with codex installed (`/var` vs `/private/var`) — pre-existing, unrelated.

Each new test was checked red-then-green against its own fix.
