issues.title: OpenCode native subagent tracking
issues.body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1316
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Summary

OpenCode runs each `task`-tool subagent as a real child session, so Entire registered every child as a top-level session: the child took the checkpoint, and the parent logged "no files modified". This PR tracks those children the way other agents' subagents are tracked — as task records on the parent session, stored under the parent's checkpoint as `tasks/<callID>/{task.json, agent-<child>.jsonl}` (the child's full exported session).

Covered, each verified against real OpenCode:

- **foreground, single and concurrent** children: one record per task call, with the child's own files and exact tokens
- **`task_id` resumption**: a child resumed for another call gets a record per call, each holding only that call's messages, files and tokens
- **nested** subagents (`subagent_depth > 1`): recorded on the top-level session
- **background** subagents (`OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_BACKGROUND_SUBAGENTS`, or a task promoted mid-run): completed when the child session finishes, not at launch
- **a resume that joins a running background child**: OpenCode queues it as the child's next run; each call completes at its own run's idle and keeps only its own messages
- **command subtasks** (`subtask: true` commands): OpenCode keys their tool hooks by the task part's id rather than its `callID`; start and stop are paired under the `callID`
- **aborted or failed task calls** (Esc, `opencode run` teardown, a throwing execute): OpenCode skips `tool.execute.after`; the task part's `error` state completes the record instead
- **reused or unsafe callIDs**: some providers number tool calls per conversation (`call_0`) or use IDs that aren't path-safe (`functions.task:0`). An unsafe ID maps to a deterministic safe key (`functions_task_0-<hash>`). A stop that reuses an earlier call's ID for a different child, or for the same child starting later, is recorded under its own key (`<callID>-<child>[-<startMs>]`) instead of being dropped. The plugin keys its in-flight call state by session plus callID, so a nested call can't take its parent's.
- **a failed or not-yet-run export**: condensation re-exports the child, so a mid-task commit or a stop-time export failure still stores the transcript (unless the parent is left out of that commit; see Known gaps)

Size: +3392/-103 across 30 files, mostly tests and the plugin plus its generated dogfood copy.

## How it works

The embedded plugin learns child sessions from `parentID` and the task part's metadata and forwards no lifecycle hooks for them. It fires `subagent-start` when a task part is `running` with its child bound, and `subagent-stop` from `tool.execute.after` (foreground), from the task part reaching `error` (aborted or failed), or from the child's own busy → idle (background, oldest held call first). It keeps each announced task's payload until it stops, so every start gets exactly one stop under the same `tool_use_id`. Each hook carries `started_at`, the plugin's clock at `tool.execute.before`. The Go adapter turns the stop into a `Final` + `CompletionWithoutLaunch` `SubagentEnd` with no transcript. After its skip checks, the shared final capture calls `FetchSubagentTranscript` (at most one export per stop): it runs `opencode export` for the child, cuts it to this call's slice (from its prompt, the first real user message at or after `started_at`, to the next call's prompt), writes it to `.entire/tmp/<child>.<callID>.json`, declares it, and completes the record exactly once.

## Please look at

Changes outside the OpenCode package:

- `Event.DeferredCompletion` — a start that records an in-flight marker without a pre-task baseline.
- `Event.SubagentStartedAt` — becomes the task record's `StartedAt` when an agent supplies it; zero keeps today's `time.Now()`, so other agents are unchanged.
- `agent.SubagentTranscriptFetcher` — optional, built-in-only capability; the materializer calls it after the declared, inventory and agent-layout paths fail. Only OpenCode implements it (its `AgentID` is a fetchable session).
- `opencode export` now runs without git's repo-override variables (`gitrepo.EnvWithoutRepoOverrides`), since it runs inside git hooks.
- Merge with main: in-flight launch markers set `TaskRecord.Background`, so OpenCode's deferred launches (foreground included) count as overlapping background tasks. A Claude Code background stop in the same worktree then won't claim new untracked files while an OpenCode task overlaps it. Claude Code's own records are unchanged.
- event-files-only capture now keys on `SubagentTranscriptUnavailable` rather than `CompletionWithoutLaunch` (Copilot sets both, so it is unchanged).
- OpenCode prompt extraction and the condensed transcript (`explain`, summary prompts) skip a user message made only of synthetic text — how OpenCode delivers a background task's result.

Judgment call to confirm: children are suppressed plugin-side, so a child session a user opens directly in the TUI and drives by hand is not tracked at all. Deliberate for v1, documented in `AGENT.md`.

## Verified

- Live, OpenCode 1.18.33, branch binary, with a development-only probe script (not in the repo; `openai/gpt-5.5`): all ten probe scenarios — single, concurrent, read-only, nested, background, resume, background-resume (a resume joining a running background child), background-abort (aborting the parent with a joined call queued), subtask, abort and subtask-abort (Esc over `opencode serve`) — show one Entire session, one start and one stop per task call under the same `tool_use_id`, every record completed, and each record holding only its own call's files and child transcript.
- Paid e2e, full OpenCode suite (earlier head): 52/56 passed, including `TestSubagentCommitFlow` and `TestSingleSessionSubagentCommitInTurn`; 3 skipped (other agents). `TestInteractiveAttributionMultiCommitSameSession` failed identically with a binary built from `main` (the model had not committed within the 20 s window), so it is not from this branch.
- Unit, integration, Vogon canary and `mise run check` pass on the current head. The plugin's start/stop pairing is pinned by Node-driven tests (`plugin_tasks_test.go`) that replay OpenCode's hook and event orderings, including the subtask key mismatch, aborts, failures, stop-before-start ordering, reused `callID`s, nested errors and queued background runs.

## Known gaps

- One message resuming the same child twice in parallel: the queued call ends at the first run's idle, so its own run's work lands in no record. Needs the model to resume one child twice in one message.
- Aborting while the parent is already idle (no `MessageAbortedError` on it) relies on the child's own abort error to end calls queued on it; a joined run that keeps executing then holds later dropped calls until that child's next idle.
- Under `opencode run`, a background child still running when the parent finishes is aborted; its record completes with the transcript so far, but OpenCode's teardown starts a second plugin instance that leaves the parent ACTIVE until the exited-owner sweep ends it. The TUI is unaffected.
- entire.io has no subagent view yet for any agent. When one lands, entire-api's OpenCode parser needs to use the part's `callID` as the tool-call ID (it assigns a random one today) for records to join their task call.
- On macOS a child that spells a path through an unresolved symlink is dropped from the record's `files` by the shared normalizer (the parent's turn-end still attributes the file). Agent-agnostic; separate PR.
- A running background child's edits reach the parent's files only at its stop. Until then, an IDLE parent with no tracked files of its own is left out of a commit another session also claims. Counting a running child for that check is a follow-up PR.
- A reused-callID call has no in-flight record while it runs (its start is deduplicated), so it's recorded only at its stop. A reused-callID stop with no `started_at` (plugin restarted mid-call) on an already-recorded child is skipped as a duplicate, on purpose.
- entire.io joins task records to calls by exact `tool_use_id`, so mapped or re-keyed records show as unmatched until the subagent view joins on the child session (`agent_id`) and start time; see `AGENT.md`.
- Parent-level `SubagentTokens` aggregate is a follow-up; record-level tokens are exact.
- Three commits by implementer subagents carry a `Claude Sonnet 5` co-author trailer; a squash merge normalizes it.

issues.title: Bound checkpoint git subprocesses to their context deadline
issues.body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/440
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Problem

A `git push`/`git fetch` over a custom transport (e.g. `entire://`) can hang the pre-push hook for ~an hour despite a 2-minute timeout. A `doctor trace` of a stuck checkpoint push:

```
push_checkpoints_branch        3,502,176ms
  ├─ fetch_and_rebase             13,695ms
  │  └─ git_fetch                 12,612ms
  ├─ git_push                      1,163ms  x
  └─ git_push~1                3,487,316ms  x   ← ~58 min
```

The context deadline SIGKILLs the `git` process, but the spawned remote-helper grandchild (e.g. `git-remote-entire`) keeps the output pipe open, so `cmd.CombinedOutput()` blocks until that helper finally exits.

## Fix

Harden every git subprocess built by `newCommand` (push / fetch / fetch-pack / ls-remote / cat-file):

- **WaitDelay backstop (all platforms):** after the process is killed, Go force-closes the pipes instead of waiting on a pipe-holding descendant.
- **Process-group kill (unix):** the child runs in its own process group and the whole group is SIGKILLed on cancellation, so the remote helper is terminated too rather than orphaned. Windows relies on the WaitDelay backstop (reliable process-tree kill there needs a Job Object, out of scope).

Turns "stuck forever" into a bounded failure: checkpoints stay saved locally and the user's own push proceeds.

## Testing

- Unit tests assert `newCommand` sets `WaitDelay` + a group-kill `Cancel` (unix `Setpgid`).
- A behavioral test reproduces the failure shape — a backgrounded grandchild holding the pipe — and confirms the group-kill terminates it promptly.
- Existing remote, strategy push/fetch/rebase, and integration remote tests pass.

## Notes

- The transport itself still hangs on the retry upload — that's the entiredb / `git-remote-entire` side; this PR just stops it from hanging the hook.
- The per-phase perf spans that produced the trace above are in a separate branch (`hooks-slow-push-db-mirror`).

> 
> **Overview**
> Checkpoint git subprocesses built by `newCommand` (push, fetch, fetch-pack, ls-remote, cat-file) are **hardened** so context timeouts are not defeated by orphaned transport helpers.
> 
> Every such command gets a **10s `WaitDelay`** so `CombinedOutput`/`Wait` cannot block indefinitely on pipe-holding descendants after the parent is killed. On **Unix**, children run in their own process group with a custom **`Cancel` that SIGKILLs the whole group**, so helpers like `git-remote-entire` are torn down instead of keeping stdout open for tens of minutes. **Windows** only gets the `WaitDelay` backstop (process-tree kill deferred).

issues.title: Add remote plugin install, index discovery, and plugin dependencies
issues.body:
https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/973

## Summary

Expands the kubectl-style external-command layer so users can discover and install plugins without cloning anything, from any git host. 18 files, ~5,540 insertions.

- **Remote install** — `entire plugin install <name|url|path>`. Newest **stable** semver tag via `git ls-remote` (forge-agnostic, inherits git auth and proxies; no forge REST client anywhere). Optional `entire-plugin.yml` metadata read via blobless shallow clone. Release assets download over HTTPS through a small per-host URL convention table (GitHub/Gitea-style, GitLab-style, `download_url` template escape hatch), selected and verified against the release's `checksums.txt`. Binaries land in `pkg/<name>/` with a provenance `manifest.yml`; `bin/` stays the only dispatch surface and the resolver in `plugin.go` is untouched.
- **Upgrade** — `entire plugin upgrade [name|--all]`, `--pin` to hold a tag, next-highest-tag fallback for pushed-but-unpublished releases, Windows locked-binary rename-aside.
- **Discovery** — krew-style git-synced index ([entireio/plugin-index](https://github.com/entireio/plugin-index)): shallow-cloned into the user cache keyed by URL hash, flock-guarded, 24h TTL, stale-copy-on-offline. Six new subcommands (`upgrade`, `search`, `info`, `browse`, `doctor`, `index update`) join the pre-existing `install`/`list`/`remove`; bare-name installs resolve through the index. Index URL: `--index` > `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_INDEX_URL` > built-in default.
- **Dependencies** — `entire-plugin.yml` `requires` (`name` + optional `min_version`, no ranges), resolved by name through the index. Install-time transitive planning, apt-style single confirmation, remove guard for depended-on plugins, and `entire plugin doctor`. Dispatch stays zero-cost — no runtime dependency checks.

## Security model

This code ends in downloading a binary and making it executable, so the trust boundaries are the design:

- **Transport.** HTTPS required for anything off-machine, re-validated on every redirect hop (Go follows redirects across schemes; validating only the entry point is bypassable). Loopback exempt so `httptest` fixtures work.
- **Authentication.** A release that publishes no `checksums.txt` for the platform is **refused by default**; `--allow-unverified` opts in, is recorded in the manifest, reported by `doctor`, and inherited by `upgrade`.
- **Integrity.** The installed binary's digest is recorded as `binary_sha256` and re-checked by `doctor`. (`sha256` covers the downloaded *asset*, which is discarded with the staging dir — provenance only.)
- **URLs reaching git.** Every repo/index URL is scheme-validated by one definition and every git invocation passes `--` before positionals. Repo URLs are attacker-influenced (index entries, `--index`, env), and git reads an option-shaped positional as an option — `--upload-pack`'s value is shell-interpreted.
- **The trust root is not repo-choosable.** The index URL cannot be set from committed settings; see below.
- **Names.** The installed name comes from the remote, so callers that already committed to a name pass it as a required argument and a mismatch is fatal.
- **Credentials.** Userinfo and query strings are stripped from every URL before printing, logging, or persisting (`.entire/logs/` is inside the working tree and `doctor bundle` collects it wholesale; `manifest.yml` is mode 0644).

Not claimed: **authenticity**. `checksums.txt` shares an origin with the asset, so it proves integrity in transit, not publisher identity. Real authenticity needs signatures.

## Design notes

- Built on the recorded founding decisions of this layer: PATH dispatch unchanged, built-ins win, `agent-` prefix reserved, env filtering untouched, no new telemetry.
- The only forge-specific code is the download-URL convention table; version listing, metadata, and the index all ride on the git protocol. No `go-github`-class dependency (uses existing `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` + `golang.org/x/mod`).
- **The plugin layer reads no settings at all.** The `settings` package is byte-identical to `main`.

## Changed since this description was first written

The branch was reviewed (Bugbot ×5 rounds, Copilot, four trail agent reviews, and a three-agent adversarial pass), then merged with `main` (2053 commits). Reviewers should know these are new:

**Behavior changes**
1. Checksums are now **required** by default (`--allow-unverified` opts out). Previously a release without them installed silently.
2. `http://` and `git://` are no longer accepted for repo or index URLs — unauthenticated transports, and the catalog decides what installs without a prompt.
3. Prereleases are excluded from tag resolution. `v2.0.0-rc1` outranks stable `v1.9.0` in semver, so `upgrade --all` was migrating users onto release candidates.

**Removals**
4. **`plugins.index_url` and `plugins.index_ttl_hours` are gone.** `.entire/settings.json` is committed and resolved from the working directory, while an index-listed plugin installs with *no prompt* — so a cloned repo could redirect the catalog and get an attacker-chosen binary onto `PATH` silently. The setting's value was that contributors got a different catalog *without knowing*, which is the vulnerability stated as a feature. Internal catalogs now use `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_INDEX_URL`, which applies across repos and cannot be chosen by checked-out content. Go takes the same position with `GOPROXY`; npm's per-project registry is the cautionary counter-example.
5. **`requires[].repo_url` is gone.** Dependencies resolve by name through the index, so a dependency's URL comes from the curated catalog rather than the requiring plugin's author — planning contacted that URL *before* the confirmation prompt. A user can still install an out-of-catalog dependency themselves, with the usual prompt; the authority moved to the user.

**Fixes worth naming**
6. Argument injection into the git CLI allowing arbitrary command execution from a malicious index entry or dependency URL — verified live on the pre-fix tree, on a path that never prompts.
7. `entire-plugin.yml` now decodes **leniently**. Strict decoding meant the first author to adopt any future field would break installs on every older CLI, permanently. This is also what made removals 4 and 5 migration-free for already-published files.
8. Silent truncation of archive entries over 512 MiB, index-cache races (now flock-guarded), a diamond `min_version` skip, `darwin_all` universal binaries never matching, empty `entire-plugin.yml` being fatal, `index_ttl_hours` overflowing to "always stale", and credential leaks through download errors.

## Testing

- 77 unit tests against `file://` git repos and `httptest` asset servers (zero real network in CI), covering tag resolution, asset selection/verification, extraction guards, index sync/TTL/offline/concurrency, dependency planning, doctor.
- 4 integration tests drive the spawned binary end to end (install/dispatch, unlisted-URL gating, dependencies + remove guard, search/info): bare-name install → real dispatch → dependency install → remove guard → doctor exit code. They run the **verified** path — no test passes `--allow-unverified`, so their passing is the proof that verification succeeds.
- Security regressions assert the stronger property where it matters: that an injected payload never executes and that credentials never appear, not merely that a call errors. Each was verified RED against the pre-fix tree.
- `mise run check` green (fmt, lint, unit + integration + Vogon canary).

## Docs

- `docs/architecture/external-commands.md` — remote install, plugin index, dependencies, and the trust-boundary sections.
- README — user-facing Plugins section.

## Open, deliberately

- `browse` and `index.json`'s `platforms` are candidates to cut — `browse` adds no capability over `search` + `install` and installs unprompted; `platforms` warns but never enforces.
- `min_version` is not enforced on the install *outcome* (the planner computes a constraint nothing downstream checks), and dependencies have no `auto_installed` marker, so orphans leak.
- Two notions of "official": the `officialPlugins` telemetry allowlist and `index.json`'s `official` flag.
- `entire upgrade` (the self-update plugin) vs `entire plugin upgrade` (plugins).
- Follow-up outside this branch: a credential-redaction pass at `main.go`'s error print. `%w`-wrapped `url.Error` leaks the full URL regardless of call-site discipline, because `net/url.Error.Error()` does no redaction.
- Outside this repo: `graph` should be added to `entireio/plugin-index`, or `entire plugin install brain` reports its dependency as unindexed.

issues.title: fix(checkpoint): serialize OPF ref updates
issues.body:
Fixes #2204

A native Git checkpoint writer and an OPF rewrite could both read the same ref value and then both report a successful update. The OPF paths used go-git's compare-and-swap, which does not participate in native Git's reference-locking protocol. A native transaction could therefore commit after the OPF rewrite and silently discard it.

## The fix

Introduce `gitrepo.CompareAndSwapRef`, a shared direct-ref compare-and-swap built on a native `git update-ref --stdin` transaction. The transaction prepares the update first, acquiring Git's ref lock, verifies that the ref is not symbolic while that lock is held, and then commits.

The native helper now backs:

- shadow-branch updates
- all persistent-ref writers using `updatePersistentRef`, including the Stop hook
- both OPF rewrite paths: the shared v1 ref and per-checkpoint refs

The OPF scan remains outside the ref transaction. Its final CAS uses the value observed before the scan, so a concurrent update is rejected instead of overwritten.

`CASPersistentRef` deliberately does not acquire Entire's persistent-writer flock. Its expected value predates the call, and native Git is the correctness boundary. Avoiding the flock also prevents deadline-free pre-push operations from waiting indefinitely. Transient native lock contention is retried with a bounded budget; a genuine stale-value conflict is terminal.

## Transaction and failure behavior

The separate `git symbolic-ref` invocation is deliberate. Git does not allow `symref-verify` and an update of the same ref in one transaction because it treats them as multiple updates to that ref. Preparing the native update first keeps the ref locked while the symbolic-ref probe runs, closing the conversion race.

CAS error classification recognizes only Git's exact stale-value diagnostics. Corrupt refs, unreadable refs, namespace conflicts, and other permanent failures retain their underlying diagnosis rather than being mislabeled and retried. The v1 rewrite reports `V1RefMovedError` only after a successful reread confirms that the ref actually changed.

Cancellation closes the transaction's stdin so Git can abort cleanly. A three-second `WaitDelay` bounds shutdown if a hook or inherited pipe prevents the process from exiting.

## Performance

Routing the shared write path through the transaction increases a measured ref update from 13.4 ms to 22.0 ms—an 8.6 ms cost per update. That is under 1% of the roughly 3-second p50 Stop-hook latency.

The extra symbolic-ref process is required for the direct-ref guarantee described above; it is not an accidental round trip.

## Verification

Regression tests use real native Git transactions and cover both files and reftable repositories. They exercise:

- both OPF lost-update races
- symbolic-ref rejection and concurrent symbolic conversion
- native lock contention and bounded retry behavior
- cancellation and lock release
- malformed, corrupt, unreadable, and namespace-conflicting refs
- preservation of the original failure when a v1 ref cannot be reread

The focused race tests passed ten consecutive runs.

`mise run check` passed after the review fixes, including formatting, lint, race-enabled unit and integration tests, and the Vogon and Roger-Roger canary suites.

issues.title: Add `entire trace` command to find slow performance hooks etc.
issues.body:
## `entire trace` command

Adds a new `entire trace` CLI command that displays hook performance traces, and extends the `perf/span` package with loop iteration tracking.

### New command: `entire trace`

Parses structured perf log entries from `.entire/logs/entire.log` and renders them as formatted timing tables with hierarchical sub-step breakdowns.

- `entire trace` — show the most recent hook trace
- `entire trace --last 5` — show the last 5 traces
- `entire trace --hook post-commit` — filter by hook type

Traces require `ENTIRE_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG` to be enabled.

**Implementation** (`cmd/entire/cli/trace.go`, `trace_cmd.go`):

- JSONL log parser that extracts `steps.*_ms` and `steps.*_err` keys into a hierarchical step tree
- Sub-step detection: keys like `foo.0`, `foo.1` are nested under their parent `foo` when the parent exists
- ASCII tree rendering (`├─`/`└─`) with manual padding to avoid UTF-8 multi-byte alignment issues
- Input validation on `--last` flag (must be >= 1)

Example output:

```
❯ entire trace --hook post-commit --last 2
post-commit  123ms  2026-03-06T16:35:48-08:00

  STEP                        DURATION
  cleanup_shadow_branches         12ms
  find_sessions_for_worktree       0ms
  open_repository_and_head         0ms
  process_sessions               100ms
    ├─ process_sessions.0          3ms
    ├─ process_sessions.1          0ms
    ├─ process_sessions.2         95ms
    └─ process_sessions.3          0ms
  resolve_commit_trees             5ms
```

### `perf/span`: LoopSpan and child deduplication

Extends the span package to support tracking loop iterations as grouped sub-spans.

- **`LoopSpan`** — wraps a grouping span; `Iteration()` creates child spans, `End()` auto-ends unfinished iterations
- **`childStepKey()`** — deduplicates child span names (`.1`, `.2` suffixes) so repeated loop iterations don't overwrite each other in log output
- **Grandchild emission** — group spans emit their children as `steps.<name>.<index>_ms` entries with 0-based indexing

### Hook integration

`PostCommit` in `manual_commit_hooks.go` now wraps the session processing loop with `StartLoop`/`Iteration`/`End` to emit per-session timing in traces.

`openCodeMsgToken` declared only `input` and `output`:

```go
type openCodeMsgToken struct {
    Input  int `json:"input"`

}
```

OpenCode exports also carry `reasoning`, `cache.read`, `cache.write`, `total` and a per-message `modelID`. `openCodeRecord` therefore wrote a `CallUsage` with only two fields, and the stored transcript line dropped the rest. Readers of a checkpoint transcript saw:

instead of cache read 100, cache write 160 and the model the export reported. Every other adapter keeps what its agent records.

Reasoning has the same problem in a second form: 1.3.16+ stores it apart from output, while older or provider-specific messages already include it. The condensed line's `reasoning_tokens` is a subset of `output_tokens`, so it has to be counted exactly once.

## Reproduction

On `main`, `TestCompact_OpenCodeUsageKeepsCacheReasoningAndModel` produces `cache_read_tokens: 0, cache_write_tokens: 0, reasoning_tokens: 0` and no `model`, although the input export carries `cache:{read:5,write:2}`, `reasoning:40` and `modelID`.

The existing `TestCompact_OpenCodeTokenUsage` input also has cache read 100 / write 160; its expected line omitted both, pinning the loss.

- Parse `reasoning`, `cache`, `total` and `modelID` from the export.
- Populate `CallUsage` with cache read/write, reasoning and model.
- Compute output with the same identity the OpenCode agent already uses in `Tokens.OutputWithReasoning`: if `total == input + output + cache.read + cache.write`, reasoning is already inside output; otherwise add it. `reasoning_tokens` then stays a subset of `output_tokens`.

The existing golden fixture is regenerated: every assistant line gains its model and cache counts, and no message in it has reasoning stored apart, so its output counts are unchanged.

- New `TestCompact_OpenCodeUsageKeepsCacheReasoningAndModel` covers reasoning stored apart (80 + 40 → 120), reasoning already inside output (total identity → 90), cache counts and model.

## Summary

Write-side fixes for the token data behind `session tokens`, `checkpoint tokens`, and `tokens profile`. This PR makes the numbers written into checkpoints correct and complete; the report redesign follows in a separate PR off main. **One visible change:** `entire status`' per-session token total is now the session total again (see review fix 2 below) — everything else is metadata only.

Five commits, each independently reviewable:

### 1. `fix(tokens)`: Gemini and OpenCode parsers
- **Gemini** counted `cached` twice (it is a subset of `input`) and dropped `thoughts` (reported outside `output`). Real committed checkpoints were inflated 58–89%, with output understated 34–47%. Fresh input is now `input − cached + tool`; output is `output + thoughts`.
- **OpenCode** ignored `reasoning`, which is outside `output` in some versions and inside in others (7,456 vs 2,991 assistant messages in this repo's history). `Tokens.BilledOutput()` uses the per-message `total` identity to count it exactly once.
- Verified against every committed Gemini (19/19) and OpenCode (116/116) transcript on `entire/checkpoints/v1`: the four classes now sum to the provider's own total on all of them.

### 2. `fix(strategy)`: checkpoint `token_usage` gets its own window
`carryForwardToNewShadowBranch` resets `CheckpointTranscriptStart` to 0 after a partial commit (deliberately, for a self-contained transcript). Checkpoint tokens were computed from the same offset, so every post-carry-forward checkpoint re-reported the **whole session's** tokens: 53% of non-first checkpoints in this repo's history, 65% of all cache-read tokens ever recorded are re-counts, and anything summing `token_usage` was inflated 2–3×. `SessionState.TokenTranscriptStart` now scopes tokens; `advanceTranscriptWindows` moves both offsets at every condensation site; carry-forward resets only the transcript one. Legacy state files migrate on load.

### 3. `feat(tokens)`: persist what the agents already record
- `types.TokenUsage` gains `thinking_tokens` (⊂ `output_tokens`) and `cache_creation_1h_tokens` (⊂ `cache_creation_tokens`), both `omitempty`, **read verbatim from agent fields, never inferred** — Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini for thinking; Claude Code and Pi for the 1-hour cache TTL (priced 2× vs 1.25×; sessions are usually all-one-or-the-other). Plus `model` on subagent entries so cost can be weighted per model.
- `AddTokenUsage` / `SubtractTokenUsage` / `accumulateTokenUsage` carry the new fields at every nesting level; Claude's subagent aggregation goes through `AddTokenUsage` instead of a field-by-field loop.
- Root `metadata.json` stamps `token_usage_version: 2` once no pre-delta row is left in the checkpoint (see review fix 3). Absent = legacy checkpoint whose `token_usage` may be a session-cumulative total.

### 4. `feat(checkpoint)`: persist `token_transcript_start`
Each session's `metadata.json` now records where its token window began. Without it a reader attributing a checkpoint's tokens from the stored `full.jsonl` had nothing to slice at — `checkpoint_transcript_start` is reset to 0 by carry-forward, so slicing there would re-create the cumulative bug. Written by `token_usage_version ≥ 2` CLIs, but presence is not a version marker: `omitempty` drops it at offset 0, so a session's first checkpoint omits it too; absent decodes as 0, which is the correct start in exactly those cases.

## Review findings addressed (trail 1167)

All six findings raised on the trail, each with a regression test:

1. **HIGH — tokens in the post-commit tail belonged to no checkpoint** (`manual_commit_hooks.go`). After a complete mid-turn commit, condensation wrote the checkpoint's `token_usage` over `[TokenStart, N]` and `finalizeAllTurnCheckpoints` then rewrote that checkpoint with the transcript only — no token recompute. The turn-end advance moved *both* offsets to the turn end M, so the tokens in `(N, M]` — the tool results, token counts and `task_complete` that land after the commit, which for Codex is the turn's whole accounting — were recorded nowhere. The turn-end advance now moves only the stored-transcript offset, via the new `advanceStoredTranscriptWindow`; the token window stays where condensation left it, the same separation carry-forward already makes.
2. **`entire status` reported a checkpoint delta as the session total** (`manual_commit_condensation.go`). `applyBackfilledSessionTokenUsage` adopted `checkpointUsage` — a per-checkpoint delta since this PR — as `state.TokenUsage`, the session accumulator `entire status` reads. Pre-existing (the fallback predates this PR), but this PR removed the accident that repaired it. `sessionStateBackfillTokenUsage` now reports whether its value is session-wide; only a session-wide recompute may replace the accumulator, and the delta stays a last-resort fill for a session that never accumulated one.
3. **`token_usage_version: 2` was asserted over legacy rows** (`checkpoint/persistent.go`, `checkpoint/fsstore`). The stamp was unconditional, so a CLI upgrade between two writes to one checkpoint claimed the delta scope for sessions whose `token_usage` is still cumulative, and readers skipped the dedupe those rows need. New shared policy `ResolveTokenUsageVersion`: the summary reports the weakest guarantee across its rows — the delta version only once no older row survives the write.
4. **A load-bearing doc comment had been reattached to the wrong function** (`manual_commit_git.go`). `advanceTranscriptWindows` was inserted between `resetCheckpointWindow` and its comment (the `SubagentTokensBaseline` rescoping plus the #2058 task-record "single post-write mutation site" contract). Moved below; both functions now carry their own docs.
5. **OpenCode thinking tokens could exceed output tokens** (`agent/opencode`). `BilledOutput()` folds reasoning in only when the per-message `total` identity confirms it is billed separately; the caller added `reasoning` unconditionally, so a message with no `total` could report more thinking than output and make a reader's "non-thinking output" negative. Reasoning is now capped at the output actually counted. Hardening — `total` is present on all 116 committed transcripts.
6. **Docs claimed `token_transcript_start` presence marks v2** — corrected in the field comment and `sessions-and-checkpoints.md` (see above).

## Found while fixing those (pre-push self-review)

7. **Imported turns declared a token window of 0.** `agentimport.writeTurn` set `checkpoint_transcript_start` but never `token_transcript_start`, while every turn of an imported session stores the same whole-session transcript and `turn.Tokens` is a per-turn delta over `[LineStart, LineEnd)`. Each turn is written as a single-session checkpoint, so it stamps `token_usage_version: 2` — meaning a reader obeying the contract this PR reinforces would recompute turn 40 of a 50-turn import from line 0 and re-report the session's cumulative total. The turn's own `LineStart` is now recorded; an import has no carry-forward, so the two windows coincide.

Fixes ENT-2463.

## Problem

An agent that starts in the main checkout and moves into a linked worktree (Claude Code's `EnterWorktree`, which creates `.claude/worktrees/…`) stays homed in the main checkout. When it commits from the linked worktree, no session is homed there, so worktree matching falls back to every session of the main checkout. The shortcuts that skip content checks then condense every one of those sessions that is mid-turn into the agent's commit. These shortcuts are the no-TTY fast path, content detection by transcript growth, and post-commit ACTIVE condensation. The result is one checkpoint that holds the committer's session plus unrelated sessions from the main checkout, and the trail shows all of them.

Reproduced on the 0.10.7 release and on current main. #2668 hides the unrelated session only while that session's agent is still running.

## Fix

In `findSessionsForCommitLinking`: when process ancestry identifies the committer and no session is homed in the committing worktree, the fallback's matches are dropped.
- A session from another worktree joins only through its record of this worktree (`hasWorktreeEntry`, from #2531), and is held to those edits (`LinkedByWorktreeEntry`).
- Sessions homed in the committing worktree still join alongside the identified committer, as before.
- A commit with no identified committer (Windows, no recorded owner) keeps the fallback unchanged.

`findSessionsForWorktreeFromStates` now reports whether its result came from the fallback. Amend restore and post-rewrite (`findSessionsForWorktree`) are unchanged.

- An identified committer in a sibling worktree, and in a worktree nested under the main checkout, links only itself plus a main-checkout session that recorded edits there. That session is flagged `LinkedByWorktreeEntry`.
- An identified committer homed in a third worktree, where the fallback would otherwise pick the main checkout's recent session.
- Through `PrepareCommitMsg` + `PostCommit`: the committer is stamped and condensed, and a mid-turn main-checkout session with pending work is not condensed into the checkpoint.

Guards that also pass without the fix:

## What was missing

OpenCode child sessions and Factory AI Droid Workers keep their token usage in their own sessions. The parent's transcript never includes it, so it was missing from every total: status, sessions, session tokens, attach and checkpoint metadata. The `entire explain` header total also left out subagents.

## The fix

- A child is credited exactly once, in the same locked state change that completes its task record.
- The credit goes to a new summed field, `ChildSessionTokens`. It stays separate from `TokenUsage.SubagentTokens`, which each turn's snapshot replaces, so a later snapshot cannot erase a Worker.
- A bounded ledger, `CreditedChildCalls` (last 256), survives condensation. It is keyed like completion-record keying: call ID, child and start. A stop repeated after condensation is not credited again. A reused call ID with a new start is still credited. An unknown start on either side matches any entry for the same child and call.
- OpenCode declares `agent.ChildSessionSubagents`, so every completion of its children credits, including the SessionEnd sweep's completion of a child still running when the session ends. The sweep records the call's start as unknown, and an unknown start on either side matches in the ledger, so a later stop adds nothing. Droid Worker turns are credited on the existing per-turn path.
- A child's task entry is not recounted from its transcript at condensation, so task.json shows the same figure the parent was credited. A child whose export failed keeps no usage in either place.
- Checkpoints add the pending child share to their subagent total. Displays use `SessionState.TotalTokenUsage()`.
- `entire explain` now counts subagents in its header total.

## Overlaps

- #2820 (merged): `TestFactoryDroidWorkerTokensComeFromItsOwnSettings` now also checks that `TotalTokenUsage()` counts the Worker once.
- #2782: if totals later switch to cumulative sources, OpenCode children must keep this credit, and Droid Workers must not be added a second time.

## Known limits

- A child the SessionEnd sweep completes while it is still running counts only the usage its export held at that moment.
- Tasks launched inside an OpenCode child are still skipped, both files and tokens.
- Sessions that were already condensed are not backfilled.
- After `entire session attach`, a child's tokens go into the attach checkpoint while its task.json goes into the next one. Nothing is counted twice.

## Tests

New strategy, session, explain and integration tests. Each one fails on main, and the ledger tests also fail without the ledger. `mise run test:integration` and the canary pass, and lint reports 0 issues.

An OpenCode session whose background subagent is still running can now be credited for a commit that another session also claims, whether the parent is IDLE or still in its turn (ACTIVE).

A running subagent's edits reach the parent's tracked files only when it stops. Until then, post-commit's read-only gate asks the live task records whether they touched a committed file (`liveTaskFilesInCommit`). It read only transcripts on disk, and a running OpenCode child has none (its transcript exists only through `opencode export`), so the parent was skipped as read-only and the commit lost its link to that session.

## Changes

- New `agent.LiveSubagentFileReporter`: reports the files a running subagent call has modified so far. OpenCode implements it by exporting the child to a private staging file, cutting it to the running call, and removing it. Only completed tool parts count: a pending, running or failed edit is no evidence. It writes nothing a capture reads, so a report that finishes after the call's stop cannot replace the stop's complete transcript.
- `liveTaskFilesInCommit` uses the reporter for a live record with no transcript on disk. A report that fails, or runs out of budget, is no evidence.
- Fetch budgets: the co-authorship checks of all a commit's sessions share 10s, counted from the start of post-commit's session loop, so a hung export there cannot hold the commit. Condensation's re-exports of completed tasks keep their own 30s per session (`agent.SubagentFetchBudget`), as on `main`.
- The gate is memoized per session (`sync.OnceValue`), since each consultation may export.
- prepare-commit-msg's check of a foreign session's running subagents shares the same 10s deadline, so a slow or hung export cannot hold up `git commit` either.
- The gate's evidence applies to an ACTIVE parent too (`hasFreshLiveTaskRecord`: any phase but ENDED), for every agent. A parent keeps working after launching a background subagent. For OpenCode this is what credits it at all, since its live transcript does not include its children; for Claude and others it applies when the parent's own transcript does not yet show the subagent's files and its on-disk transcript names a committed file. When to skip the overlap check is unchanged (`idleWithLiveTaskRecord`, IDLE only).
- Docs: OpenCode `AGENT.md` and `sessions-and-checkpoints.md`, including that a still-running subagent credits its session again on a later commit of the same file (as Claude's on-disk transcripts do on main).

A commit made outside the parent's agent process (a terminal, another window) goes through #2668's foreign-session checks. #2668 has merged, and this PR switches both of them (the prepare-commit-msg staged-file overlap and post-commit's `liveTaskCoauthored`) to `hasFreshLiveTaskRecord`, so an ACTIVE parent's running subagent counts there too, as #2668 already allowed for an IDLE one.

This redoes the co-authorship part cut from #2390, rebuilt on what landed there: `readTaskTranscript` no longer re-exports live records, so the check uses its own non-writing probe instead.

## Tests

- Live-tested with OpenCode 1.18.33 (`opencode serve`, gpt-5.6-luna): an IDLE parent whose background child rewrote a file the coder session also claimed, committed while the child was still running: main 1 session, this PR 2; with #2668 merged in, also 2 (both sessions foreign). The condensation path in `CondenseSession()` had three issues:

1. **Redundant redaction** — The same transcript was redacted up to 3 times during a v2 condensation: once in `CondenseSession` for the compact transcript input, once in `GitStore.writeTranscript` for v1, and once in `V2GitStore.writeTranscriptBlobs` for v2 full transcript.

2. **Scattered v2 checks** — `settings.IsCheckpointsV2Enabled(ctx)` was checked in `CondenseSession`, again redundantly inside `compactTranscriptForV2`, and in `writeCommittedV2IfEnabled`.

3. **Implicit redaction contracts** — The `compact` package and checkpoint stores accepted raw `[]byte` transcripts with no indication of whether redaction had been applied. The expectation that data should be redacted was implicit and undocumented.

## Solution

Introduce `redact.RedactedBytes` — an opaque struct type (unexported `data` field) that can only be produced by `redact.JSONLBytes()` or the escape-hatch `redact.AlreadyRedacted()` for trusted sources. This establishes compile-time contracts at package boundaries:

- **`compact.Compact`** accepts `RedactedBytes`, enforcing that only redacted transcripts are compacted
- **`WriteCommittedOptions.Transcript`** and **`UpdateCommittedOptions.Transcript`** use `RedactedBytes`, documenting the store contract
- **`replaceTranscript`** and **`writeTranscriptBlobs`** accept `RedactedBytes` at the function parameter level, preventing unredacted writes to permanent storage

### Key changes

- **`CondenseSession`** redacts the transcript once early, then passes the single `RedactedBytes` result to both the compact path and the checkpoint stores — eliminating 2 redundant redaction passes
- **Store write paths** (`writeTranscript`, `writeTranscriptBlobs`, `replaceTranscript`, `UpdateCommitted`) no longer redact internally for in-memory data. The `TranscriptPath` file-read fallback retains its own redaction since data from disk is untrusted
- **`attach.go`** now explicitly redacts before calling `WriteCommitted` (previously relied on store-internal redaction)
- **`compactTranscriptForV2`** accepts `RedactedBytes` and drops the redundant `IsCheckpointsV2Enabled` guard (both callers already check)
- **Hooks finalize path** propagates `RedactedBytes` end-to-end instead of stripping to `[]byte` and re-wrapping

### Safety

If transcript redaction fails in `CondenseSession`, the transcript is dropped rather than persisting potentially sensitive content. The checkpoint metadata (files touched, attributions, etc.) is still written — only the transcript is omitted.

<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## What was missing

No agent stored a subagent's model. Subagent tokens were priced at the parent's model, even when a subagent ran on a cheaper or more expensive one.

## The change

`TokenUsage` gains `Model` and `ByModel` (JSON `model` and `by_model`). An entry from one model carries `model`. An entry from several models carries a `by_model` split, which always sums to the entry. A model that was not recorded counts as its own `""` bucket.

Where the model comes from:

- Claude Code: `message.model` in each subagent transcript, including subagents launched by subagents (read in the same pass that counts their usage).
- Codex: `turn_context.model` in the child rollout. A child that stays on one model labels its exact total. A child that switches is split by how much the cumulative snapshot grew under each model. If the snapshot shrinks across a switch, the total stays unlabelled.
- OpenCode: per-message `modelID` in the child export. Buckets key on `modelID` alone, so the same model from two providers is one entry.
- Factory Droid Workers: the Worker's own turn-end model, read from its settings file.
- Cursor: `subagent_model` from `subagentStart` is stored on the task record (`task.json` `subagent_model`). Cursor reports no subagent tokens, so there is nothing to label. Placeholders like `auto` and `default` are dropped.

## Merge rules

- Adding merges per model. A sum over different models becomes a split; a zero entry never makes a sum mixed.
- Subtracting a baseline works per model. If the same model shrank, the excess is taken from the other models, so the split still sums to the delta. If the baseline spent tokens on a model the snapshot lacks (a baseline from before models were recorded, or a child that went away), the delta is left unlabelled. We cannot tell which model it belongs to.
- A `by_model` read back from a pushed blob is checked. If it does not sum to its entry, sits next to a `model`, or has more than 32 entries, the entry is treated as unlabelled counts.
- Session accumulation and the Droid in-transcript subagent sum now go through `AddTokenUsage`, so a split stays consistent with the totals.
- `types.LabelModel(usage, model)` labels usage whose model comes from a hook payload or settings file.

## Cumulative token counters (#2782)

Since #2782, a session's checkpoint tokens come from its token ledger and the per-agent usage counters. They now keep subagent models too:
- The Claude Code counter labels each subagent call with its message's model (first fragment naming one, `<synthetic>` skipped); the main agent's calls stay unlabelled. Codex children were already labelled; Droid Workers and OpenCode children reach the checkpoint through the child-session credit, already labelled.
- The ledger's checkpointed mark keeps the labels: when the new total covers the mark on every count, it becomes the mark as is; otherwise the per-field maximum (unlabelled) is kept as before. Counts are unchanged.
- `usageCursorVersion` 4 → 5, so cursors cached before models were recorded are read again. A mismatched cursor is a fresh read, not a restart, and the checkpointed marks are ledger fields, so nothing is counted twice. Costs: one full re-read of each live session's transcripts (all agents), and the first checkpoint after upgrading stores its subagent delta unlabelled (its baseline has no label); later ones are labelled.
- `TokenUsage` is no longer comparable with `==` (its split is a slice): the Codex counter compares snapshots field by field.

Tests: the Claude Code counter (`TestUsageCounter_SubagentModels`), the ledger (`TestTokenLedger_SubagentModels`), and an integration case with subagents in three successive checkpoints whose labels survive every mark (fails without the mark change).

## Not in this PR

Copilot CLI is deferred until #2760. That PR keeps Copilot child tokens inside the main total, so a per-child model would price nothing yet.

## Overlaps

- #2820 and #2824 (both merged): the Worker's labelled usage is what #2824 credits to the parent, so its model reaches the parent's `subagent_tokens`. `TestFactoryDroidWorkerTokensComeFromItsOwnSettings` now checks the model on the task and on the parent's total.
- #2782: merges cleanly.
- Transcript library (#2858, #2859, #2862): its per-call `model` and usage on `transcript.jsonl` lines and this PR's per-model totals agree. A streamed Claude Code message takes the first fragment's model in both, and `TestSubagentUsageByModelMatchesTranscriptLibrary` (Claude Code) and `TestChildUsageByModelMatchesTranscriptLibrary` (Codex, with a model switch) run one transcript through both and require equal per-model totals. ## Summary

Write-side fixes for the token data behind `session tokens`, `checkpoint tokens`, and `tokens profile`. This PR makes the numbers written into checkpoints correct and complete; the report redesign follows in a separate PR off main. **One visible change:** `entire status`' per-session token total is now the session total again (see review fix 2 below) — everything else is metadata only.

Five commits, each independently reviewable:

### 1. `fix(tokens)`: Gemini and OpenCode parsers
- **Gemini** counted `cached` twice (it is a subset of `input`) and dropped `thoughts` (reported outside `output`). Real committed checkpoints were inflated 58–89%, with output understated 34–47%. Fresh input is now `input − cached + tool`; output is `output + thoughts`.
- **OpenCode** ignored `reasoning`, which is outside `output` in some versions and inside in others (7,456 vs 2,991 assistant messages in this repo's history). `Tokens.BilledOutput()` uses the per-message `total` identity to count it exactly once.
- Verified against every committed Gemini (19/19) and OpenCode (116/116) transcript on `entire/checkpoints/v1`: the four classes now sum to the provider's own total on all of them.

### 2. `fix(strategy)`: checkpoint `token_usage` gets its own window
`carryForwardToNewShadowBranch` resets `CheckpointTranscriptStart` to 0 after a partial commit (deliberately, for a self-contained transcript). Checkpoint tokens were computed from the same offset, so every post-carry-forward checkpoint re-reported the **whole session's** tokens: 53% of non-first checkpoints in this repo's history, 65% of all cache-read tokens ever recorded are re-counts, and anything summing `token_usage` was inflated 2–3×. `SessionState.TokenTranscriptStart` now scopes tokens; `advanceTranscriptWindows` moves both offsets at every condensation site; carry-forward resets only the transcript one. Legacy state files migrate on load.

### 3. `feat(tokens)`: persist what the agents already record
- `types.TokenUsage` gains `thinking_tokens` (⊂ `output_tokens`) and `cache_creation_1h_tokens` (⊂ `cache_creation_tokens`), both `omitempty`, **read verbatim from agent fields, never inferred** — Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini for thinking; Claude Code and Pi for the 1-hour cache TTL (priced 2× vs 1.25×; sessions are usually all-one-or-the-other). Plus `model` on subagent entries so cost can be weighted per model.
- `AddTokenUsage` / `SubtractTokenUsage` / `accumulateTokenUsage` carry the new fields at every nesting level; Claude's subagent aggregation goes through `AddTokenUsage` instead of a field-by-field loop.
- Root `metadata.json` stamps `token_usage_version: 2` once no pre-delta row is left in the checkpoint (see review fix 3). Absent = legacy checkpoint whose `token_usage` may be a session-cumulative total.

### 4. `feat(checkpoint)`: persist `token_transcript_start`
Each session's `metadata.json` now records where its token window began. Without it a reader attributing a checkpoint's tokens from the stored `full.jsonl` had nothing to slice at — `checkpoint_transcript_start` is reset to 0 by carry-forward, so slicing there would re-create the cumulative bug. Written by `token_usage_version ≥ 2` CLIs, but presence is not a version marker: `omitempty` drops it at offset 0, so a session's first checkpoint omits it too; absent decodes as 0, which is the correct start in exactly those cases.

## Review findings addressed (trail 1167)

All six findings raised on the trail, each with a regression test:

1. **HIGH — tokens in the post-commit tail belonged to no checkpoint** (`manual_commit_hooks.go`). After a complete mid-turn commit, condensation wrote the checkpoint's `token_usage` over `[TokenStart, N]` and `finalizeAllTurnCheckpoints` then rewrote that checkpoint with the transcript only — no token recompute. The turn-end advance moved *both* offsets to the turn end M, so the tokens in `(N, M]` — the tool results, token counts and `task_complete` that land after the commit, which for Codex is the turn's whole accounting — were recorded nowhere. The turn-end advance now moves only the stored-transcript offset, via the new `advanceStoredTranscriptWindow`; the token window stays where condensation left it, the same separation carry-forward already makes.
2. **`entire status` reported a checkpoint delta as the session total** (`manual_commit_condensation.go`). `applyBackfilledSessionTokenUsage` adopted `checkpointUsage` — a per-checkpoint delta since this PR — as `state.TokenUsage`, the session accumulator `entire status` reads. 3. **`token_usage_version: 2` was asserted over legacy rows** (`checkpoint/persistent.go`, `checkpoint/fsstore`). The stamp was unconditional, so a CLI upgrade between two writes to one checkpoint claimed the delta scope for sessions whose `token_usage` is still cumulative, and readers skipped the dedupe those rows need. 4. **A load-bearing doc comment had been reattached to the wrong function** (`manual_commit_git.go`). `advanceTranscriptWindows` was inserted between `resetCheckpointWindow` and its comment (the `SubagentTokensBaseline` rescoping plus the #2058 task-record "single post-write mutation site" contract). 5. **OpenCode thinking tokens could exceed output tokens** (`agent/opencode`). `BilledOutput()` folds reasoning in only when the per-message `total` identity confirms it is billed separately; the caller added `reasoning` unconditionally, so a message with no `total` could report more thinking than output and make a reader's "non-thinking output" negative. Reasoning is now capped at the output actually counted. Hardening — `total` is present on all 116 committed transcripts.
6. **Docs claimed `token_transcript_start` presence marks v2** — corrected in the field comment and `sessions-and-checkpoints.md` (see above).

## Found while fixing those (pre-push self-review)

7. **Imported turns declared a token window of 0.** `agentimport.writeTurn` set `checkpoint_transcript_start` but never `token_transcript_start`, while every turn of an imported session stores the same whole-session transcript and `turn.Tokens` is a per-turn delta over `[LineStart, LineEnd)`. Each turn is written as a single-session checkpoint, so it stamps `token_usage_version: 2` — meaning a reader obeying the contract this PR reinforces would recompute turn 40 of a 50-turn import from line 0 and re-report the session's cumulative total. The turn's own `LineStart` is now recorded; an import has no carry-forward, so the two windows coincide.
8. **The new offset divergence did not survive a state reload.** `NormalizeAfterLoad` re-couples the token window to the transcript window whenever `token_transcript_start` is 0 and `checkpoint_transcript_start` is not — which is exactly the shape the turn-end advance produces for a session whose window legitimately still starts at line 0 (`omitempty` drops the 0, so "absent" and "deliberate 0" were indistinguishable). `SessionState.TokenWindowInitialized` now marks a window this CLI maintains, so the legacy migration only fires on files that predate the field.

| `strategy/manual_commit_condensation.go` | 1 new `case` |
| `activity_cmd.go` | 1 map entry |

Nothing routes through Goose unless a user runs `entire enable --agent goose`. The four `AgentType` switches I touched are the ones with no compile-time exhaustiveness check, where a missing case degrades to `Unknown` in silence, so I wired all four rather than leaving a latent gap.

## Design: Goose keeps sessions in SQLite

`goose info` reports the store at `~/.local/share/goose/sessions/sessions.db`. The binary carries in-place `ALTER TABLE` migrations for at least four columns, so reading that schema would couple us to something the vendor rewrites under us.

The integration follows the OpenCode pattern instead. It reads through `goose session export --format json` and restores through `goose session import`, and never opens the database. `--format json` is not optional: export defaults to markdown, which is lossy and cannot be imported back.

![hooks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Ar9av/cli/assets-goose/goose/04-hooks.png)

## What the docs got wrong

I installed goose v1.46.0 and round-tripped a transcript through an isolated `XDG_DATA_HOME` to capture the export schema. Three findings that guessing would have missed:

1. **The message array is `conversation`, not `messages`.** OpenCode's analogous export uses `messages`. Copying that shape yields an empty transcript with no error.
2. **Cache token fields disagree between layers.** The export spells them `cache_read_input_tokens` and `cache_write_input_tokens`; the SQLite columns behind them are `cache_read_tokens` and `cache_write_tokens`.
3. **Tool names arrive in more than one spelling.** Goose namespaces tools as `<extension>__<tool>` at runtime, but the Almanac records a live-verified case where a hook received the bare name, so a matcher on the documented spelling never fires. File extraction matches on suffix and accepts the bare, namespaced, and import-inherited spellings.

`AGENT.md` in the new package records the protocol with per-claim provenance, tagging each fact `[verified]` (observed from the binary) or `[documented]` (read from docs, not executed).

Chunking and reassembly operate on a raw field map rather than the modelled struct, so top-level keys the package does not describe survive a round trip instead of vanishing on every checkpoint. A test asserts this against the real export.

## Verification

`gofmt`, `golangci-lint` 2.11.3, `go test -race ./cmd/...`, the integration suite, and the Vogon E2E canary all pass.

Beyond that I ran the agent end to end against a built binary. Firing `session-start`, `turn-start` and `turn-end` produced a checkpoint carrying the right commit trailer, the extracted file list, and a transcript that reads back out through `checkpoint explain`. Token totals match the export exactly: input 124.6k, cache read 112.8k, cache write 11.8k, output 394.

![status](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Ar9av/cli/assets-goose/goose/02-status.png)

![explain](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Ar9av/cli/assets-goose/goose/03-explain.png)

The 40+ unit tests include a genuine v1.46.0 export committed as `testdata/real_export_v1_46_0.json`, which guards the field names above. `security_contract_test.go` pins the path-component guard on `ResolveSessionFile` and on both session-id entry points.

## Three things to push back on

1. **`CalculateTokenUsage` ignores its `fromOffset` argument.** Goose reports usage as session-level totals with no per-message block to scope by, so the method returns the session total whatever offset it gets. The method comment says so and a test pins it, but it deviates from the interface contract and a reviewer may want a different shape.
2. **The hook payload is `[documented]`, not `[verified]`.** Firing a hook needs a configured model provider (`goose doctor` reports none), so I could not execute one here. The payload shape and native tool names come from docs plus the Almanac's live test on v1.44.0. No `e2e/` harness ships for the same reason.
3. **I set `IsPreview() = true` and left `agent-help` classification alone.** CLAUDE.md calls those product judgments, so I took the safe default and am flagging both rather than deciding them.

Adds **Devin CLI** ("Devin for Terminal", Cognition) as a supported Entire agent (Preview): `cmd/entire/cli/agent/devin/` plus registry/resume/hook-command wiring, a cross-fire guard, docs, and full unit tests. Every behavioral assumption was **verified against a live devin 3000.2.17** install — captured payloads, transcript format, flush timing, and a full end-to-end checkpoint flow. The findings live in `cmd/entire/cli/agent/devin/AGENT.md`.

## How it works

- **Hooks**: Devin natively supports Claude Code-format hooks. Entire installs into `.devin/hooks.v1.json` (the hooks object is the whole file): `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `Stop`, `SessionEnd`, and `PostToolUse` scoped by matcher `^(write|edit|notebook_edit)$`.
- **No transcript_path in payloads**: `SessionRef` is derived from the session ID → `~/.local/share/devin/cli/transcripts/<session_id>.json` (flat layout, `%APPDATA%\devin\cli\transcripts` on Windows, XDG honored).
- **Transcript**: ATIF-v1.7 JSON. Chunking splits the `steps` array (OpenCode pattern); token usage comes from per-step `metrics` (`prompt_tokens` includes cache reads → `input = prompt - cached`); `ModelExtractor` backfills the model (e.g. `SWE-1.7`).
- **Flush timing**: Devin writes the transcript only when a session run ends. `PrepareTranscript` polls for the post-Stop flush (print mode) and otherwise materializes a minimal ATIF stub so per-turn checkpoints proceed; the eager condensation at SessionEnd captures the complete transcript.
- **Live file tracking**: `PostToolUse` → `ToolUse` events populate `files_touched` mid-turn (the transcript can't, since it lags) — this is what makes mid-session commits link via the `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer.
- **Cross-fire guard**: Devin loads `.claude/settings.json` hooks by default, so in claude-code-enabled repos Devin fires `entire hooks claude-code …` with Devin payloads. These are detected (`DEVIN_PROJECT_DIR` set, `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` absent) and skipped — this protects existing Claude Code users today, independent of Devin support. `DEVIN_PROJECT_DIR` is also added to the agent-subprocess TTY sentinels.
- **Resume**: `devin -r <session_id>` / `devin -c`, in the foreground resume command registry with parity test.

## Verification

- `gofmt` clean, `golangci-lint` 0 issues, `go test -tags=integration -race ./...` green, Vogon E2E canary green.
- Live end-to-end in a clean repo against an authenticated devin 3000.2.17: `entire enable --agent devin` installs 5 hooks (preserving user hook entries) → interactive pty-driven session checkpoints per turn on the shadow branch → mid-session `git commit` receives the `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer → commit-after-exit condenses the **complete 10-step ATIF transcript with real token usage** to `entire/checkpoints/v1` → `entire checkpoint explain`, `entire session list` (agent, model, tokens), `entire session resume` (prints `devin -r <id>`), and `entire checkpoint rewind --to` (restores session + writes transcript back) all verified working.

## Known v1 limitations (documented in AGENT.md)

- Devin resumes conversations from its SQLite store, so rewind restores the transcript file but not Devin's own conversation memory; cross-machine resume needs the session present locally.
- Checkpoints condensed mid-session carry a stub/previous-run transcript; the first condensation after the session run ends captures the complete one.
- No subagent hooks (Devin has no `SubagentStop`).

## What

Extends `entire import` (PR #1527, Claude Code only) to the other supported agents: **Cursor, Pi, Factory AI Droid, Codex, Copilot CLI, and Gemini CLI**. Each `entire import <agent>` subcommand now surfaces automatically. Supports https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues/1336.

OpenCode is intentionally **out of scope**: it has no on-disk transcript Entire can read (transcripts only materialize via `opencode export`), and its sessions aren't repo-attributable.

## How

PR #1527 built the agent-agnostic orchestration (discovery loop, idempotent per-turn IDs, redaction, checkpoint write) behind an `Importer` seam. This adds one self-contained `Importer` per agent and registers them in the `importers` slice — no command wiring, since `import_cmd.go` iterates `agentimport.All()`.

Each importer reuses its agent's **existing** transcript methods rather than re-encoding parsing:

| Agent | Granularity | Tokens / Model |
|---|---|---|
| cursor | per-turn | none (nil tokens, empty model — records neither) |
| pi | per-turn | `CalculateTokenUsage` + `ExtractModel` (branch-aware) |
| factoryai-droid | per-turn | subagent-aware `CalculateTotalTokenUsage`; model from adjacent `.settings.json` |
| codex | per-turn | cumulative-usage delta; **global store**, filtered by `session_meta.cwd` |
| copilot-cli | per-turn | `CalculateTokenUsage`; **flat store**, filtered by `session.start` cwd/gitRoot |
| gemini | per-session | single JSON doc, message-index offsets → one checkpoint/session |

Codex and Copilot share a `repoMatches` helper (equal-or-descendant, symlink-normalized) so their global/flat stores only import the current repo's sessions.

Imported checkpoints keep the merged Claude behavior: commit-less, `Kind:"imported"`, `[imported]` label, not rewindable, idempotent per `sha256(sessionID + "/" + turnUUID)`.

No changes to `claude.go`, `Run`, the `Importer` interface, or `Turn`.

## Testing

- Per-agent unit tests: `Discover` (lookback / `--session` filter / repo-match) and `SplitTurns` (turn boundaries, prompt/model/tokens; Gemini single-turn).
- Registry test asserts all seven importers register with distinct names.
- End-to-end `Run` test through the Cursor importer (nil tokens / empty model) confirms the generic pipeline + idempotency.
- `mise run lint` (0 issues) and the import/agentimport test suites pass locally. Verified against sample fixtures: cursor 3 turns / pi 2 / factory 2 / codex 2 / copilot 2 / gemini 1.

## Summary

Triage of the persistent E2E failures on `main` (run [26496760848](https://github.com/entireio/cli/actions/runs/26496760848)) found that ~75 of the failures came from two agents — **opencode (43)** and **gemini-cli (32)** — and **neither is caused by CLI product code**. Both are defects in the `e2e/` agent runners. This PR fixes both. No `cmd/entire/cli/` changes.

### opencode (43 failures) — wrong working directory
`RunPrompt` set `cmd.Dir` but not `PWD`. Go's `cmd.Dir` chdirs the child without updating the inherited `PWD` env var, and opencode (Node) resolves its project/worktree root from `process.env.PWD`. So opencode's file writes landed in the `go test` package dir instead of the `/tmp/e2e-repo-*` test repo, the per-repo `.opencode/plugins/entire.ts` never loaded, and no checkpoint was created — surfacing as `checkpoint ref entire/checkpoints/v1 did not advance within 30s` and `git add <path>: exit status 128` (file never existed in the repo).

Fix: extract `openCodePromptEnv()`, which strips any stale `PWD` and forces it to match `cmd.Dir`. The tmux/interactive path was already correct (`tmux new-session -c dir` sets `PWD`), which is why the 5 interactive tests passed.

### gemini-cli (32 failures) — aborted turn exits 0
gemini-cli intermittently aborts a turn server-side with `Invalid stream: The model returned an empty response or malformed tool call` on stderr while **exiting 0** with empty stdout. The turn never completes → the `after-agent` lifecycle hook never fires → no checkpoint. Because the process exits 0, the harness's transient-retry path (`err != nil && IsTransientError`) was never reached, so a retryable glitch was scored as a hard "checkpoint did not advance" failure.

Fix: `RunPrompt` now synthesizes an error when it detects the abort signature in stderr, and `IsTransientError` recognizes it (`geminiAbortSignatures`), so the scenario restarts (up to 3 attempts) instead of failing on a missing checkpoint.

## Tests
- `e2e/agents/opencode_test.go` (new): `TestOpenCodePromptEnv_OverridesPWD`
- `e2e/agents/gemini_test.go`: `TestGeminiIsTransientError_RecognizesAbortedTurn`, `TestGeminiAbortedTurn`

These run in the **standard** `mise run test` suite — `e2e/agents` is not behind the `e2e` build tag — so they gate merges without needing a paid E2E run.

## Verification
- `mise run lint` — clean
- `go test ./e2e/agents/` — pass
- `gofmt` / `dup:staged` — clean
- Real E2E validation to be run remotely on this branch.

## Notes / caveats
- gemini's failures were 100% correlated with `Invalid stream`, which is high for pure flakiness. The retry will salvage genuinely transient cases; if gemini-2.5-flash is *systematically* choking, retries will exhaust and it'll still fail (correctly) — at which point it's a model/version question, not a harness one.
- Out of scope (separate clusters from the same triage): cursor-cli (account out of usage quota) and factory/copilot interactive PTY (`FACTORY_API_KEY` device-auth + Copilot trust-dialog sentinel).

### What's implemented

- **Agent package** (`cmd/entire/cli/agent/codex/`) with all core + optional interfaces:

| **`codex_hooks` feature flag** | Default off (stage: UnderDevelopment) | `entire enable` writes it to project config + trusts the project, but if the feature graduates to stable this config becomes unnecessary |
| **PreToolUse is shell-only** | Only fires for Bash tool, not MCP/other tools | File modification detection relies on transcript parsing (apply_patch), not hooks |
| **TranscriptPreparer** | Not needed — Codex materializes rollout before firing hooks | Confirmed by reading `hook_transcript_path()` → `ensure_rollout_materialized()` in Codex source |
| **TextGenerator** | No `codex --print` equivalent | Can't generate AI-powered metadata (trail titles, summaries) |


`cmd.StderrPipe` is replaced with a pipe we own. `Wait` now reaps the agent first and only then drains stderr:

- normal agent: the capture goroutine has already reached EOF, so nothing changes;

Fixes #3052.

### Background
On Unix, `execx.TerminateOnCancel` and `procutil.TerminateOnCancel` configure a new process group (`Setpgid = true`) and send `SIGKILL` to `-cmd.Process.Pid` on cancellation to terminate the entire process group.
On Windows, `killProcessGroupOnCancel` was previously a no-op stub:
```go
func killProcessGroupOnCancel(_ *exec.Cmd) {}
```
This fell back to Go's default `Cancel` behavior, which calls `TerminateProcess` on the direct child only. Because Windows does not automatically terminate child processes when a parent process exits, any descendants spawned by the child (such as `git-remote-https.exe`, `ssh.exe`, MCP servers, subagents, or clean filters) remained running in the background. Whenever descendants inherited stdout/stderr pipes, `cmd.Wait()` blocked for the full `KillWaitDelay` (10s in `execx`, 5s in `procutil`), causing noticeable delays and leaking running processes and pack file locks.

### Solution
1. **`execx.KillProcessTree(rootPid int)`**:
   - Uses `windows.CreateToolhelp32Snapshot(windows.TH32CS_SNAPPROCESS, 0)` to capture running processes and map parent-child relationships.
   - Traverses the process hierarchy to find all descendants of `rootPid`.
   - **PID Reuse Protection**: Queries `GetProcessTimes` on the root process and candidates, ensuring only processes created after the root process started are treated as descendants.
   - Terminates descendants bottom-up (deepest leaves first) before terminating the root process.
   - Falls back gracefully to direct process termination if taking the snapshot fails.

2. **Integration**:
   - Configures `cmd.Cancel` in `execx_windows.go` to invoke `KillProcessTree(cmd.Process.Pid)`.
   - Configures `cmd.Cancel` in `procutil_windows.go` to invoke `execx.KillProcessTree(cmd.Process.Pid)`.

3. **Tests**:
   - Added `TestTerminateOnCancel_SetsWaitDelayAndCancelWindows` and `TestTerminateOnCancel_KillsProcessTreeWindows` in `cmd/entire/cli/execx/execx_windows_test.go`.
   - Added `TestTerminateOnCancel_UnblocksGrandchildHoldingPipeWindows` in `cmd/entire/cli/procutil/procutil_windows_test.go`.
   - Both tests verify that a background grandchild process holding the stdout pipe is cleanly terminated and `cmd.Wait()` unblocks immediately without waiting for `WaitDelay`.

## Verification
Tested on a native Windows machine:
- Grandchild process holding the output pipe unblocks in **<10ms** upon context cancellation.
- Grandchild process (`ping.exe`) is confirmed terminated from the system process table.
- Verified that `go build ./cmd/entire` and `go vet` pass cleanly.

`entire trail watch` replays the trail's whole event history every time it connects, so a person or agent re-running it after a push first scrolls through every earlier push's reviews, gates and agent runs.

## Fix

entire-api now accepts `from=head` on the trail events stream (et/entirehq/entire-api change 807, merged): it starts at the current head's first event and never skips one of that push's events.

- `trail watch` sends `from=head` on every request. A resume cursor (`Last-Event-ID`) outranks it on the server, and sending it every time means a retry before any event can't fall back to a full replay. Servers without it ignore the parameter (old behavior).
- `--full` replays the whole history, as before.
- An idle first connection sees no event ids, so the server's ~50s reconnect would have replayed everything. The resume cursor is now seeded from the ready frame's `cursor`, in both text and `--json` modes (including a cursor of 0 on an empty trail, so a reconnect never re-resolves the head and skips earlier pushes).
- A start line on stderr says where the stream began (`Showing the latest push (<sha>); --full replays the whole history`, or "no events for the latest push yet", or "no head yet"). `--json` stdout still carries the server's frames unchanged.
- Help text describes the default and `--full`.

## Testing

- New tests: idle first connection then reconnect resumes from the ready cursor; a failed first connection retries with `from=head`; `--full` sends no `from`; start-line text (head, tail, beginning, short/empty SHA, older server); `--json` stdout unchanged; the route rewrite keeps `?from=head` for both cell route shapes.
- Live with a binary built from a fresh checkout of this branch, on a throwaway trail: watch started at the latest push; a new commit pushed mid-watch streamed its code version and gate results live; reconnects resumed with no replay; restarting watch started at the new push, not the earlier one.
- Earlier live run on a US-cell trail: default starts at the latest push (after event 135) with the start line; `--full` starts at event 1; a 75s idle run reconnected 14 times, each resuming at the last event with no replay.
