**Problem:** review feedback only arrives after a push. Every finding from the trail's runners costs a round trip through the server, and the fix for one often surfaces the next.

**Solution:** `entire review --use-runner-config` reads `.entire/runners/*.json` and runs those runners locally, so you can see what the trail will say before pushing.

This is a spike, opened as a draft. It came out of [a Slack thread](https://entireio.slack.com/archives/C0A095SNK32/p1788784813352809); the flag shape is Stefan's suggestion, so the existing `entire review` keeps working untouched and this can be merged and tried without changing anything for anyone who does not pass the flag.

## What it does

`--use-runner-config` bypasses review profiles entirely. A runner config already names its agent, model, prompt and timeout, so `--agent`, `--model`, `--profile` and `--prompt` are rejected rather than silently ignored. `--runner <id>` runs a single runner, with the leading `trail-` optional.

Five of this repo's six runners are eligible. The summary runner is skipped because a trail body has no local meaning.

Each runner's prompt goes through verbatim, with `{{branch}}` and `{{base_branch}}` filled from the resolved scope and `{{previous_findings}}` left empty. The local scope statement is **prepended**, not appended, because the templates hand the agent numbered diff commands that see committed work only, and the reason to run this before pushing is that the work often is not committed yet. That is still a contradiction the model resolves rather than a guarantee. The honest fix is templates that take the diff command as a variable.

Results are parsed with the runners' own last-JSON-line adapter and printed per runner. No judge sits over them: across five output shapes it would only reinterpret scores the trail reports verbatim. A completed run always exits 0, because a preview that failed the shell on a low score is a preview nobody runs.

## What it looks like

```
Reviewing main vs origin/HEAD: 0 commits, 0 files changed, 2 uncommitted
Running 5 runner config(s) from .entire/runners locally.

Runner results

  Security Review (trail-security)
    Security 78/100 (lower is better)
    ...

  Trail Review (trail-review)
    1 comment
      [high] cmd/entire/cli/review/runnerconfig.go:578 (confidence 0.85) ...
```

## Blocker for merging

The remote runs each runner in a sandbox with a read-only repo token. This does not. A repo-committed prompt template becomes the verbatim prompt of an agent spawned with `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`, so a pull request editing a runner config gets arbitrary instructions run on any teammate who passes the flag.

`settings.enforceAgentPromptTrust` already gates exactly this channel for every other prompt field, and this path routes around it. Wiring that gate is the next step and the reason this is a draft.

All five runners found this independently when pointed at the branch, which is a decent argument that the loop works.

## Other known gaps, all deliberate

- Runner configs are read from disk only, so runners defined in the UI are invisible. The slop monitor is one of them.
- Nothing is persisted, so `entire review --findings` does not see these runs.
- `RunMulti` applies one shared deadline, so the longest runner's timeout governs the whole run.
- The config loader duplicates `loadTuneRunners` in `cmd/entire/cli/runner_prompt.go`. That one lives in package `cli`, which imports `review`, so sharing it means lifting it into its own package.
- No tests yet.

## Two things worth a second opinion

`NewCommand` carries a `//nolint:maintidx`. Measured before this change its maintainability index is exactly 20, the lowest that passes, so any added branch trips it. I moved the flags, dispatch and conflict rules into `runnerconfig.go` and got the closure down to one call and it still trips. Lifting `RunE`'s mode dispatch out of the closure is the real fix and is a refactor of existing wiring.

Separately, the runs surfaced a live bug outside this change: the claude adapter marks a whole run failed on one unparseable `stream-json` envelope, long after the agent has finished. Four of five runners were marked failed while still producing complete results. That affects normal `entire review` too.

`mise run lint` is green. Four tests fail on `mise run test:ci`, all of them symlink and hooks-dir tests that fail identically on a clean `main`.

Fixes #1642 — on worktrees with large gitignored trees, the Claude Code `user-prompt-submit` hook takes 40–55s per prompt and every turn-end checkpoint pays the same cost again. Root cause: three hot paths still used go-git's `worktree.Status()`, which stats and hashes every file on disk including gitignored directories. Several sibling call sites had already been converted to the native git CLI for exactly this reason (see the existing comments in `checkpoint/ephemeral.go` and `getStagedFiles` in `strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go`); this PR finishes the job.

## Changes

- **`strategy/common.go`**: new exported `GitCLIStatus(ctx)` helper — runs `git status --porcelain=v1 -z -uall --no-renames` at the worktree root and parses the output into a go-git-compatible `git.Status` map. Porcelain v1 status letters are byte-identical to go-git's `StatusCode` constants, so this is a drop-in replacement for `worktree.Status()`.
- **`state.go`**: `getUntrackedFilesForState` (→ `capture_pre_prompt_state`) and `DetectFileChanges` (→ turn-end checkpointing) now use `GitCLIStatus`.
- **`strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go`**: `calculatePromptAttributionAtStart` (→ `init_session`) now uses `GitCLIStatus`.
- **`state_test.go`**: the hand-rolled test repos gain a `.git/refs/` directory — the native git CLI requires it to recognize a repository (go-git did not).

## Measurements

61GB / ~686k-file worktree (~34GB in gitignored SwiftPM `.build/` dirs), measured with `entire doctor trace` + `ENTIRE_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG`:

## Problem

`entire checkpoint list` shows 0 checkpoints in a fresh clone of a git-refs repo whose checkpoints are all imported, although `git ls-remote origin 'refs/entire/checkpoints/*'` shows them.

## Root cause

Not the remote selection: `ListCheckpointRefsOnRemote` already queries origin when no `checkpoint_remote` is set (the #1771 description is outdated there).

Imported checkpoints carry no commit trailer, so they only surface through `getImportedPendingCheckpoints`. That function opened a second store and listed **local refs only**. Remote-discovered stubs would have been dropped anyway: `Imported` is unknown until the ref is read.

## Fix

- Reuse the discovery-enabled List from `getBranchCheckpoints` and hydrate remote-only stubs that could be imported: legacy-hex IDs not linked by a commit trailer. Imports always get hex IDs (`agentimport.DeriveCheckpointID`); ULIDs are native git-refs checkpoints and are skipped.
- Each candidate is fetched lazily, one ref at a time. No bulk `git fetch refs/entire/checkpoints/*` (keeps #1770's constraint).
- Hydration recovers `CreatedAt`, so legacy hex IDs (no ULID timestamp) sort correctly.
- On feature branches, main's trailers also mark checkpoints as linked, so they aren't fetched just to learn they're not imported.
- Both hydration passes share one `ListHydrationPassTimeout` budget (was two back-to-back 30s passes). Stubs skipped or failed are counted in a stderr warning.
- Imported prompts are read only for entries that survive `--limit`.

## Known trade-off

A fresh clone with many unlinked legacy-hex checkpoints still fetches them one per ref, bounded by the 30s budget, converging across runs as refs become local. Making importedness visible names-only (ref namespace or index ref) would remove this; left as a follow-up since it's a storage-format change.

## Testing

- `TestGetBranchCheckpoints_ListsRemoteOnlyImportedCheckpoints`: no `checkpoint_remote`, two remote-only imported legacy-hex checkpoints listed newest-first by `CreatedAt`; an unlinked ULID stub is not fetched.
- `TestGetBranchCheckpoints_FeatureBranchSkipsMainLinkedStubs`: main-linked stub is not f…367249 chars truncated…` is a real, populated field: trail 1076 returned `etag = W/"2026-08-18T23:29:25.468469Z"`; trail 1075 returned an empty etag alongside an empty snapshot, exercising the graceful-degradation path. The entire-api schema also lists `etag` as required on `TrailBodyDocumentJSON`.

## Known tradeoff (by design, not a bug)

The non-interactive `--body` path fetches an etag purely to attempt CAS, even though the caller supplied replacement text without having read the current document — this etag doesn't protect against a race the caller could have avoided by reading first, only against one that happens to occur in the fetch-to-write window. This is the ticket's explicit design (Linear ENT-1741), not something this PR reconsiders; flagging it here since a reviewer raised it independently.

That fetch-to-write window is also the only one closable today: `trail show --json` emits no etag field, so a read-modify-write caller (read the description, compose an edit, write back later) has no way to pass back what they read — there is no `--if-match` escape hatch. Widening CAS to cover that case (etag on `trail show --json`, an `--if-match` flag) is out of scope for ENT-1741; filed as a follow-up finding on the trail so it isn't lost.

## What

`entire repo remote` collapses to one verb:

```
entire repo remote add <remote-name> [repo] [--cluster host] [--override]
```

- **`repo remote use` → `repo remote add <remote-name>`.** The remote name is the positional, not `--remote`, so the command names what it writes.
- **`repo remote url` is deleted.** `entire repo mirror get` already lists a clone URL per cluster for both forges, in a table and in `--json` — the same question, answered all at once instead of one line per invocation.
- **Non-interactive cluster selection now defaults to the repo's primary**, for `repo remote add` *and* `repo clone`.

## Why the primary default

`selectPlacement` used to refuse whenever a repo had several placements, no `--cluster` and no terminal:

```
repo is mirrored on 2 clusters; pass --cluster to choose one of: ...
```

Since native mirrors landed (#2529), a native repo has a primary *plus* its ready mirrors — so every non-interactive `repo clone /et/…` and every scripted remote write started failing the moment somebody added a mirror. A script that named no cluster wants the cluster the repo lives on. `selectPlacement` now takes that host and resolves it in exactly that case; a terminal still gets the picker, and `--cluster` still wins either way.

Both forges resolve a primary, by different routes. A native repo carries its own cluster. A GitHub repo takes a second read: `GET /mirrors/placements` returns peers with no role among them, so `githubPrimaryHost` asks `POST /repos/resolve` for `primaries.processing` — an id from the same space as `ResolvedPlacement.MirrorId` — and matches it back to a listed placement. (Its sibling `data_primary` is the *forge* for a GitHub repo, `github:<id>`, so it can never name a remote.) That second read is skipped unless its answer would be used — an explicit `--cluster`, a lone placement, or a terminal all decide without it — and is best-effort: if it fails you get the `--cluster` pointer you had before, not a hard failure.

The primary is matched against the deduped placement set rather than trusted, so a host no placement vouched for asks instead of resolving.

## Why `--override` rather than a prompt

`git remote add origin <url>` on an existing name exits 3 with `error: remote origin already exists.` — verified, git 2.55.0. `add` that silently repoints is not an add, so an occupied name is refused and `--override` is the way through. A remote already carrying that exact URL is a reported no-op, not a collision, so re-running is safe.

That replaces `promptMirrorRemoteChoice` — the interactive replace-vs-add prompt existed only to resolve this ambiguity, so it and its huh form are deleted (~90 lines plus tests).

## `--upstream` is gone too

It existed because `remote use` repointed `origin` by *default*, so preserving the forge URL guarded a write the caller never asked for. `add <remote-name> --override` **is** that opt-in, which leaves preservation writing a remote the caller did not name — and that name can itself be taken, the case where a collision printed a clean ✓ over a URL that had left git config for good. `--override` now writes exactly the remote it names; the report echoes the replaced URL (redacted) and that is its only record.

Removed with it: `defaultMirrorUpstreamRemote`, the `preserveAs`/`preserveSkipped` plan fields, the preserve write, the stderr `WARNING` block, and seven subtests.

## Also removed

`validateEntireURLForPrinting` and the `passthroughNeedsHost` parameter it gated: `repo clone` was the only caller that passed `false`, and it is now the only caller at all.

Both old spellings are banned in `deprecated_strings_test`, per the no-backcompat rule for control-plane commands.

## Testing

`mise run check`: lint reports 0 issues. The test sweep surfaced three failures, all environmental and none in this area — `TestOpenCodeSeedRepoPlantsDeps` fails identically on clean `main` (local opencode/npm dep cache), and `TestExtractPluginBinary_OversizeEntryIsRejected` plus `REDACTED` were a full disk (`no space left on device`); the latter passes on its own.

Manually verified against a real multi-placement GitHub repo: `ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0 entire repo remote add <name>` in a clone of `entireio/cli` resolves `entire://aws-us-east-2.entire.io/gh/entireio/cli`, its processing primary.

`e2e/controlplane/native_mirror_test.go` is updated for the rename and gains phases for the refusal, the no-op re-add, and the non-interactive primary default. **Not run** — it makes paid API calls.

## Related

`repo view`'s side of this — it still omits the synthesized `remote` field from `--json` and refuses `/gh/` refs — is handled in #2547.

## Why

entiredb now stores per-branch protection rules for Entire-native repositories, and Core exposes them at `/repos/{repoId}/branch-protection` (entiredb ADR `20260908-branch-protection-and-trail-review`, #3600/#3643). Until now, the only way to manage these rules was `entire api` with a hand-written request body.

## What

Adds the `entire repo protection` command group:

- `entire repo protection list <repo>` lists each rule as `BRANCH` and `LEVEL` (`protected` or `server-side merge only`).
- `entire repo protection add <repo> <branch> [--server-side-merge-only]` sends one PATCH with `addRules`. The server upserts by ref, so re-adding a branch replaces its level.
- `entire repo protection remove <repo> <branch>` sends one PATCH with `removeRefs`.

A short branch name expands to `refs/heads/<name>`. `HEAD` and values beginning with `refs/` pass through unchanged; wildcard validation remains server-side.

Every verb accepts `--project` when a repository is addressed by name. `add` and `remove` print the resulting rules and never perform a read-modify-write; each is a single PATCH.

### Empty-list behavior

An empty Core rule list does not always mean that nothing protects the repository:

- An Entire-native repository prints `Nothing is protected yet.`
- A GitHub mirror explains that protection is governed upstream and that Entire always protects its default branch.
- If the repository provider is absent, unknown, or cannot be looked up, the output says that the protection source could not be determined rather than assuming the repository is native.

With `--json`, stdout remains a bare `[]` for scripts. Any mirror or unknown-provider qualification is written to stderr.

### Existing-rule behavior

`add` is an upsert, not a strictly additive operation. Because `--server-side-merge-only` defaults to `false`, running `add` without the flag currently lowers an existing merge-only rule to ordinary `protected`. The command help documents that re-adding replaces the level, and the resulting rules are printed.

There is an open discussion about whether omitting `serverSideMergeOnly` should preserve an existing value or default it to `false`. That server/API decision determines whether the CLI can make `add` non-weakening without first reading the current rules.

## Core API generation

The Core OpenAPI spec is refreshed. The normalizer now handles two upstream compatibility issues, documented in `internal/coreapi/UPSTREAM.md`:

- It removes interactive `oauth2`/`oidc` alternatives that ogen cannot generate and this client never drives. It refuses to transform a non-empty security list into an unauthenticated empty list.
- It treats newly required, non-load-bearing read-model fields as optional and selected read enums as open sets, allowing older or mixed-version Core deployments and future enum values to decode safely.

The generated `SecuritySource` remains unchanged.

## Agent-help classification

Not listed; user-owned. The parent `repo` group is unlisted, and these commands modify repository write rules.

- `go generate ./internal/coreapi/...` produces no diff
- `git diff --check`
- Live staging verification covered list, add, level replacement, JSON output, and remove; the test repository was restored afterward.

Unit tests cover branch-ref expansion, level rendering, PATCH bodies, upsert behavior, JSON output, provider-aware empty states, failed/unknown provider lookup, avoiding the extra repository lookup for non-empty lists, backward-compatible decoding of newly added read fields, and the name-without-project error.

## Problem

Since the single-remote gate (ENT-1451, shipped in v0.10.0), a push to a non-elected remote silently stops carrying checkpoints. A user whose habitual push remote loses the default election to a dormant `origin` sees checkpoints strand locally with **no signal in the push output** — the skip only shows in `entire status` and the debug log. The first real user hit this within a day of the release ("I have a bunch of repos where the git remote I push to isn't called origin. It looks like this means I no longer push checkpoints. Is that intentional?").

## Change

The pre-push hook prints a two-line stderr hint on a gated push:

```
[entire] 3 checkpoint(s) are waiting to sync to "origin", this repo's checkpoint sync remote; this push to "fork" does not carry them.
[entire] To sync checkpoints to "fork" instead, set strategy_options.checkpoint_push_remote to "fork" in .entire/settings.json.
```

It stays quiet when:
- the election was **explicit** (a configured `checkpoint_push_remote` is a decision already made — gated pushes are intentional, no nagging),
- the push target is a **raw URL** (the setting takes a remote name; nothing actionable to suggest),
- **nothing is waiting** (a gated push after checkpoints already synced stays clean),
- the **election failed** (the fail-closed path already warns through the gate).

Fully local — reuses `CountUnpushedCheckpoints` (push-queue length on git-refs, v1-ahead count on git-branch), no network in the hook.

## Testing

- Unit: `TestHintGatedCheckpointSync` covers the hint and all four silence conditions.
- Integration: `assertSingleRemoteRouting` now asserts the gated leg's output on both backends — hint present for the default and tracking-config elections, absent for the explicit `checkpoint_push_remote` override. New `RunPrePushOutput` harness variant captures hook output.
- `mise run fmt`, `mise run lint` (0 issues), full unit suite (8837 pass), and the `TestCheckpointSyncRemote` integration slice all green.

## Non-goals

Whether the election itself should gain a tracking tier (so a habitually-pushed remote can win over a dormant origin without config) stays the product call deferred in #1893/#1951 — this PR only makes the existing gate self-explaining.

## What

Adds `entire cluster list`, a read-only control-plane group that renders the cluster catalog (`GET /clusters`) so a user can see where to create a project or a mirror.

```
$ entire cluster list
REGION  CLUSTER             HOST
au      aws-ap-southeast-2  aws-ap-southeast-2.entire.io
eu      aws-eu-central-1    aws-eu-central-1.entire.io
in      aws-ap-south-1      aws-ap-south-1.entire.io
us      aws-us-east-2       aws-us-east-2.entire.io
```

Each column is a value another command takes:

- **REGION** is the jurisdiction slug behind `org create --region` and `project create --region`.
- **CLUSTER** is the placement slug `repo mirror list --cluster` accepts.
- **HOST** is the bare host behind `repo create --cluster-host`, `repo mirror create` and `repo clone --cluster`. It goes through the existing `hostFromPublicURL` guard, so a `publicUrl` that fails validation renders `-` rather than a spoofable host.

`--json` emits the wire model as a bare array, `apiUrl` and `isDefault` included, plus a synthesized `host` on each object: the same validated host the table shows, absent rather than dashed when `publicUrl` fails validation, so a script never re-implements the guard over the raw URL. `apiUrl` is never a table column, since the CLI dials the API URL itself. `isDefault` becomes a DEFAULT column only when the catalog holds a non-default cluster; with one cluster per region, today's shape, every row would read yes and the column would say nothing.

## Why no metrics

The catalog exposes exactly slug, jurisdiction, publicUrl, apiUrl and isDefault. There is no health, capacity or usage data anywhere server-side, and hidden or decommissioned clusters are already filtered out by the server.

## `repo create` gets the same host guard

Reviewing the JSON path showed `repo create` had none: `--cluster-host` went to the wire unvalidated, and `repoRemoteURL` emitted a spoofable `entire://` URL for whatever `clusterHost` the server returned, on the confirmation line, in `repo list`, and in `--json`. The `remote` and `host` merges share one additive-only helper, `mergeSynthesizedField`.

## What

OPF progress UX (`→ scanning` / `✓ done` / `× unavailable`) was written to `/dev/tty` so the messages would survive the post-commit hook's `2>/dev/null` redirect. That rationale is obsolete:

- OPF no longer runs at post-commit — it lives solely in the **pre-push rewrite path** (`strategy/manual_commit_opf_rewrite.go`), whose hook is installed **without** a stderr redirect (`pre-push "$1"`).
- Post-commit condensation calls the 7-layer functions directly via `RedactBlobBytes(..., usePrivacyFilter=false)`, so it never reaches the OPF progress writes.

So `opfStderr` now defaults to `os.Stderr`. During `git push` the messages are still visible (stderr isn't swallowed there); in tests they're captured by `go test` instead of bleeding straight to the developer's terminal — which fixes the stray `→ scanning…` lines that interleaved with `PASS`/`ok` output.

## Changes

- `redact/opf.go`: default `opfStderr` to `os.Stderr`; remove the now-dead `openTTYOrDiscard` helper; update the comment.
- `redact/global_test.go` (new): silence `opfStderr` once in `TestMain`, matching how the `strategy` package handles its own pre-push progress writer (`strategy/global_test.go`).
- `redact/{opf,batch}_test.go`: remove the 11 per-test `io.Discard` overrides — now redundant, and race-free as a single set-once (the per-test blocks mutated a global under `t.Parallel()`).

<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## What

Four tests in `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/hooks_test.go` fail on a clean checkout of `main`, on a machine whose `~/.gitconfig` sets `init.defaultBranch = feature`.

```
$ go test ./cmd/entire/cli/strategy
--- FAIL: TestGetGitDirInPath_Worktree
    hooks_test.go:147: failed to create worktree: exit status 255
--- FAIL: TestGetHooksDirInPath_Worktree
    hooks_test.go:225: failed to create worktree: exit status 255
--- FAIL: TestInstallGitHook_WorktreeInstallsInCommonHooks
    hooks_test.go:420: failed to create worktree: exit status 255
--- FAIL: TestIsGitSequenceOperation_Worktree
    hooks_test.go:647: failed to create worktree: exit status 255
```

## Cause

The 38 `exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", …)` calls in this file leave `cmd.Env` unset, so every child git reads the developer's real global config. The worktree setups do:

```go
cmd = exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "worktree", "add", worktreeDir, "-b", "feature")
```

With `init.defaultBranch = feature`, `git init` has already created that branch, so the add fails with `fatal: a branch named 'feature' already exists`. Isolating the cause:

```
$ git worktree add /tmp/wt -b feature
fatal: a branch named 'feature' already exists
EXIT=255
$ GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null git worktree add /tmp/wt2 -b feature2
HEAD is now at 4dce75c init
EXIT=0
```

And on the unmodified tree:

```
$ GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/tmp/empty GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/tmp/empty go test ./cmd/entire/cli/strategy -run Worktree
ok      github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/strategy  1.843s
$ go test ./cmd/entire/cli/strategy -run Worktree
FAIL
```

This is the failure mode that erodes trust in the gate: `mise run check` goes red for a correct change, the message (`exit status 255`, no stderr) explains nothing, and it gets written off as a flake.

The file already knew about the problem in one shape — `clearGlobalHooksPath` exists to defeat a global `core.hooksPath` — but that fix is per-setting. `init.defaultBranch`, `commit.gpgsign`, `core.autocrlf`, aliases, and `init.templateDir` all still leak in.

## Fix

`cmd.Env = testutil.GitIsolatedEnv()` on every git invocation in the file. That helper is already the repo's answer here: it strips inherited `GIT_CONFIG_*` and points global and system config at an empty file. Unlike `testutil.IsolateGitConfigEnv`/`t.Setenv` it is safe in the parallel tests in this file.

`clearGlobalHooksPath` is kept — pinning the local value is still correct for a repo under test.

## Verification

Fixes #2089.

`checkpoint explain --session <id>` can report `checkpoints 0` and `No checkpoints found on this branch.` when the underlying checkpoint scan reaches its limit and the requested session is not present in the returned window. That output is a false negative: older checkpoints may exist but were not examined.

## Root cause

`getBranchCheckpoints` already returns a truncation signal, but the branch-view path discarded that state before applying the session filter. When filtering removed every checkpoint from the bounded result, the formatter could not distinguish “the branch has no checkpoints” from “no matching checkpoint was found in an incomplete scan.”

## Changes

* Preserve the scan-truncation state through the branch formatter.
* Report that no matching checkpoint was found **in the scanned results** when a session-filtered scan is truncated.
* Keep the existing empty-history message unchanged for genuinely non-truncated empty results.
* Add a native regression test covering the truncated, zero-match-after-filter case.

This change does not alter checkpoint collection limits, JSON output, or the behavior of an unfiltered empty branch.

### Pi extension uses invalid hooks **Medium Severity** The new `.pi/extensions/entire.ts` invokes `entire hooks pi` with hyphenated names like `session-start` and `turn-start`, but the CLI only registers snake_case verbs (`session_start`, `before_agent_start`, `agent_end`, `session_shutdown`). Hook failures are swallowed, so Pi sessions would silently skip checkpoints, transcripts, and context injection if this file is used instead of the installed `entire/index.ts` template.
 
Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit f98758d0d39d775c27ff697f753d046669f2dd52. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

Removed the accidental duplicate `.pi/extensions/entire.ts`. The repository already has `.pi/extensions/entire/index.ts`, which forwards the supported Pi snake_case hook names (`session_start`, `before_agent_start`, `agent_end`, `session_shutdown`).

The TerminateOnCancel doc comment claims it makes the command “and its descendants” die on context cancellation, but on Windows killProcessGroupOnCancel is a no-op (descendants are not terminated). This is misleading for callers reading the API docs; please document the OS-specific behavior (Unix process-group kill vs Windows WaitDelay-only backstop).
Updated the package/function comments to document the OS-specific behavior: Unix uses a process-group SIGKILL plus `WaitDelay`; Windows currently has only the `WaitDelay` backstop.

The comment/docstring for `openCodeRecord` says token-only assistant messages should produce a `\"content\":null` line, but this path returns a `Record` with `Content` left as nil. If `Record.Content` is tagged with `omitempty` (common for `json.RawMessage`), this will omit the `content` field entirely, which is semantically different per the README (present `null` vs absent). To make the behavior unambiguous and consistent with the documented wire semantics, explicitly set `r.Content` to the JSON literal `null` (and ensure the fold treats it as ‘present’) for the token-only case.

A live follow then shows remaining messages before the summary, while `Convert` of the compacted export puts the summary first.

On Windows this is currently a no-op, so cancelling a review/investigate run can still wedge if the agent spawns helper grandchildren that inherit stdout/stderr (the original hang scenario). `WaitDelay` only bounds `cmd.Wait`/`cmd.Run`, but it won’t necessarily unblock readers draining `StdoutPipe`/`StderrPipe` to EOF.

Consider implementing a best-effort process-tree kill for Windows (e.g., `taskkill /T /F /PID <pid>`) so cancellation reliably closes inherited pipes and the caller can finish draining output.

This test doesn’t call `t.Parallel()`. The repo’s tests generally parallelize by default, and this test doesn’t appear to mutate process-global state (it spawns an isolated `sh` subprocess with a local context), so it should be safe to run in parallel to keep the suite fast.

This test uses an 8MB markdown input. If the size guard regresses, glamour rendering can take minutes; even with the 5s timeout, the render goroutine will keep running after `t.Fatal`, and `go test` will wait for it, effectively wedging the suite.

Reducing the test input size (while still being > MaxRenderBytes) keeps the regression case bounded while still validating that oversized inputs are returned raw/unstyled.

This new file appears to duplicate the existing Pi extension entry point at `.pi/extensions/entire/index.ts` (which already forwards hooks and includes additional behavior). Having two different implementations in the same repo risks confusion about which one is packaged/loaded, and it doesn’t relate to the PR’s stated goal (review finalize wedging).

If this file is an accidental artifact from `entire enable --agent pi`, it should be removed from this PR; otherwise, the repo should have a single canonical extension source for Pi.

https://entire.com/gh/entireio/-/trails/2547/changes/cli/1680
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Stacked on #2834 (base `alex/ent-3337-transcript-format-fields`). README, a doc comment and a changelog entry; no behavior change.

## What

- `input_tokens` gets one rule that holds on every line: it excludes the tokens in that line's `cache_read_tokens` and `cache_write_tokens`. Old lines carry no cache fields, so `input_tokens + cache_read_tokens + cache_write_tokens` never double counts. The sum is complete only on lines from converters that write the cache fields: old fresh-only lines (Claude Code, most Pi) understate input, and old cache-inclusive lines (Codex, Pi on Google models before pi-ai's March 2026 fix) have the right total with an unknown cache share. #2834 said readers "cannot distinguish" old from new meaning, and #2858 filled that gap with "a set `model` means fresh input". With this rule no marker is needed.
- `model` is the per-call model the source reports, verbatim, and is omitted when none is reported. It is never a placeholder: Claude Code's `<synthetic>` (API-error entries) is omitted.
- Pi is listed with Claude Code and Codex as recording per-call usage. I checked pi-ai at `pi-mono@a37306d43`: every provider path writes fresh `input` (OpenAI responses/completions since 2025-12-03, Google/Vertex since 2026-03-26 `6d744f02e`, Mistral subtracts, Anthropic/Bedrock are fresh natively), which local `~/.pi` sessions confirm.
- `Line.InputTokens` doc comment states the rule; `CHANGELOG.md` notes the new `Line` fields and the `int` → `int64` change.

## Follow-ups for #2858

- Omit `model` instead of writing `"unknown"`.
- Omit `<synthetic>` (it is in the regenerated `claude_expected2.jsonl`).
- Drop "a set `model` means `input_tokens` is fresh" from its README.

## Check

`mise run check`: fmt and lint clean, all tests pass except `e2e/agents` `TestOpenCodeSeedRepoPlantsDeps`, which also fails on `main` locally (it cannot parse `opencode v2.1.2` from a local OpenCode 2 install).

Ships alone because the v1 fields and reader API are additive; current converters keep producing the same transcript content until the converter slice lands.

+Usage and model fields are per call, never copied from a session aggregate. A zero omitted by JSON encoding does not assert that the source reported zero.
+
+On every line, `input_tokens` excludes the tokens in that line's `cache_read_tokens` and `cache_write_tokens`, so adding them never double counts. The sum is the call's total input only on lines from a converter that writes the cache fields. Lines written before that carry no cache fields, and their `input_tokens` is one of two things:

+- Fresh input only (Claude Code, and Pi except as below): the cached input is missing from the line, so the sum understates the call's input.
+- Fresh plus cached input (Codex, and Pi on Google models before pi-ai subtracted cached tokens in March 2026): the total is right, but its cache share is unknown, so pricing it at the fresh-input rate overstates the cost.
+

## The bug

`templateProcess.Wait` waited for stderr EOF before calling `cmd.Wait`:

```go
if p.stderrDone != nil {
    <-p.stderrDone
}
err := p.cmd.Wait()
```

stderr reaches EOF only when every writer closes it. A review agent that leaves a background helper running — a language server, an MCP process, a sandbox helper — hands that helper the same stderr pipe. The agent can exit, the findings can be parsed, and `entire review` still blocks forever on the final wait.

## Reproduction

```go
// BuildCmd
exec.CommandContext(ctx, "sh", "-c", "sleep 5 >/dev/null & exit 0")
```

`Start` succeeds, the agent exits 0 immediately, and `Wait` is still blocked 2s later. On a real run the helper can outlive the review by minutes or hours.

## The fix

`cmd.StderrPipe` is replaced with a pipe we own. `Wait` now reaps the agent first and only then drains stderr:

- normal agent: the capture goroutine has already reached EOF, so nothing changes;
- helper still holding stderr: after a 250ms grace period we close our read end, the capture goroutine finishes, and `Wait` returns with whatever stderr it copied (kept for `ProcessError` diagnostics).

This also keeps the `Process` contract: no goroutine outlives `Wait`.

## Tests

`TestReviewerTemplate_WaitDoesNotBlockOnInheritedStderr` starts the shell above and fails on `main` after 2s with:

```
Wait() blocked on stderr held by a grandchild after the agent exited
```

The existing `WaitIncludesStderrOnFailure` test still passes, so normal failure diagnostics are preserved.

## Verification

- `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/review/...` passes
- `mise run lint:go`: 0 issues

## The bug

`openCodeMsgToken` declared only `input` and `output`:

```go
type openCodeMsgToken struct {
    Input  int `json:"input"`
    Output int `json:"output"`
}
```

OpenCode exports also carry `reasoning`, `cache.read`, `cache.write`, `total` and a per-message `modelID`. `openCodeRecord` therefore wrote a `CallUsage` with only two fields, and the stored transcript line dropped the rest. Readers of a checkpoint transcript saw:

```json
{"input_tokens":150,"output_tokens":90,"content":[...]}
```

instead of cache read 100, cache write 160 and the model the export reported. Every other adapter keeps what its agent records.

Reasoning has the same problem in a second form: 1.3.16+ stores it apart from output, while older or provider-specific messages already include it. The condensed line's `reasoning_tokens` is a subset of `output_tokens`, so it has to be counted exactly once.

## Reproduction

On `main`, `TestCompact_OpenCodeUsageKeepsCacheReasoningAndModel` produces `cache_read_tokens: 0, cache_write_tokens: 0, reasoning_tokens: 0` and no `model`, although the input export carries `cache:{read:5,write:2}`, `reasoning:40` and `modelID`.

The existing `TestCompact_OpenCodeTokenUsage` input also has cache read 100 / write 160; its expected line omitted both, pinning the loss.

## The fix

- Parse `reasoning`, `cache`, `total` and `modelID` from the export.
- Populate `CallUsage` with cache read/write, reasoning and model.
- Compute output with the same identity the OpenCode agent already uses in `Tokens.OutputWithReasoning`: if `total == input + output + cache.read + cache.write`, reasoning is already inside output; otherwise add it. `reasoning_tokens` then stays a subset of `output_tokens`.

The existing golden fixture is regenerated: every assistant line gains its model and cache counts, and no message in it has reasoning stored apart, so its output counts are unchanged.

## Tests

- New `TestCompact_OpenCodeUsageKeepsCacheReasoningAndModel` covers reasoning stored apart (80 + 40 → 120), reasoning already inside output (total identity → 90), cache counts and model.
- `TestCompact_OpenCodeTokenUsage` now asserts the cache fields it already supplied.
- `go test ./transcript/... ./internal/transcript/...` passes.
- `mise run lint:go`: 0 issues.

Independent of #2823: that PR fixes the agent's `CalculateTokenUsage` path used for checkpoint metadata; this one fixes the stored condensed transcript line itself.

Slice 1 of 2 for ENT-3337 (cli/transcript: add model and cache/reasoning token fields to the Entire Transcript Format (additive v1)).

Ships alone because the v1 fields and reader API are additive; current converters keep producing the same transcript content until the converter slice lands.

What
`transcript.Line` and `transcript.Decode` now expose optional assistant `model`, fresh-input, cache-read, cache-write (total and reported 5m/1h split), output and reasoning token fields. All token counts use `int64`; split pointers distinguish unknown from a reported zero. Old v1 lines, unknown fields and JSON `null` on optional scalars remain readable. `v` stays 1. This slice defines the format and typed decode only: it does not populate the new fields in converters, change native timestamps or regenerate golden fixtures.

How to check
Run `go test ./transcript -run '^TestDecode_' -count=1`, then `go test ./transcript -count=1`, then `GOMAXPROCS=4 GOFLAGS=-p=1 mise run check`, `mise run lint` after formatting, and `go build ./cmd/entire`. Look for old-line decode, wrong-type partial skips, unknown-field tolerance, and absent versus explicit-zero cache-write splits. In read-only entire-api, `go test ./internal/transcript -run 'TestUnified_(ParsesSimpleExchange|IsUnifiedTrueForAssistantFirst)|TestCodex_UnifiedDelegation' -count=1` passed; its unified parser ignores added JSON keys.

Notes
The converter follow-up for ENT-3337 will consume ENT-3336's `ReadCalls` rather than parse usage again, update native timestamps where available, and regenerate/review `*_expected.jsonl` fixtures. Copilot, Cursor, external plugins and Antigravity have no native per-call usage to put on assistant lines. Consumers pin a CLI module version; entire-api was checked read-only, not edited. Under laptop CPU contention, two early full-check attempts timed out in the CLI package; a narrower lower-parallelism retry passed, then the complete check passed with `GOMAXPROCS=4 GOFLAGS=-p=1`. For the int64 review fix, the steward corrected one lint finding and reran the full check successfully. {"n":3064,"title":"transcript: a streaming adapter for OpenCode exports","body":"A streaming adapter for OpenCode, so a live consumer can follow a session as it changes with the same mapping `Convert` uses. OpenCode keeps sessions in its database, not in a file to follow, so a live producer runs `opencode export <id>` (1.x) or `opencode session export --standalone <id>` (2.x) after each change and feeds the snapshots.

- `OpenCodeSnapshotLines(export)`: splits an export of either version into one 1.x-shaped message per line (a 2.x export goes through `NormalizeOpenCodeExport`).
- `NewOpenCodeAdapter()`: `Feed`/`Flush`/`Lines`, `Drop(id)`, and `FeedExport(export)`, which feeds every message in order and then drops the ones the export no longer has (a revert, a compaction). A message is keyed by `info.id`, sent again only when its record changed, and replaced in place; a dropped message's next snapshot restores it where it was.
- A pending undo (`info.revert`) hides what OpenCode hides: the reverted message and every later one (for a part revert, that message's parts from it on). Before, the live view showed undone messages until the next prompt. `Convert` still writes them, since the database still holds them.
- `NormalizeOpenCodeExport`, `IsOpenCodeV2Export` and `OpenCodeNativeKey` move into `transcript` from the agent package (its `export_v2.go` is now a thin wrapper, behaviour unchanged).

`Convert` changes, which also change what checkpoints store for OpenCode:
- A tool still `pending` or `running` gets no `result` (it was written as an error, so a live view showed every running tool as failed).
- An assistant message with no text or tool parts gets no line without tokens, and a `"content":null` line with them, so its usage still counts (was `"content":[]`).
- A raw 2.x export converts properly (it converted to almost nothing).

Tests: synthetic 1.x and 2.x exports; the fold equals `Convert` for growing snapshots, drops via `FeedExport` and `Drop` with restore in place, chunked feeding, a hidden empty message keeping its place; undo and redo; the revert rules for both versions. Each behaviour test fails without its code. `lineSplitter` is copied from #2953 (an add/add conflict on `transcript/line_splitter.go` for whichever merges second).

Consumer: `entire stream opencode` in entire-stream, checked end to end against a local entire-api on OpenCode 1.18.33 and 2.2.6 with real replies, undo/redo, resume and an undo made while nothing streamed, each matching the server's snapshot (`stream-replay --check`).

<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Replaces #1559.

## Summary
- Avoid rendering large worker dump markdown through glamour during review finalization.
- Add render-size guardrails and keep finalize/cancel UI state consistent.
- Kill agent process groups on cancellation so review/investigate runs don't hang.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes subprocess teardown (process-group kill) and review finalize/manifest paths; behavior is well-covered by tests but affects cancellation and persistence on Unix review/investigate runs.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes multi-agent **review** runs that appeared stuck on **“Finalizing output…”** by stopping expensive glamour passes over large per-worker dumps and tightening finalize/cancel behavior.
> 
> **Finalize performance:** `DumpSink` now writes **plain markdown** (no `mdrender` on worker narratives). `mdrender.Render` skips glamour above **256KB** and returns raw input. Sink composition drops `DumpSink.RenderWriter`; styling stays on the synthesized final report path.
> 
> **Cancel / hang fixes:** New `procutil.TerminateOnCancel` SIGKILLs the **whole process group** on Unix when the run context is cancelled (plus `WaitDelay`), wired into review `ReviewerTemplate` and investigate turns so grandchildren holding stdout pipes cannot block `Wait`/Ctrl+C indefinitely.
> 
> **Finalize robustness:** Post-review manifest writing uses `context.WithoutCancel` with a **30s** timeout so a late Ctrl+C after workers finish does not drop persisted findings. The review TUI **keeps animating** during finalize (spinner + elapsed), and row status syncs from the orchestrator summary so failed/cancelled agents match the counts line.
> 
> Also adds an auto-generated **pi** extension (`.pi/extensions/entire.ts`) forwarding session/turn hooks to `entire hooks pi`, and reviewer prompt guidance to keep outputs compact.
>

{"n":3175,"title":"fix(transcript): keep OpenCode cache, reasoning and model in condensed transcripts","body":"## The bug

`openCodeMsgToken` declared only `input` and `output`:

```go
type openCodeMsgToken struct {
    Input  int `json:"input"`
    Output int `json:"output"`
}
```

OpenCode exports also carry `reasoning`, `cache.read`, `cache.write`, `total` and a per-message `modelID`. `openCodeRecord` therefore wrote a `CallUsage` with only two fields, and the stored transcript line dropped the rest. Readers of a checkpoint transcript saw:

```json
{"input_tokens":150,"output_tokens":90,"content":[...]}
```

instead of cache read 100, cache write 160 and the model the export reported. Every other adapter keeps what its agent records.

Reasoning has the same problem in a second form: 1.3.16+ stores it apart from output, while older or provider-specific messages already include it. The condensed line's `reasoning_tokens` is a subset of `output_tokens`, so it has to be counted exactly once.

## Reproduction

On `main`, `TestCompact_OpenCodeUsageKeepsCacheReasoningAndModel` produces `cache_read_tokens: 0, cache_write_tokens: 0, reasoning_tokens: 0` and no `model`, although the input export carries `cache:{read:5,write:2}`, `reasoning:40` and `modelID`.

The existing `TestCompact_OpenCodeTokenUsage` input also has cache read 100 / write 160; its expected line omitted both, pinning the loss.

## The fix

- Parse `reasoning`, `cache`, `total` and `modelID` from the export.
- Populate `CallUsage` with cache read/write, reasoning and model.
- Compute output with the same identity the OpenCode agent already uses in `Tokens.OutputWithReasoning`: if `total == input + output + cache.read + cache.write`, reasoning is already inside output; otherwise add it. `reasoning_tokens` then stays a subset of `output_tokens`.

The existing golden fixture is regenerated: every assistant line gains its model and cache counts, and no message in it has reasoning stored apart, so its output counts are unchanged.

## Tests

- New `TestCompact_OpenCodeUsageKeepsCacheReasoningAndModel` covers reasoning stored apart (80 + 40 → 120), reasoning already inside output (total identity → 90), cache counts and model.
- `TestCompact_OpenCodeTokenUsage` now asserts the cache fields it already supplied.
- `go test ./transcript/... ./internal/transcript/...` passes.
- `mise run lint:go`: 0 issues.

Independent of #2823: that PR fixes the agent's `CalculateTokenUsage` path used for checkpoint metadata; this one fixes the stored condensed transcript line itself.","head":"8a9ee8ccdb99d9a3d850ce94bab33c773c0f8c7c","state":"open"}

{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Action completed."}],"structuredContent":{"pull_request":{"url":"https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2210","number":2210,"state":"open","merged":false,"mergeable":false,"draft":false,"body":"<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->

> **Opens against `tokens` (#2155), not `main`.** It needs the `thinking_tokens` /
> `cache_creation_1h_tokens` subset fields and the corrected per-checkpoint scoping from that PR.
> Retarget to `main` once #2155 merges.

## What this does

`entire checkpoint tokens` now says where a checkpoint's tokens went, by billing class, with each
class's share of **volume** and — where a verified per-model price ratio applies — share of **cost**.

```
How it was billed
                     tokens   volume    cost
  Fresh input         42.1k      10%     15%
  Cache write        118.4k      29%     57%  (1h TTL 22k)
  Cache read         240.6k      58%      8%
  Output              11.2k       3%     20%  (thinking 4.1k)
  Total              412.3k
```

The two columns are the point. Cache read is 58% of the volume and 8% of the cost; cache write is
29% of the volume and 57% of the cost. "95% of your tokens are cache reads" tells you nothing;
"57% of your cost is cache writes" does. Today the command prints five totals and no shares at all.

## Agent-agnostic by construction

It reads **no transcript** — the four classes are already normalised into checkpoint metadata by
every agent's parser. So it works for all eight supported agents *and* anything external that lands
a checkpoint. Cursor included: its usage arrives from the stop hook rather than the transcript, so
*per-tool* attribution is impossible for it, but the totals are there and it gets the full block
like everyone else (Cursor token capture landed 2026-05-26 in `fadc4a06a`).

Per-tool drill-down ("which tool burned this") is genuinely per-agent and needs transcript parsing;
that is the next PR, one agent at a time.

## Pricing is withheld rather than guessed

Three cases, each tested:

- **No model recorded** → no verified ratio row, so volume only.
- **Models disagree across a multi-session checkpoint** → one row cannot cover both, and a cost
  column silently covering some sessions is worse than none.
- **A legacy row whose cache-write TTL split is unknowable** → Anthropic bills the two TTLs at 2×
  versus 1.25×, so the split changes the answer. Providers charging a single cache-write rate have
  no ambiguity and are still priced.

Volume shares are always exact — largest-remainder corrected so they sum to 100, never 99 or 101
(mutation-checked: disabling the correction makes a set sum to 98). A checkpoint that recorded
nothing keeps saying so rather than rendering four zeros.

## Bug found and fixed on the way

`addCheckpointTokenUsage` copied five fields by hand and so silently dropped `ThinkingTokens`,
`CacheCreation1hTokens` and `Model` — the subsets this report displays. A test caught it. It now
delegates to `types.AddTokenUsage`, the single summing primitive CLAUDE.md mandates
("a field-by-field copy is how the nested total came to be dropped in the first place"). That
primitive gained saturation so the pre-existing overflow expectation still holds.

## Scope

**1,283 insertions / 52 deletions across 7 files** — roughly 60% of it tests. Long-context tiers are
deliberately not modelled: they are decidable only per call, and this works from a checkpoint total.

Deliberately **not** here: per-tool rows, any transcript read, `session tokens` / `tokens profile`
(next PRs), and deleting the two noisy recommendation rules — that lands with the rules rewrite,
since eight `--agent-brief` branches across three commands depend on them.


## Verified on real checkpoints, six agents, three repos

Built the branch and ran `entire checkpoint tokens` against committed history rather than fixtures.

**Codex — priced** (`gpt-5.4`, real checkpoint in `entirehq/demo-repository`):

```
How it was billed
                     tokens   volume    cost
  Fresh input        126.8k      55%     88%
  Cache write             0       0%      0%
  Cache read         102.5k      44%      7%
  Output               1.3k       1%      5%
  Total              230.7k
```

55% of the volume is 88% of the cost, and 44% of the volume is 7%. That inversion is the whole
argument for the column, on real data.

**Copilot CLI — priced** (`claude-sonnet-4.6`): fresh input 60% volume → 92% cost.

**Claude Code / Gemini CLI / OpenCode — volume only.** Those checkpoints record no model at all, so
withholding cost is correct and the printed reason is accurate.

**Cursor — `Token data: unavailable`**, no breakdown, no zeros. Those checkpoints predate Cursor
token capture (2026-03-04 against a 2026-05-26 feature), so this exercises the no-usage degradation
path rather than an agent limitation.

**This testing found two bugs the unit tests could not**, both fixed here:

- `buildSessionTokensUsage` set `Total` from `totalTokens` (which recurses into subagents) while
  reading its class fields from the top level, so its own parts never summed to its own total.
  Rendering the breakdown beside it turned that into two contradictory lists under the same labels
  on a real 50M-token checkpoint. Flattened at the source; all three commands now agree.
- A class holding 274.8k tokens printed `0%`. Now `<1%`; a genuinely empty class still prints `0%`.

**One thing to know about scope:** every checkpoint in this repo's own history predates the
`token_usage_version: 2` stamp *and* has cache writes, so the TTL rule withholds cost on all of
them. The cost column lights up once #2155 ships and new checkpoints accumulate — and immediately on
cache-write-free checkpoints, which is why Codex and Copilot price fine today.

This replaces #2165, which reached 19.5k lines and was closed. The plan now slices per command with

1,283 after two review passes and real-checkpoint testing found further bugs. Every increment is

The four class values in `--json`'s `tokens` object — `input`, `cache_read`, `cache_write`,
`output` — **now include subagent usage**, and so does the same line in the human output. Before
this PR they excluded it while `tokens.total` included it, so the parts did not sum to their own

one label, which is what forced the fix.

`tokens.total` is unchanged. No key is removed, renamed, or reshaped. But a consumer reading the
four class values will see larger numbers, so this is a behaviour change rather than an additive
one, and it is listed in the changelog below.

The same flattening reaches `entire session tokens`, which PR 2 otherwise owns — unavoidable, since

The cost column had never rendered outside a unit test: no checkpoint in this repo's history is
priceable (all 99 predate the cache-write TTL split, and none carries `token_usage_version`). So it

```
  Fresh input           42k      10%     15%
  Cache write          118k      29%     58%  (1h TTL 22k)
  Cache read           240k      58%      8%
  Output                11k       3%     19%  (thinking 4k)
  Total                411k
```

Writer stored `thinking_tokens: 4000`, `cache_creation_1h_tokens: 22000` and stamped

## Also in this PR

- **`formatTokenCount` scales past `k`.** A 286M cache-read total rendered as `286344.6k` — nine
  characters whose magnitude you have to count digits to recover, in the one column a token report
  exists to communicate. It now carries M and B, promoting on the carry so 999,999 reads `1M` and
  never `1000k`. Seven golden expectations updated.
- **A command-level test for the priced path**, parsing the volume and cost percentages back out of
  the rendered table so the acceptance criterion is asserted on what a user sees. Mutation-checked
  both ways: forcing the model unpriced and skewing one cost share by 1 each fail it.
- **Overflow hardening across the token math** (three commits, from gate findings): the class
  flattening is bounded at `types.MaxSubagentDepth` and every sum saturates; `clampAdd` saturates at
  both int edges, not just the top (`clampAdd(minInt, -1)` returned `maxInt`); and `Total` and the
  four classes now come from one walk via `sumTokenClasses`, so they cannot disagree on a malformed
  chain.
- **A class the provider does not bill prints `0%`, not `<1%`.** `openai-6x`, `openai-8x` and the
  Gemini families define no `CacheWrite` weights, so a cache-write class with real tokens costs
  exactly nothing; `<1%` claimed a fraction of a percent the user is never charged. The contrast is

pull_request.body:
## Description
Fixes #3052.

### Background
On Unix, `execx.TerminateOnCancel` and `procutil.TerminateOnCancel` configure a new process group (`Setpgid = true`) and send `SIGKILL` to `-cmd.Process.Pid` on cancellation to terminate the entire process group.
On Windows, `killProcessGroupOnCancel` was previously a no-op stub:
```go
func killProcessGroupOnCancel(_ *exec.Cmd) {}
```
This fell back to Go's default `Cancel` behavior, which calls `TerminateProcess` on the direct child only. Because Windows does not automatically terminate child processes when a parent process exits, any descendants spawned by the child (such as `git-remote-https.exe`, `ssh.exe`, MCP servers, subagents, or clean filters) remained running in the background. Whenever descendants inherited stdout/stderr pipes, `cmd.Wait()` blocked for the full `KillWaitDelay` (10s in `execx`, 5s in `procutil`), causing noticeable delays and leaking running processes and pack file locks.

### Solution
1. **`execx.KillProcessTree(rootPid int)`**:
   - Uses `windows.CreateToolhelp32Snapshot(windows.TH32CS_SNAPPROCESS, 0)` to capture running processes and map parent-child relationships.
   - Traverses the process hierarchy to find all descendants of `rootPid`.
   - **PID Reuse Protection**: Queries `GetProcessTimes` on the root process and candidates, ensuring only processes created after the root process started are treated as descendants.
   - Terminates descendants bottom-up (deepest leaves first) before terminating the root process.
   - Falls back gracefully to direct process termination if taking the snapshot fails.

2. **Integration**:
   - Configures `cmd.Cancel` in `execx_windows.go` to invoke `KillProcessTree(cmd.Process.Pid)`.
   - Configures `cmd.Cancel` in `procutil_windows.go` to invoke `execx.KillProcessTree(cmd.Process.Pid)`.

3. **Tests**:
   - Added `TestTerminateOnCancel_SetsWaitDelayAndCancelWindows` and `TestTerminateOnCancel_KillsProcessTreeWindows` in `cmd/entire/cli/execx/execx_windows_test.go`.
   - Added `TestTerminateOnCancel_UnblocksGrandchildHoldingPipeWindows` in `cmd/entire/cli/procutil/procutil_windows_test.go`.
   - Both tests verify that a background grandchild process holding the stdout pipe is cleanly terminated and `cmd.Wait()` unblocks immediately without waiting for `WaitDelay`.

## Verification
Tested on a native Windows machine:
- Grandchild process holding the output pipe unblocks in **<10ms** upon context cancellation.
- Grandchild process (`ping.exe`) is confirmed terminated from the system process table.
- Verified that `go build ./cmd/entire` and `go vet` pass cleanly.

Slice 2a of ENT-3337: the Claude Code converter now writes pricing-grade per-call usage on assistant lines of `transcript.jsonl`.

**Base is `main`** (slice 1, #2834, has merged). Slice 2b (Codex converter, #2859) is stacked on this PR.

## What
- Every Claude Code assistant line that carries usage gets the call's `model`, fresh `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cache_read_tokens`, `cache_write_tokens`, and the 5m/1h cache-write split when Claude reports both durations. This follows the contract merged in #2834: `model` is omitted when the source reports none, Claude Code's `<synthetic>` placeholder is never taken as a model, and `input_tokens` excludes the same line's cache fields.
- Streaming fragments of one message ID merge to one line using the fragment row with the strictly highest `output_tokens` (earlier wins ties) and the first reported model; the line keeps the last fragment's timestamp.
- A tool result between fragments of the same message ID no longer double counts: later fragments become continuation lines without usage, and an improved snapshot updates the call's first visible line through a `usage` record.
- Additive optional `Record.Usage` (`CallUsage`) on the record wire format, documented in `transcript/README.md`. Records get their own copy of each snapshot.
- `NewClaudeAdapter` emits per-call usage; `NewCursorAdapter` and `NewDroidAdapter` keep legacy counts. `Convert` builds its JSONL adapters with the same constructors (`opts.Agent == "claude-code"` picks the Claude one), so live streams and checkpoints share one source of records. entire-stream needs only a library bump.

## Check
`mise run check` is green apart from `TestOpenCodeSeedRepoPlantsDeps`, which also fails on `main` locally (OpenCode 2 install). Focused: `go test ./transcript/ -run 'ClaudeUsage|Fold|ExportedConstructors|UsageSnapshot|LateUsage' -count=1`. Outside the usage fields, the regenerated `transcript/testdata/claude_expected*.jsonl` match `main` exactly; in `claude_expected2.jsonl` interleaved message IDs carry usage on exactly one line.

## Notes
- Per-call usage must be read from the full converted transcript: in a checkpoint slice, a usage row that arrives after a tool result lands on the call's first line, which can sit before the slice boundary (documented in the README, pinned by `TestConvertWithBoundary_LateUsageLandsBeforeBoundary`). Current Claude Code writes identical usage on every fragment of a message, so this only shows with older versions.
- Continuation lines no longer repeat `input_tokens`/`output_tokens`, so legacy-field sums over stored checkpoints drop for split calls; that is the double-count fix.
- No exported native-reader API (`transcript/` stays conversion-only).

{"n":2782,"title":"Count session and checkpoint tokens from each agent's running total","state":"closed","body":"<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/entireio/-/trails/2250/changes/cli/1579
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Makes token accounting correct by construction. Today `entire` works out each checkpoint's tokens by slicing transcripts at offsets, and every double count and undercount we've found comes from those slices starting or ending in the wrong place: turns without file changes went missing (Claude Code `entire status` showed 64k against 285k actually spent), a repeated Stop on a turn that changed files counts the turn twice, a message whose lines straddle an agent's mid-turn commit counts twice, and Copilot counts cache twice.

This PR has each session keep the agent's own running total (the **token ledger**), and each checkpoint store what that total grew by since the session's previous checkpoint.

## 1. One shared reader for every agent
`agent.ReadCumulativeUsage` reads a session's running total for any agent. It owns the files:
- it reads only the bytes appended since the last reading (a no-op reading costs under 1ms), and waits for a line's end;
- it detects a rewritten transcript (the 512 bytes before its last offset no longer match) and reads it again, reporting `Restarted`;
- it reads a small or rewritten file (OpenCode's export, Droid's `settings.json`, a Claude Code subagent) whole, only when its size or last bytes changed, and never reports that as a restart;
- it never follows a symlink or opens a FIFO beside the transcript, and reads `.entire` through its confined reader.

Each agent supplies a `UsageCounter` (50–150 lines) built from shared parts in `agent/usage_counting.go`:
- `KeyedUsage` counts per-call records once per key, with the agent's rule for a repeated record (`KeepFirst` for replays, `KeepLast` for records re-written, `KeepMostOutput` for streamed messages), a window of open records per file, and per-child sums;
- `RunningTotal` sums running totals across a counter restart; `KeyedUsage.CoveredBy` combines records with a running total where an agent writes both.

| Agent | What it counts |
|---|---|
| Claude Code | Assistant messages by `message.id`, most output winning; subagents (and their subagents, Workflow agents) as children |
| Codex | `token_usage_record` by `response_id` (replays keep the first copy), combined with segment-summed `token_count` totals; children from the session's subagent inventory |
| Copilot CLI | `session.usage_record` by `apiCallId` (cache split out of input), combined with `session.shutdown` totals, which include subagents, so their records are subtracted |
| OpenCode | The export's assistant messages, reasoning counted once |
| Pi | Per-message usage on every branch |
| Factory Droid | `settings.json`'s `tokenUsage`, one call per assistant message |
| Antigravity | `PLANNER_RESPONSE` step usage by step index |

Child sessions (Droid Workers, OpenCode child sessions) are not read here: #2824's child-session credit counts them once, and ledger checkpoints add it as the per-turn path does.

## 2. The token ledger
- `SessionState.TokenLedger` (`session/token_ledger.go`, `strategy/token_ledger.go`) holds the running total, read **under the session lock** at turn start, every Stop and every condensation. `TokenUsage` is its total; a checkpoint stores its pending growth; a successful checkpoint write (or attach) marks it checkpointed, and that mark never moves back.
  - A repeated or concurrent Stop reads the same total, so it adds nothing — including on a turn that changed files.
  - A commit in the middle of a turn stores everything up to the commit; the rest lands in the next checkpoint. A message straddling that commit counts once.
- **Which sessions:** sessions this CLI starts at a turn start, for the seven agents above. Legacy states, states created at Stop or by attach, Cursor, Vogon and external agents keep today's per-turn path unchanged.
- **Takes over at the first reading with usage**; what the per-turn accounting already checkpointed counts as checkpointed.
- **Rewritten transcripts:** a lower reading is ignored (a stale copy), unless the transcript restarted: then the difference moves to `Base` and the total carries on.
- **Stop** skips the per-turn token calculation for ledger sessions (for Claude Code it read every subagent transcript only to be discarded).
- **Session end** takes a last reading, so usage an agent writes after its final Stop (Copilot's shutdown totals) is counted.
- **A new transcript path** for the session is read as a restart, so history the new file repeats is not counted twice.
- **Attach** reads the transcript being attached, updates session state under the session lock, and marks as checkpointed exactly what its checkpoint stored.
- **Checkpoint metadata** adds `session_token_usage`, the session's running total at that checkpoint, next to `token_usage`.

## Checked
- **Real sessions, old vs new:** 726 local sessions across six agents on the final code (154 Copilot, 302 Codex, 149 Claude Code, 39 Antigravity, 37 Pi, 45 Droid), plus 36 OpenCode exports on an earlier revision: the shared reader gives exactly the totals of the per-agent code it replaces, and reading each file in nine pieces gives the same totals as one read. The only difference is intended: Droid Workers are no longer the ledger's children (13 sessions), because #2824's child-session credit counts them. Worst incremental step 126ms; largest cursor 38KB (a Claude session with 190 subagents: 123KB).
- **Live sessions** (`e2e/tests/token_ledger_test.go`): turns that changed files, one that changed nothing, and an agent commit mid-turn; for every session, checkpoints plus pending equal the session total, which equals a fresh read of the agent's files. Passes for all seven agents: Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, OpenCode, Pi, Droid and Antigravity.

## Tests
- `TestUsageCounters_Conformance`: every agent with a counter needs a fixture in `testdata/usage/<agent>/`, read whole, in pieces cut at and around every line end, and after a rewrite.
- Reader tests: partial lines, rewrites, whole files, symlinked files beside the transcript, files that fail to read and return, moved files, the per-file window, merge policies.
- Ledger unit and strategy tests: repeated readings, growth, stale reads, rewrites, child high-water marks, handover from the per-turn accounting, attach under the lock, adopt's copy.
- Integration through the real hooks: Claude Code (repeated Stop on a file-changing turn, no-change turns between commits, mid-turn agent commit, a message straddling it, a subagent finishing in a later turn, a rewritten transcript), Codex (repeated Stop, mid-turn commit), Droid (Worker plus the parent's second Stop). With the ledger off, the repeated Stop and the straddling message fail.

`mise run lint`: 0 issues. Unit and integration suites pass.

Size: +3016/-56 in total.

## Not in this PR / known limits
- External agents keep the per-turn accounting (the protocol has no incremental token call).
- A session's first reading reads its files whole (1.3s on an 82MB Claude transcript with 190 subagents); every later reading reads what was appended. Codex children are read through the inventory again only when a child file changed.
- Only an appended transcript can report a rewrite; for an OpenCode undo, or a Droid rewrite, a lower total is ignored until the total passes the old one — an undercount, not a double count.
- A crash between a checkpoint write and the state save can store the same growth twice (true of main's accounting too).
- A session whose state was lost counts from its next turn start; seeding from the latest checkpoint's `session_token_usage` is a follow-up. Deleting the per-turn path once legacy states age out, and server use of `session_token_usage`, are follow-ups.
- Overlaps #2856 (mid-turn double count): for ledger sessions it is superseded; whichever lands second reconciles.
