{"n":2210,"title":"feat(tokens): billing-class breakdown for every agent","state":"open","body":"<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1198
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

> **Opens against `tokens` (#2155), not `main`.** It needs the `thinking_tokens` /
> `cache_creation_1h_tokens` subset fields and the corrected per-checkpoint scoping from that PR.
> Retarget to `main` once #2155 merges.

## What this does

`entire checkpoint tokens` now says where a checkpoint's tokens went, by billing class, with each
class's share of **volume** and — where a verified per-model price ratio applies — share of **cost**.

```
How it was billed
                     tokens   volume    cost
  Fresh input         42.1k      10%     15%
  Cache write        118.4k      29%     57%  (1h TTL 22k)
  Cache read         240.6k      58%      8%
  Output              11.2k       3%     20%  (thinking 4.1k)
  Total              412.3k
```

The two columns are the point. Cache read is 58% of the volume and 8% of the cost; cache write is
29% of the volume and 57% of the cost. "95% of your tokens are cache reads" tells you nothing;
"57% of your cost is cache writes" does. Today the command prints five totals and no shares at all.

## Agent-agnostic by construction

It reads **no transcript** — the four classes are already normalised into checkpoint metadata by
every agent's parser. So it works for all eight supported agents *and* anything external that lands
a checkpoint. Cursor included: its usage arrives from the stop hook rather than the transcript, so
*per-tool* attribution is impossible for it, but the totals are there and it gets the full block
like everyone else (Cursor token capture landed 2026-05-26 in `fadc4a06a`).

Per-tool drill-down ("which tool burned this") is genuinely per-agent and needs transcript parsing;
that is the next PR, one agent at a time.

## Pricing is withheld rather than guessed

Three cases, each tested:

- **No model recorded** → no verified ratio row, so volume only.
- **Models disagree across a multi-session checkpoint** → one row cannot cover both, and a cost
  column silently covering some sessions is worse than none.
- **A legacy row whose cache-write TTL split is unknowable** → Anthropic bills the two TTLs at 2×
  versus 1.25×, so the split changes the answer. Providers charging a single cache-write rate have
  no ambiguity and are still priced.

Volume shares are always exact — largest-remainder corrected so they sum to 100, never 99 or 101
(mutation-checked: disabling the correction makes a set sum to 98). A checkpoint that recorded
nothing keeps saying so rather than rendering four zeros.

## Bug found and fixed on the way

`addCheckpointTokenUsage` copied five fields by hand and so silently dropped `ThinkingTokens`,
`CacheCreation1hTokens` and `Model` — the subsets this report displays. A test caught it. It now
delegates to `types.AddTokenUsage`, the single summing primitive CLAUDE.md mandates
("a field-by-field copy is how the nested total came to be dropped in the first place"). That
primitive gained saturation so the pre-existing overflow expectation still holds.

## Scope

**1,283 insertions / 52 deletions across 7 files** — roughly 60% of it tests. Long-context tiers are
deliberately not modelled: they are decidable only per call, and this works from a checkpoint total.

Deliberately **not** here: per-tool rows, any transcript read, `session tokens` / `tokens profile`
(next PRs), and deleting the two noisy recommendation rules — that lands with the rules rewrite,
since eight `--agent-brief` branches across three commands depend on them.


## Verified on real checkpoints, six agents, three repos

Built the branch and ran `entire checkpoint tokens` against committed history rather than fixtures.

**Codex — priced** (`gpt-5.4`, real checkpoint in `entirehq/demo-repository`):

```
How it was billed
                     tokens   volume    cost
  Fresh input        126.8k      55%     88%
  Cache write             0       0%      0%
  Cache read         102.5k      44%      7%
  Output               1.3k       1%      5%
  Total              230.7k
```

55% of the volume is 88% of the cost, and 44% of the volume is 7%. That inversion is the whole
argument for the column, on real data.

**Copilot CLI — priced** (`claude-sonnet-4.6`): fresh input 60% volume → 92% cost.

**Claude Code / Gemini CLI / OpenCode — volume only.** Those checkpoints record no model at all, so
withholding cost is correct and the printed reason is accurate.

**Cursor — `Token data: unavailable`**, no breakdown, no zeros. Those checkpoints predate Cursor
token capture (2026-03-04 against a 2026-05-26 feature), so this exercises the no-usage degradation
path rather than an agent limitation.

**This testing found two bugs the unit tests could not**, both fixed here:

- `buildSessionTokensUsage` set `Total` from `totalTokens` (which recurses into subagents) while
  reading its class fields from the top level, so its own parts never summed to its own total.
  Rendering the breakdown beside it turned that into two contradictory lists under the same labels
  on a real 50M-token checkpoint. Flattened at the source; all three commands now agree.
- A class holding 274.8k tokens printed `0%`. Now `<1%`; a genuinely empty class still prints `0%`.

**One thing to know about scope:** every checkpoint in this repo's own history predates the
`token_usage_version: 2` stamp *and* has cache writes, so the TTL rule withholds cost on all of
them. The cost column lights up once #2155 ships and new checkpoints accumulate — and immediately on
cache-write-free checkpoints, which is why Codex and Copilot price fine today.

## Context

This replaces #2165, which reached 19.5k lines and was closed. The plan now slices per command with
a hard per-PR size budget. This PR overran its 700-line budget substantially: 836 at first review, then
1,283 after two review passes and real-checkpoint testing found further bugs. Every increment is
recorded in the commit history rather than absorbed silently, but the budget did not hold, and PR 2's
number is being set against that experience rather than against the original estimate.

## Test plan

- Every behaviour test-first; the share correction and the pricing rules are mutation-checked.
- `mise run fmt && mise run lint`: 0 issues.
- `mise run test:ci`: green (integration + both canaries, 56 and 4).

## Consumer-visible change to existing figures (not additive)

The four class values in `--json`'s `tokens` object — `input`, `cache_read`, `cache_write`,
`output` — **now include subagent usage**, and so does the same line in the human output. Before
this PR they excluded it while `tokens.total` included it, so the parts did not sum to their own
total: on a real checkpoint from this repo's history the shortfall was **29,099,852 tokens, exactly
`subagent_total`**. Rendering a class breakdown beside those figures put two different answers under
one label, which is what forced the fix.

`tokens.total` is unchanged. No key is removed, renamed, or reshaped. But a consumer reading the
four class values will see larger numbers, so this is a behaviour change rather than an additive
one, and it is listed in the changelog below.

The same flattening reaches `entire session tokens`, which PR 2 otherwise owns — unavoidable, since
both commands read the same figures through `buildSessionTokensUsage`, and leaving one command
wrong was worse than the small scope overlap. On the session used to test this, the old output
understated the four classes by 45,871k — **15% of the session total** unaccounted for.

**New `--json` keys**, both additive: `classes` (the breakdown itself) and, inside each class,
`cost_zero`. The latter exists because a `cost_percent` of `0` is ambiguous — see the rendering fix
below — and a consumer needs the same distinction the table now makes.

## Verified end-to-end, not just in tests

The cost column had never rendered outside a unit test: no checkpoint in this repo's history is
priceable (all 99 predate the cache-write TTL split, and none carries `token_usage_version`). So it
was driven through the real pipeline — fresh repo, `entire enable`, real `session-start` /
`user-prompt-submit` / `stop` hooks, real `git commit` triggering post-commit condensation, then read
back — with #2155's writer and this PR's reader in the same binary:

```
                     tokens   volume    cost
  Fresh input           42k      10%     15%
  Cache write          118k      29%     58%  (1h TTL 22k)
  Cache read           240k      58%      8%
  Output                11k       3%     19%  (thinking 4k)
  Total                411k
```

Writer stored `thinking_tokens: 4000`, `cache_creation_1h_tokens: 22000` and stamped
`token_usage_version: 2`; reader returned `priced: true`, volume summing to 100 and cost summing to
100. Separately, `checkpoint tokens --json` was run over **all 99 committed checkpoints**: zero
non-zero exits, zero volume shares off 100%, zero disagreements between the rendered classes and the
stored metadata.

## Also in this PR

- **`formatTokenCount` scales past `k`.** A 286M cache-read total rendered as `286344.6k` — nine
  characters whose magnitude you have to count digits to recover, in the one column a token report
  exists to communicate. It now carries M and B, promoting on the carry so 999,999 reads `1M` and
  never `1000k`. Seven golden expectations updated.
- **A command-level test for the priced path**, parsing the volume and cost percentages back out of
  the rendered table so the acceptance criterion is asserted on what a user sees. Mutation-checked
  both ways: forcing the model unpriced and skewing one cost share by 1 each fail it.
- **Overflow hardening across the token math** (three commits, from gate findings): the class
  flattening is bounded at `types.MaxSubagentDepth` and every sum saturates; `clampAdd` saturates at
  both int edges, not just the top (`clampAdd(minInt, -1)` returned `maxInt`); and `Total` and the
  four classes now come from one walk via `sumTokenClasses`, so they cannot disagree on a malformed
  chain.
- **A class the provider does not bill prints `0%`, not `<1%`.** `openai-6x`, `openai-8x` and the
  Gemini families define no `CacheWrite` weights, so a cache-write class with real tokens costs
  exactly nothing; `<1%` claimed a fraction of a percent the user is never charged. The contrast is
  the feature working as intended — the same 90k of cache writes: `26% / 0%` on gpt-5.5,
  `26% / 52%` on claude-sonnet-4.6.
- **A withheld-cost reason that names the real case.** `unpricedMixedModels` appeared exactly once
  in the tree — its own declaration — and was never assigned, so a checkpoint mixing
  `claude-sonnet-4.6` and `gpt-5.3-codex`, both individually priceable, was told "no verified price
  ratios for this checkpoint's model". It now says their ratios differ.

## Deferred, tracked in the plan's known-bugs list

Same shape — unbounded or unaudited arithmetic over push-writable metadata — and none can
contradict a printed figure: `subagentModelsMatch`'s unbounded `SubagentTokens` walk (dismissed on
the trail with this reason), `SubagentTotal`'s unbounded `totalTokens` walk, and the un-audited
`exactPercents` / weighting math. One small follow-up together.

## Changelog additions

### Changed
- `entire checkpoint tokens` and `entire session tokens` now report per-class token figures that
  include subagent usage, so the four classes sum to the reported total. Previously the classes
  excluded subagent tokens while the total included them, understating each class (`tokens.total`
  in `--json` is unchanged; the four class values are larger) ([#2210](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2210))
- Token counts above a million are formatted as `M`/`B` rather than large `k` values, e.g.
  `286.3M` instead of `286344.6k` ([#2210](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2210))

### Fixed
- A billing class its provider does not charge for now shows a `0%` cost share instead of `<1%`
  ([#2210](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2210))
- A checkpoint whose sessions use models with different price ratios now says so, instead of
  claiming its model has no verified price ratios ([#2210](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2210))

{"n":3102,"title":"feat(execx,procutil): terminate process tree on Windows when context is cancelled","state":"open","body":"## Description
Fixes #3052.

### Background
On Unix, `execx.TerminateOnCancel` and `procutil.TerminateOnCancel` configure a new process group (`Setpgid = true`) and send `SIGKILL` to `-cmd.Process.Pid` on cancellation to terminate the entire process group.
On Windows, `killProcessGroupOnCancel` was previously a no-op stub:
```go
func killProcessGroupOnCancel(_ *exec.Cmd) {}
```
This fell back to Go's default `Cancel` behavior, which calls `TerminateProcess` on the direct child only. Because Windows does not automatically terminate child processes when a parent process exits, any descendants spawned by the child (such as `git-remote-https.exe`, `ssh.exe`, MCP servers, subagents, or clean filters) remained running in the background. Whenever descendants inherited stdout/stderr pipes, `cmd.Wait()` blocked for the full `KillWaitDelay` (10s in `execx`, 5s in `procutil`), causing noticeable delays and leaking running processes and pack file locks.

### Solution
1. **`execx.KillProcessTree(rootPid int)`**:
   - Uses `windows.CreateToolhelp32Snapshot(windows.TH32CS_SNAPPROCESS, 0)` to capture running processes and map parent-child relationships.
   - Traverses the process hierarchy to find all descendants of `rootPid`.
   - **PID Reuse Protection**: Queries `GetProcessTimes` on the root process and candidates, ensuring only processes created after the root process started are treated as descendants.
   - Terminates descendants bottom-up (deepest leaves first) before terminating the root process.
   - Falls back gracefully to direct process termination if taking the snapshot fails.

2. **Integration**:
   - Configures `cmd.Cancel` in `execx_windows.go` to invoke `KillProcessTree(cmd.Process.Pid)`.
   - Configures `cmd.Cancel` in `procutil_windows.go` to invoke `execx.KillProcessTree(cmd.Process.Pid)`.

3. **Tests**:
   - Added `TestTerminateOnCancel_SetsWaitDelayAndCancelWindows` and `TestTerminateOnCancel_KillsProcessTreeWindows` in `cmd/entire/cli/execx/execx_windows_test.go`.
   - Added `TestTerminateOnCancel_UnblocksGrandchildHoldingPipeWindows` in `cmd/entire/cli/procutil/procutil_windows_test.go`.
   - Both tests verify that a background grandchild process holding the stdout pipe is cleanly terminated and `cmd.Wait()` unblocks immediately without waiting for `WaitDelay`.

## Verification
Tested on a native Windows machine:
- Grandchild process holding the output pipe unblocks in **<10ms** upon context cancellation.
- Grandchild process (`ping.exe`) is confirmed terminated from the system process table.
- Verified that `go build ./cmd/entire` and `go vet` pass cleanly.
"}

import subprocess,json,pathlib,concurrent.futures
out=pathlib.Path('/Users/puneetpalsingh/.codex/entire-pr-review-2026-11-17/public');out.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
def api(path):return json.loads(subprocess.check_output(['gh','api',path],text=True))
prs=[]
for page in range(1,8):
 rows=api(f'repos/entireio/cli/pulls?state=open&per_page=100&page={page}');prs+=rows
 if len(rows)<100:break
(out/'open-prs.json').write_text(json.dumps(prs))
def files(p):
 n=p['number'];rows=[]
 for page in range(1,15):
  x=api(f'repos/entireio/cli/pulls/{n}/files?per_page=100&page={page}');rows+=x
  if len(x)<100:break
 (out/f'{n}-files.json').write_text(json.dumps(rows))
 return {'n':n,'title':p['title'],'head':p['head']['sha'],'paths':[x['filename'] for x in rows]}
with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=6) as pool: results=list(pool.map(files,prs))
(out/'all-open-file-inventory.json').write_text(json.dumps(results))
paths={'cmd/entire/cli/review/types/template.go','transcript/opencode.go','transcript/opencode_records.go'}
hits=[x for x in results if paths.intersection(x['paths'])]
print(json.dumps({'count':len(prs),'hits':hits},indent=2))
PY

# Contributing to the Entire CLI

Thank you for your interest in contributing to Entire! We welcome contributions from everyone.

Please read our [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) before participating.

> **New to Entire?** See the [README](README.md) for setup and usage documentation.

---

## Before You Code: Discuss First

The fastest way to get a contribution merged is to align with maintainers before writing code. Please **open an issue first** using our [issue templates](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues/new/choose) and wait for maintainer feedback before starting implementation.

### Contribution Workflow

1. **Open an issue** describing the problem or feature
2. **Wait for maintainer feedback** -- we may have relevant context or plans
3. **Get approval** before starting implementation
4. **Submit your PR** referencing the approved issue
5. **Address all feedback** including automated Copilot comments
6. **Maintainer review and merge**

---

## First-Time Contributors

**New to open source or to Entire?** Start with the [First-Time Contributors Guide](docs/first-time-contributors.md). It walks through the full path: finding an issue, forking, setting up your dev environment, opening a PR, and what to expect afterwards.

The rest of this document is the reference for ongoing contributors.

---

## Submitting Issues

All feature requests, bug reports, and general issues should be submitted through [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues). Please search for existing issues before opening a new one.

For security-related issues, see the Security section below.

---

## Security

If you discover a security vulnerability, **do not report it through GitHub Issues**. Instead, please follow the instructions in our [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) file for responsible disclosure. All security reports are kept confidential as described in SECURITY.md.

---

## Contributions & Communication

Contributions and communications are expected to occur through:

- [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues) - Bug reports and feature requests
- [Discord](https://discord.gg/jZJs3Tue4S) - Questions, general conversation, and real-time support

Please represent the project and community respectfully in all public and private interactions.


## How to Contribute


There are many ways to contribute:

- **Feature requests** - Open a [GitHub Issue](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues) to discuss your idea
- **Bug reports** - Report issues via [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues) (see [Reporting Bugs](#reporting-bugs))
- **Code contributions** - Fix bugs, add features, improve tests
- **Documentation** - Improve guides, fix typos, add examples
- **Community** - Help others, answer questions, share knowledge


## Reporting Bugs

Good bug reports help us fix issues quickly. When reporting a bug, please include:

### Required Information

1. **Entire CLI version** - run `entire version`
2. **Operating system**
3. **Go version** - run `go version`

### What to Include

Please answer these questions in your bug report:

1. **What did you do?** - Include the exact commands you ran
2. **What did you expect to happen?**
3. **What actually happened?** - Include the full error message or unexpected output
4. **Can you reproduce it?** - Does it happen every time or intermittently?
5. **Any additional context?** - Logs, screenshots, or related issues

## Local Setup

### Prerequisites

- **Go 1.27.3+** - Check with `go version`. `go.mod` pins the minimum, so an older toolchain fails unless it can download the pinned one (`GOTOOLCHAIN=local` cannot).
- **mise** - Task runner and version manager. Install with `curl https://mise.run | sh`

### Clone and Install

```bash
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/entireio/cli.git
cd cli

# Trust the mise configuration (required on first setup)
mise trust

# Install dependencies (mise will install the correct Go version)
mise install

# Download Go modules
go mod download

# Build the CLI
mise run build

# Verify setup by running tests
mise run test
```

# Contributing to the Entire CLI

Thank you for your interest in contributing to Entire! We welcome contributions from everyone.

Please read our [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) before participating.

> **New to Entire?** See the [README](README.md) for setup and usage documentation.

---

## Before You Code: Discuss First

The fastest way to get a contribution merged is to align with maintainers before writing code. Please **open an issue first** using our [issue templates](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues/new/choose) and wait for maintainer feedback before starting implementation.

### Contribution Workflow

1. **Open an issue** describing the problem or feature
2. **Wait for maintainer feedback** -- we may have relevant context or plans
3. **Get approval** before starting implementation
4. **Submit your PR** referencing the approved issue
5. **Address all feedback** including automated Copilot comments
6. **Maintainer review and merge**

---

## First-Time Contributors

**New to open source or to Entire?** Start with the [First-Time Contributors Guide](docs/first-time-contributors.md). It walks through the full path: finding an issue, forking, setting up your dev environment, opening a PR, and what to expect afterwards.

The rest of this document is the reference for ongoing contributors.

---

## Submitting Issues

All feature requests, bug reports, and general issues should be submitted through [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues). Please search for existing issues before opening a new one.

For security-related issues, see the Security section below.

---

## Security

If you discover a security vulnerability, **do not report it through GitHub Issues**. Instead, please follow the instructions in our [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) file for responsible disclosure. All security reports are kept confidential as described in SECURITY.md.

---

## Contributions & Communication

Contributions and communications are expected to occur through:

- [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues) - Bug reports and feature requests
- [Discord](https://discord.gg/jZJs3Tue4S) - Questions, general conversation, and real-time support

Please represent the project and community respectfully in all public and private interactions.


## How to Contribute


There are many ways to contribute:

- **Feature requests** - Open a [GitHub Issue](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues) to discuss your idea
- **Bug reports** - Report issues via [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues) (see [Reporting Bugs](#reporting-bugs))
- **Code contributions** - Fix bugs, add features, improve tests
- **Documentation** - Improve guides, fix typos, add examples
- **Community** - Help others, answer questions, share knowledge


## Reporting Bugs

Good bug reports help us fix issues quickly. When reporting a bug, please include:

### Required Information

1. **Entire CLI version** - run `entire version`
2. **Operating system**
3. **Go version** - run `go version`

### What to Include

Please answer these questions in your bug report:

1. **What did you do?** - Include the exact commands you ran
2. **What did you expect to happen?**
3. **What actually happened?** - Include the full error message or unexpected output
4. **Can you reproduce it?** - Does it happen every time or intermittently?
5. **Any additional context?** - Logs, screenshots, or related issues

---

## Local Setup

### Prerequisites

- **Go 1.27.3+** - Check with `go version`. `go.mod` pins the minimum, so an older toolchain fails unless it can download the pinned one (`GOTOOLCHAIN=local` cannot).
- **mise** - Task runner and version manager. Install with `curl https://mise.run | sh`

### Clone and Install

```bash
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/entireio/cli.git
cd cli

# Trust the mise configuration (required on first setup)
mise trust

# Install dependencies (mise will install the correct Go version)
mise install

# Download Go modules
go mod download

# Build the CLI
mise run build

# Verify setup by running tests
mise run test
```

The repo includes a `.devcontainer/` configuration that installs the system packages used by local development and CI (`git`, `tmux`, `gnome-keyring`, etc) and then bootstraps the repo's `mise` toolchain.

Open the folder in a Dev Container, or start it from the `devcontainer` CLI as follows:

devcontainer up --workspace-folder .

#!/bin/sh
#MISE description="Run E2E canary tests with deterministic agents (no API calls)"
#USAGE arg "[filter]" help="Test name filter (regex)" default=""

set -eu

exe=""
case "$(uname -s)" in
  MINGW* | MSYS* | CYGWIN*) exe=".exe" ;;
esac

# Build entire CLI
mise run build
# go build -o adds no .exe even on Windows; the harness copies this to
# entire.exe beside it (ensureHookEntireBinary), which is what hooks and
# exec's extension lookup then find.
export E2E_ENTIRE_BIN="$PWD/entire"

# Build vogon binary. Go's PATH lookup on Windows only finds it with .exe.
go build -o "vogon$exe" ./e2e/vogon
# mise hands a Windows shell $PWD as D:/a/..., whose drive colon would split a
# PATH entry; prepend the POSIX form, which the shell converts back for Go.
bin_dir="$PWD"
if [ -n "$exe" ]; then
  bin_dir="$(cygpath -u "$PWD")"
fi
E2E_PATH="$bin_dir:$PATH"

if [ -z "${E2E_ARTIFACT_DIR:-}" ]; then
  E2E_ARTIFACT_DIR="$PWD/e2e/artifacts/canary-$(date +%Y-%m-%dT%H-%M-%S)"
fi
export E2E_ARTIFACT_DIR
mkdir -p "$E2E_ARTIFACT_DIR"
echo "artifacts: $E2E_ARTIFACT_DIR"

filter="${usage_filter:-}"
vogon_rc=0
rr_rc=0

# --- vogon: runs all tests (built-in agent) ---
echo "--- canary: vogon ---"

# Preflight, mirroring the roger-roger check below: vogon registers itself only
# if its binary is on PATH when the test binary starts. Without it nothing
# registers, every test skips, and the lane exits 0 having run nothing.
if ! PATH="$E2E_PATH" command -v vogon >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "error: vogon binary not found on PATH after build; the canary lane would skip every test and still report success." >&2
  exit 1
fi

PATH="$E2E_PATH" E2E_AGENT=vogon gotestsum --format dots \
  --jsonfile "$E2E_ARTIFACT_DIR/test-events-vogon.json" -- \
  -tags=e2e -count=1 -timeout=10m \
  ${filter:+-run "$filter"} \
  ./e2e/tests/... || vogon_rc=$?

go run ./e2e/cmd/testreport -color \
  -o "$E2E_ARTIFACT_DIR/report-vogon.txt" \
  "$E2E_ARTIFACT_DIR/test-events-vogon.json"

# Entire CLI — repository instructions

Go CLI built with Cobra and Charmbracelet Huh. `AGENTS.md` is a symlink to this
file. Keep this entry point short: repo-wide rules and pointers, not command
catalogs, implementation histories, or subsystem specifications.

## Project map

- `cmd/entire/`: entry point and external-command dispatch.
- `cmd/entire/cli/`: Cobra commands, group roots, and CLI helpers. Group/verb files
  use `<noun>_group.go` and `<noun>_<verb>.go`.
- `cmd/entire/cli/agent/`: built-in agent integrations and external-agent protocol.
- `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/`: manual-commit strategy and lifecycle/git hooks.
- `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/`: persistent checkpoint storage (written at commit).
- `cmd/entire/cli/session/`: session state shared across worktrees.
- `cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/`: simulated-hook integration tests.
- `e2e/`: real-agent tests and deterministic Vogon canary.
- `internal/entireclient/`: API clients, authentication, and user directories.

Use the Go version pinned by `go.mod` and tools configured in `mise.toml`.
For installed CLI usage, run `entire agent-help`, then
`entire agent-help <command>` for current flags; do not guess from a static list.

## Read when relevant

Read the applicable reference **before changing that area**, not every reference
at session start. Follow its related links when the task crosses those boundaries.

| Area being changed | Reference |
| --- | --- |
| Commands, help, experimental visibility, repo refs, prompts | [CLI conventions](docs/development/cli-conventions.md) |
| Test harnesses, isolation, TTY behavior, source guards | [Testing](docs/development/testing.md) |
| Filesystem I/O, `.entire`, symlinks, hook configs, root anchors | [Filesystem safety](docs/development/filesystem-safety.md) |
| Git operations, executable lookup, subprocesses, Windows launching | [Git and subprocess safety](docs/development/git-safety.md) |
| Caller identification or session current/tokens/adopt | [Caller-session resolution](docs/development/caller-session-resolution.md) |
| Control-plane auth or data-plane routing | [API routing](docs/development/api-routing.md) |
| Checkpoint writes, lifecycle, sync, settings trust, redaction | [Implementation contracts](docs/development/checkpoint-implementation.md), [domain model](docs/architecture/sessions-and-checkpoints.md), [scenarios](docs/architecture/checkpoint-scenarios.md) |
| Ref-based checkpoint backend | [Ref backend](docs/architecture/ref-checkpoint-backend.md) |
| Agent integrations | [Agent guide](docs/architecture/agent-guide.md), [integration checklist](docs/architecture/agent-integration-checklist.md) |
| External commands or agents | [External commands](docs/architecture/external-commands.md), [agent protocol](docs/architecture/external-agent-protocol.md) |
| Security, privacy, scanners | [Security and privacy](docs/security-and-privacy.md), [implementation contracts](docs/development/checkpoint-implementation.md) |
| Review command | [Review architecture](docs/architecture/review-command.md) |
| Release artifacts, install scripts, version-check origins | [Release origins](docs/architecture/release-origins.md) |
| E2E tests | [E2E guide](e2e/README.md) |
| Complexity/coverage measurement and the CI complexity gate | [Complexity tooling](tools/complexity/README.md) |

## Verification

| Task | Command / requirement |
| --- | --- |
| Unit tests | `mise run test` |
| Integration tests | `mise run test:integration`; required when changing integration test code |
| Deterministic E2E canary | `mise run test:e2e:canary`; safe without API calls |
| All CI tests | `mise run test:ci` (unit + integration + canary) |
| Format and lint | `mise run fmt && mise run lint` |
| Before every commit | **`mise run check`** (format, lint, all CI tests) |
| Before any push or remote code update | **`mise run lint` on the current tree**, after the latest formatting pass |
| After every push to an open PR | **check the trail's findings** (`entire trail finding list cli/<n> --freshness any`; `<n>` is the PR branch's cli trail number, not the PR number); fix real ones, resolve with `-m`, and re-check after the fix lands. Not done until findings are clear |
| Duplication checks | `mise run dup` or `mise run dup:staged`; normal lint also checks duplication |
| Complexity gate | `mise run complexity:gate`; CI fails a PR on functions over cognitive complexity 30 that are new or worsened against the merge base. The threshold is a gate flag (`COGNIT_WARN`), not a `.golangci.yaml` setting |
| Windows installer | `mise run test:ps1`; see testing reference for prerequisites |

**Do not run real-agent E2E tests unless the user explicitly requests them.** They
make paid API calls. Vogon is the exception: its canary is deterministic and free.
When changing E2E prompt wording, run the canary and update Vogon's regex parsing
if needed. Formatting can rewrite files; an earlier lint pass is not sufficient.

Before implementing Go code, search nearby packages and helpers for reusable
patterns. Use `/go:discover-related` when available, otherwise `rg` and related
implementations/tests. Check `.golangci.yaml`; handle errors and avoid duplication.

## Test safety

- Every top-level test and subtest calls `t.Parallel()` unless it changes
  process-global state (`t.Chdir`, `t.Setenv`, or their `os` equivalents).
- Git tests use isolated temporary repositories, preferably
  `testutil.InitRepo(t, dir)` plus its file/add/commit helpers. Redirect CWD before
  calling CWD-based handlers. Never mutate the real checkout's git/session state.
- Tests must not access the developer's real config, cache, or keychain.
  In-process fallbacks are shared per process; use per-test overrides and
  `tokenstore.UseFileBackendForTesting` when isolation between tests is needed.
  Tests that can reach the OS keyring need `keyring.MockInit()` in `TestMain`.
- Spawned binaries do not inherit Go's test detection. Harnesses must isolate
  `ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, `ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE=file`,
  `ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE_PATH`, and `ENTIRE_TEST_AUTH_STORE_FILE`.
- Prefer `execx.NonInteractive` for real CLI/git test subprocesses so a developer's
  terminal cannot make them prompt or hang.
- Caller-resolution tests clear every variable from `agent.CallerSessionEnvVars()`;
  never hand-maintain a partial list or inherit the developer's agent identity.
- Source-scanning guards discover files through testutil's guard helpers
  (`GitGrepGuard`, `GuardGoFiles`), restrict pathspecs to Go files, and fail on
  zero matches. Do not weaken guard ledgers to silence failures.

## Filesystem and settings safety

**Use the existing anchor for each tree; never assemble a path and perform bare
I/O beneath it.** Read the filesystem reference before adding or changing I/O.

| Tree | Canonical owner |
| --- | --- |
| `.entire` | `entiredir` |
| Git common directory | `gitdir` |
| Working tree | `worktreedir` |
| Agent hook configuration | `agent.HookConfigFile` |
| Agent session store | `agent.SessionStore` |
| Active git hooks directory | `strategy.hooksRootForInstall` / `ForRemoval` |
| Per-user config/cache | `userdirs.ConfigRoot` / `CacheRoot` |
| Managed plugins | `pluginRoot` |

- Root bases come from trusted resolvers, **not `filepath.Dir(target)`**. Confining
  a file to its own derived parent proves nothing. Prefer an existing anchor.
- Roots share the `osroot.Shared` registry. Open child roots with
  `osroot.SharedChild` / `OpenChild`, not bare `parent.OpenRoot`.
- Use `osroot` operations and `jsonutil.WriteFileAtomicIn` / `CreateTempIn`.
  Directories use `MkdirAllNoSymlink`; rooted read-only operations must also
  enforce symlink policy. Atomic writes replace leaf links rather than follow them.
- `.entire` must be a real directory; validate through
  `paths.ValidateEntireDirAt` / `RequireEntireDir`. Do not treat an unresolved
  repository as absent. Settings reads must also refuse symlinks themselves.
- Do not broaden symlink exceptions. Developer-vouched agent config directories
  are scoped, locally trusted exceptions; `.entire` and git hooks are not vouchable.
- `entiredir.OpenForRead` must not create directories. Reset cached roots before
  deleting/recreating their directories. Use `entiredir.Name` / `MustName` to
  bridge repo-relative constants and root-relative I/O names.
- All settings access goes through `settings`; never read or parse settings JSON
  ad hoc. Per-user config/cache resolution belongs only to `userdirs`.
- Repository-controlled settings must not authorize executable discovery, custom
  executables, or instructions for permission-bypassed agents. Preserve the
  existing local-provenance gates and their rejection reporting.
- Existing exceptions (explicit user paths, global git config, transcript-read
  protocol gaps) are documented in the references; do not generalize them.

## Git and subprocess safety

- Open repositories only through `gitrepo.OpenCurrent(ctx)` or
  `gitrepo.OpenPath(root)`, never direct go-git opens. This preserves alternates
  and reftable support. Do not fall back to CWD after failed repo resolution.
- Use `gitrepo.Status`, never `worktree.Status()`. Agent-hook capture paths use
  `StatusWithBudget` and preserve degraded-capture reporting on budget exhaustion.
- Every `git status` subprocess passes **`--no-optional-locks`**. This does not
  protect worktree-comparing `git diff` from refreshing the index; use the
  hook-safe alternatives in the git reference.
- Use the git CLI, not go-git v5, for checkout and hard reset; go-git can delete
  ignored/untracked directories. This is an implementation rule, not permission
  to run destructive git commands.
- Git-relative paths resolve against `paths.WorktreeRoot`, never process CWD.
- A git subprocess targeting a repository independently of the current hook must
  use `gitrepo.EnvWithoutRepoOverrides()`; `Dir` or `-C` alone does not override
  inherited selectors. Queries inspecting the commit Git is preparing must retain
  the hook environment, including its temporary `GIT_INDEX_FILE`. Hook queries
  reading only the hook's own refs or reflog may strip selectors and resolve from
  `paths.WorktreeRoot`. User-invoked CWD commands also honor intentionally
  exported repo selectors.
- PATH scanners use `execx.PathScanDirs()`; external-agent execution requires
  absolute binary paths. User-directory overrides use the checked `userdirs`
  resolvers before any I/O.
- When Entire owns execution, pass arguments separately; never interpolate
  dynamic values into `cmd.exe`. Agent-owned shell execution uses the shared
  escaping helper. See the reference for the literal-only Unix updater exception.

## CLI behavior and output

- Load settings through the `settings` package, not new helpers in CLI consumers.
- Operational/debug messages use `logging.Debug/Info/Warn/Error`; user output uses
  `cmd.OutOrStdout()` / `cmd.ErrOrStderr()`. Never log prompts, file contents, or
  commit messages; log operational metadata only.
- Cobra suppresses errors globally; `main.go` prints returned errors. Return
  `NewSilentError(err)` only after printing a custom error yourself.
- Every read-only workflow must work without a TUI: provide complete text/JSON,
  stable IDs and detail commands, or direct selection flags. Test that path.
- Use `uiform.New` (or `NewAccessibleForm` in `cli`) for Huh forms; these wire
  accessibility and theming centrally. Do not hand-roll `WithAccessible`.
- Separately opened prompt terminals use `interactive.OpenPromptTTY()` and
  `PromptTTY.Close()`, not a bare file close (Windows pending reads can hang).
- Register experimental commands with `experimental.Register`. Classify new
  commands in `agentHelpClassification`; default to unlisted/user-owned and
  flag the product choice for review. Agent guidance belongs in `agentHelpGuidance`,
  not Cobra `Short`/`Long` or first-turn injection.

## Session, checkpoint, and API contracts

- `*strategy.ManualCommitStrategy` is the only strategy; there is no interface or
  worktree restore path. Turn ends write session state only; checkpoints are
  metadata refs written at commit, never working-branch commits. Log resume is distinct from restoring worktree files.
- Caller identity comes from `strategy.ResolveCallerSession`, not newest state.
  Preserve resolution provenance; do not narrate worktree fallback or ambiguous
  matches as identified callers. `IsCaller()` excludes those guesses; consult
  the caller-resolution reference for current enforcement gaps.
- Preserve sanitize → image drop or externalization → redact ordering where all apply,
  fail-closed scanner behavior, and checkpoint-scoped token accounting. Read the
  implementation contracts before modifying any transcript/storage pipeline.
- Control-plane precedence belongs to `coreapi`; display `client.CoreOrigin()`
  rather than independently resolving a possibly different target.

**Use the existing anchor for each tree; never assemble a path and perform bare

| Tree | Canonical owner |
| --- | --- |
| `.entire` | `entiredir` |
| Git common directory | `gitdir` |
| Working tree | `worktreedir` |
| Agent hook configuration | `agent.HookConfigFile` |
| Agent session store | `agent.SessionStore` |
| Active git hooks directory | `strategy.hooksRootForInstall` / `ForRemoval` |
| Per-user config/cache | `userdirs.ConfigRoot` / `CacheRoot` |
| Managed plugins | `pluginRoot` |

  a file to its own derived parent proves nothing. Prefer an existing anchor.

structuredContent.body:
## The bug

`openCodeMsgToken` declared only `input` and `output`:

```go
type openCodeMsgToken struct {
    Input  int `json:"input"`
    Output int `json:"output"`
}
```

OpenCode exports also carry `reasoning`, `cache.read`, `cache.write`, `total` and a per-message `modelID`. `openCodeRecord` therefore wrote a `CallUsage` with only two fields, and the stored transcript line dropped the rest. Readers of a checkpoint transcript saw:

```json
{"input_tokens":150,"output_tokens":90,"content":[...]}
```

instead of cache read 100, cache write 160 and the model the export reported. Every other adapter keeps what its agent records.

Reasoning has the same problem in a second form: 1.3.16+ stores it apart from output, while older or provider-specific messages already include it. The condensed line's `reasoning_tokens` is a subset of `output_tokens`, so it has to be counted exactly once.

## Reproduction

On `main`, `TestCompact_OpenCodeUsageKeepsCacheReasoningAndModel` produces `cache_read_tokens: 0, cache_write_tokens: 0, reasoning_tokens: 0` and no `model`, although the input export carries `cache:{read:5,write:2}`, `reasoning:40` and `modelID`.

The existing `TestCompact_OpenCodeTokenUsage` input also has cache read 100 / write 160; its expected line omitted both, pinning the loss.

## The fix

- Parse `reasoning`, `cache`, `total` and `modelID` from the export.
- Populate `CallUsage` with cache read/write, reasoning and model.
- Compute output with the same identity the OpenCode agent already uses in `Tokens.OutputWithReasoning`: if `total == input + output + cache.read + cache.write`, reasoning is already inside output; otherwise add it. `reasoning_tokens` then stays a subset of `output_tokens`.

The existing golden fixture is regenerated: every assistant line gains its model and cache counts, and no message in it has reasoning stored apart, so its output counts are unchanged.

## Tests

- New `TestCompact_OpenCodeUsageKeepsCacheReasoningAndModel` covers reasoning stored apart (80 + 40 → 120), reasoning already inside output (total identity → 90), cache counts and model.
- `TestCompact_OpenCodeTokenUsage` now asserts the cache fields it already supplied.
- `go test ./transcript/... ./internal/transcript/...` passes.
- `mise run lint:go`: 0 issues.

Independent of #2823: that PR fixes the agent's `CalculateTokenUsage` path used for checkpoint metadata; this one fixes the stored condensed transcript line itself.

structuredContent.body:
## The bug

`templateProcess.Wait` waited for stderr EOF before calling `cmd.Wait`:

```go
if p.stderrDone != nil {
    <-p.stderrDone
}
err := p.cmd.Wait()
```

stderr reaches EOF only when every writer closes it. A review agent that leaves a background helper running — a language server, an MCP process, a sandbox helper — hands that helper the same stderr pipe. The agent can exit, the findings can be parsed, and `entire review` still blocks forever on the final wait.

## Reproduction

```go
// BuildCmd
exec.CommandContext(ctx, "sh", "-c", "sleep 5 >/dev/null & exit 0")
```

`Start` succeeds, the agent exits 0 immediately, and `Wait` is still blocked 2s later. On a real run the helper can outlive the review by minutes or hours.

## The fix

`cmd.StderrPipe` is replaced with a pipe we own. `Wait` now reaps the agent first and only then drains stderr:

- normal agent: the capture goroutine has already reached EOF, so nothing changes;
- helper still holding stderr: after a 250ms grace period we close our read end, the capture goroutine finishes, and `Wait` returns with whatever stderr it copied (kept for `ProcessError` diagnostics).

This also keeps the `Process` contract: no goroutine outlives `Wait`.

## Tests

`TestReviewerTemplate_WaitDoesNotBlockOnInheritedStderr` starts the shell above and fails on `main` after 2s with:

```
Wait() blocked on stderr held by a grandchild after the agent exited
```

The existing `WaitIncludesStderrOnFailure` test still passes, so normal failure diagnostics are preserved.

## Verification

- `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/review/...` passes
- `mise run lint:go`: 0 issues

A review can finish parsing its output and still hang in `Wait`: a helper process can inherit stderr and keep it open after the reviewer exits. Previously `Wait` waited for stderr EOF before reaping the reviewer, so the subprocess timeout backstop could not help.

Own the stderr pipe, reap the reviewer, then allow up to 250 ms for remaining stderr before closing the reader and joining its capture goroutine. Preserve bounded diagnostics, exit-error classification and cancellation behavior. Close both owned pipe ends if startup fails, retain the existing preparation cleanup, and preserve the previous refusal to overwrite a configured stderr destination.

Regression coverage uses a helper held open by a test-controlled pipe, rather than a timed sleep, and drains real stdout before calling `Wait`. Additional tests cover failed-start descriptor cleanup, rejection of a preconfigured stderr destination, and stderr larger than the capture limit. The hang regression fails against current main; the cleanup regression fails against the original PR head.

Validation: focused review tests and repeated lifecycle tests pass with race detection. Full formatting/lint, the full CLI package under race detection (20-minute runner budget), and 54 Vogon + 4 Roger-Roger deterministic scenarios pass. The repository-wide check is not green: `TestManualCommit_MidSessionRebaseFollowsHead` and `TestCheckpointDelete_LeftoverDeletedIDNeverReceivesNewWork` reproduce on untouched main `76f1b5129`; this Mac also hit aggregate package timeouts under load. No unrelated test assertions or repository timeouts are changed.

Scope: bounds stderr draining after normal reviewer exit. It does not change stdout completion or implement Windows process-tree termination; #3102 addresses that separate cancellation path. POSIX inheritance/large-stderr tests run on macOS and skip on Windows; startup cleanup is portable. No real agent/model run was needed.
